Title: Board
Text:
An infinite canvas, as the one of Figma: its content (the default slot) lives in coordinates of its own (the world, in pixels at zoom 1: place the elements in it with position absolute, left and top) and the board shows a part of it, moved and scaled. The wheel moves it (a trackpad with two fingers too; over an element of the content that scrolls that way, a list, it scrolls that element), Ctrl with the wheel or a pinch zooms at the pointer, a drag with the middle button, with Space held or on an empty place (Drag) moves it; when it has the focus, the arrows move it, + and - zoom, 0 gives zoom 1 and Shift+1 fits the content. X and Y are the point of the world at the top left corner of the view, Zoom its scale (MinZoom to MaxZoom); Grid dots, lines or none, of GridSize pixels of the world. Controls shows the buttons of the zoom and its percent. The view event tells {X, Y, Zoom} as it changes. Bounds keeps the view to a part of the world: none (anywhere, by default), content (the content with BoundsMargin pixels of the world around) or frame (the element of the content with data-frame="Frame", the first one without a Frame, BoundsMargin around it); a part smaller than the view stays in its middle, and the view follows the part as it changes. Methods: ZoomTo(zoom, point), Pan(dx, dy), FitContent(margin) (the frame alone with Bounds frame), CenterOn(x, y), ToWorld(clientX, clientY), ToScreen(x, y), Limits() (the part of the world the view is kept to, {Left, Top, Right, Bottom}, or null). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | X | 0 | | Y | 0 | | Zoom | 1 | | MinZoom | 0.1 | | MaxZoom | 8 | | Grid | 'dots' | | GridSize | 24 | | Drag | true | | Controls | true | | Bounds | 'none' | | BoundsMargin | 40 | | Frame | '' | Events - view: The view moved or zoomed: {X, Y, Zoom}. Slots default Methods - Limits() - ToWorld(clientX, clientY) - ToScreen(x, y) - ZoomTo(zoom, point) - Pan(dx, dy) - CenterOn(x, y) - FitContent(margin) Example
Drag the empty place to move
Ctrl and the wheel zoom
Far away: Shift+1 fits all

Title: Breadcrumbs
Text:
The path to the present page: Items [{ID, Label, Icon, File, Href, Disabled, Class}], the last one the present page (aria-current="page", not pressed unless CurrentClickable). Icon names an Icon, File a FileIcon (by a file name). A press on an item emits select with {Item, Index}; an item with Href is a link (the Router follows it as any link of the page) and emits select too. Separator: chevron (the default), slash, arrow, dot, or a text of its own. Max (0: all) keeps the first item and the last Max - 1: the ones between are behind a "…" that lists them in a menu. The slots start and end stand before and after the path (a button, a status); Size small, medium or large. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Items | [] | | Separator | 'chevron' | | Max | 0 | | Size | 'medium' | | Label | '' | | CurrentClickable | false | Events - select: An item was pressed, or chosen in the menu of the hidden ones: {Item, Index}. Slots start, end Example

Title: BusinessCalculator
Text:
A calculator of a business made of its fields and its results: a price of a renovation, a loan, a return on an investment, a delivery. Its formulas are read by the Calculations Service (no eval), each result as the fields change. Fields: [{ID, Label, Type, Value, Min, Max, Step, Unit, Options, Hint}], ID the name the formulas read; Type number, money (in Currency), percent (typed as 15, read as 15), range (a Slider from Min to Max), select (Options [{Value, Label}], the values numbers) or toggle (1 when on, else 0). Results: [{ID, Label, Formula, Format, Precision, Unit, Primary, Hidden, Hint}], Formula of the fields and of the other results by their IDs, in any order (a result that needs itself, through others, is an error); Format number, money, percent (0.15 shows 15%) or integer; Primary is the main one, shown large first; Hidden is computed for the others alone. The same declared inside it: CalculatorField and CalculatorResult. Breakdown names results to show as the parts of a bar (the parts of a total). Currency (USD) and Locale (the language of the page) write the money. Values holds the values of the fields (given by the owner, or as they are typed). Events: change ({Values, Results}: the numbers of the results by their IDs) as the fields change. Methods: Numbers() the same numbers, Reset() the first values back. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Title | '' | | Fields | [] | | Results | [] | | Values | null | | Breakdown | [] | | Currency | 'USD' | | Locale | '' | Events - change: A field changed: {Values, Results} (the numbers of the results by their IDs). Slots actions, default Methods - Numbers() - Reset() Example

Title: Button
Text: A button. Variant: primary, secondary (default), ghost, danger or link; Size: small, medium, large or giant; Shape round makes it round. Icon and IconRight are icons before and after its Label; without a Label it is an icon only, named by its Title. Loading shows a spinner and disables it, Disabled disables it, Pressed (true or false) makes it a toggle button (aria-pressed), Expanded (true or false) tells it opens something (aria-expanded), AriaLabel is its name for a screen reader when its text does not say it (M for Mute the drums), Block stretches it to the full width. Type is the type of the native button (button, submit, reset). Badge puts a badge over its corner, as badge does: a count, 'dot', 'busy', a text or {Value, Tone, Max, Label}. Events: click. Title: Calculator
Text:
A calculator: the keys of a basic one, or of a scientific one (Mode scientific: sin, cos, tan, their inverses with Shift, ln, log, roots and powers, factorial, pi and e, brackets, degrees or radians), read by the Calculations Service (no eval). The line above shows what is typed, the one below its value as it is typed; = keeps it, and the history (History, the last ten) brings one back by a press. The keyboard types too: digits, + - / ^ % ( ), Enter or =, Backspace, Escape (clears), Delete. A number ends with % to be a hundredth of itself (50% is 0.5, and 200 + 10% is 220, as a calculator of a shop counts). Precision is the significant digits shown (12). Value is what is typed. Events: result ({Expression, Value}) at each =, change (Value) as it is typed. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Mode | 'basic' | | Value | '' | | History | true | | Precision | 12 | | Label | '' | | Shift | false | Events - change: What is typed changed: Value. - result: The value was kept by =: {Expression, Value}. Title: Calendar
Text:
A calendar of events. Events: [{ID, Title, Start, End, AllDay, Color, Repeat}], Start and End as 'YYYY-MM-DD' (a whole day; End is its last day) or 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm' (an End at 00:00 ends with the day before). View: day, week, month, months (Span months, 3 by default), quarter, year or years (Span years, 3 by default); Date is a day of the period shown (today by default). The header moves by a period, back to today, and switches the view between Views. Month: every day lists its events, MaxEvents of them, then a "+N more" that opens the week of that day; an event of several days is a bar across them, in the same row of every day it covers, cut at the end of a week with an arrow. Week and day: the hours from StartHour to EndHour (HourHeight pixels each), the events at their time (overlapping ones side by side; one that goes on past midnight is cut there and goes on in the next day), the whole-day events and the ones of a day or more above as bars, a line at the present time. Months, quarter, year and years: a planner, a Timeline of the events (it zooms and moves as a Timeline does). Repeat makes an event recurring: {Every: day, week, month or year, Interval, Days (the days of a week: 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday, or MO, TU...), Until (the last day), Count, Except (the days left out)} or an RRULE of RFC 5545 (FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=MO,WE;COUNT=10, UNTIL); its occurrences are made for the period shown, with the ID @, the Occurrence (the day) and the Source (the event). FirstDay: 0 Sunday, 1 Monday (the default), or 'locale' for the first day of the week of Locale. Editable lets the user move events: dragged to another day (in the month and in the whole-day row) they keep their times; dragged in the week they take the day and the time under them, in steps of Snap minutes; the lower edge of a timed event changes its end, and the end of a bar its last day; in the planner they move and stretch by days. A shadow shows where the event goes; Escape cancels. With the focus on an event, Alt with the arrows moves it: a day left or right, Snap minutes up or down. The calendar does not change Events itself: the move event ({Event, Start, End}, and the Occurrence of a recurring event: the owner moves the series or that day alone) asks the owner to. Events: select (the event), day (the date pressed), slot ({Date, Time}: an empty hour pressed in the week), change ({Date, View}), move ({Event, Start, End, Occurrence}). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Events | [] | | View | 'month' | | Views | ['day', 'week', 'month', 'quarter', 'year'] | | Span | 0 | | Date | '' | | Locale | '' | | FirstDay | null | | MaxEvents | 3 | | StartHour | 7 | | EndHour | 21 | | HourHeight | 48 | | TodayLabel | '' | | MonthLabel | '' | | WeekLabel | '' | | MoreLabel | '' | | Editable | false | | Snap | 15 | Events - change: The period shown changed: {Date, View}. - select: An event was pressed: the event. - move: An event was dragged or resized: {Event, Start, End}, and Occurrence for one of a repeated event. - day: A day was pressed: its date ('YYYY-MM-DD'). - slot: A time of a day was pressed in the week or the day view: {Date, Time ('HH:MM')}. Title: Card
Text:
A card: media at the edge (Image, or the media slot), a header, a body (Title, Text and the default slot) and a footer (the footer slot, then the actions slot at its end). Variant: outlined (default), elevated, flat or filled (in Color, the accent by default). Orientation: vertical or horizontal (the media beside the content; under it again on a narrow window). Ratio is the shape of the media ('16:9' by default, '1:1', '4:3'...). Href makes the whole card a link (Target), and the buttons inside it stay buttons. Loading shows skeleton lines in place of Title and Text. The cards of the Library (PostCard, ProfileCard, CommentCard, ProductCard, PlanCard) are built the same way. Title: Chart
Text:

Title: Chat
Text:

Title: ChatComposer
Text:
The message field of a Chat. Enter sends (the send event carries the text), Shift+Enter starts a new line. The field grows with its text up to MaxRows. Attach shows a button that emits the attach event. Emoji shows the button of an ExpressionPicker: an emoji goes into the text where the caret is, a sticker is sent at once (the sticker event carries {Sticker}); Stickers turns the tab of the stickers off. Suggestions above the field: Suggest 'always' (the default) offers emoji for the word at the caret (2 letters or more) and for :word, 'colon' only for :word, 'never' none; a pressed emoji takes the place of the word (for :word, Arrow Up and Down choose and Enter or Tab takes one). SuggestStickers (true) offers the stickers of a message of one emoji (the Emoji of the Stickers Service): a pressed sticker is sent in place of the message. Escape hides them. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Placeholder | '' | | MaxRows | 8 | | Attach | true | | Emoji | true | | Stickers | true | | Disabled | false | | Suggest | 'always' | | SuggestStickers | true | Events - input: The text changed: Value. - sticker: A sticker was sent: {Sticker}. - send: Enter (or the send button): the text. - attach: The attach button was pressed. Example

Title: ChatMessage
Text:
One message of a Chat. Text, or the default slot for rich content. Own puts the message on the reader's side. Avatar is an image URL; without it the initials of Author are shown. Position places the message in a run of messages from one author: single, first, middle or last. The author name shows on the first message of a run and the avatar on the last (the newest) one. Status: sending (a clock), sent (a check), delivered (two checks), read (two checks in the accent) or error. Edited marks a message changed after it was sent ("edited"; a text, as the time of the change, is its hint). Sticker is the URL of a sticker sent as the message. Reactions: [{Emoji, Count, Mine, Users: [{Name, Avatar}]}] under the bubble; a press on one emits react. React adds the button that picks an emoji to react with (EmojiPicker). Actions: the menu of the message ([{ID, Label, Icon, Shortcut, Disabled, Danger, Separator}], as MenuList), opened by a right click (a long press on a touch screen), the Menu key or Shift+F10, or the button with three dots; a choice emits action. The item of ID 'summary' opens the summary instead. On a phone the menu is a sheet from the bottom of the screen. The summary: who reacted with what (the Users of the Reactions) and who has seen the message (Viewers: [{Name, Avatar, Time}]; Views counts them when the list is not known), in tabs. The eye with the count of views in the corner of the bubble opens it too. The choice of several messages: on a touch screen a tap opens the menu of the message and a long press (Hold milliseconds) chooses the message; with a mouse Shift and a click choose it, and the menu item of ID 'select' chooses it from the keys. While the chat is Selecting, a tap, a click or the check at the start of the message turns its choice; Selected marks a chosen message. The Chat around keeps the choice (its Selection) and the bar of its actions. Events: react ({ID, Emoji, Mine}): Mine tells whether the reader reacts (true) or takes the reaction back (false); action ({ID, Action, Item}); select ({ID, Selected}): the message asks to be chosen or let go. ID is the ID of the message. Title: Clock
Text:

Title: Combobox
Text: A field that suggests: typing filters Options ([{Value, Label, Hint, Icon, Group, Disabled}]) in a list under it, the labels that start with the text first; arrows and Enter pick, Escape closes and then restores the text. Value is the Value of the picked option. AllowCustom also takes a text that is no option: a "Create" row offers it, and Value becomes the text (create emits it). The search event carries every text typed, so the owner may load Options from a server (Loading shows a spinner; Filter: false keeps the Options as they come). Clearable adds a cross. A text left without a pick goes back to the label of Value (or is taken, with AllowCustom). Events: change (Value), search (the text), create (the text). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Options | [] | | Value | null | | Placeholder | '' | | Empty | '' | | CreateLabel | '' | | AllowCustom | false | | Filter | true | | Loading | false | | Clearable | false | | Icon | '' | | Size | 'medium' | | Shape | 'default' | | Name | null | | Disabled | false | | Invalid | false | Events - search: The text changed: the text, to load Options from a server. - create: A text that is no option was taken (AllowCustom): the text. - change: An option was picked: Value. Example <Field Label="A fruit" [hint]="Note"><Combobox Placeholder="Type to search" [options]="Fruits" [value]="Fruit" AllowCustom="true" (change)="Changed" (create)="Created" /></Field> <script> ({ Fruit: 'pear', Note: 'Type a name that is not in the list to add it.', Fruits: [{Value: 'apple', Label: 'Apple'}, {Value: 'pear', Label: 'Pear'}, {Value: 'plum', Label: 'Plum'}, {Value: 'peach', Label: 'Peach'}], Changed: function (value) { this.Fruit = value; this.Note = 'Chosen: ' + value; }, Created: function (text) { this.Fruits = this.Fruits.concat([{Value: text.toLowerCase(), Label: text}]); this.Fruit = text.toLowerCase(); this.Note = 'Added: ' + text; } }) </script> Tests - Combobox filters its options as the text is typed, tells every text, picks with the keys, and creates a text of its own — tests/regression/library-pickers.test.js

Title: CommandPalette
Text: A command palette: a search over the actions of the application, opened by Hotkey ('Mod+K' by default; '' for none) or by Open. Commands: [{ID, Label, Icon, Group, Keys, Hint, Keywords, Disabled, Run}]: Keys shows the shortcut of the command, Keywords are more words to find it by, Run(command) is called when it is chosen. IncludeHotkeys adds every shortcut of the Hotkeys Service that has a Description. The search is fuzzy: the letters of the query in their order, best at the starts of words; the matched letters are marked. With no query the recently used commands come first (Remember: a localStorage key that keeps them between visits). Keys: arrows, Page Up and Down, Home and End move; Enter runs; Escape closes. Events: run (the command), close. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Commands | [] | | Open | false | | Hotkey | 'Mod+K' | | IncludeHotkeys | false | | Placeholder | '' | | Empty | '' | | Remember | '' | | Limit | 50 | Events - close: It closed (Escape, the hotkey again, a press outside, or a command run). - run: A command was chosen: the command (its Run is called too). Methods - Run(index) Example

Title: CommentCard
Text:
A comment, a post of a social network or a tweet: the Author (Avatar, Verified, Handle), the Time it was written (shown from now: '5 minutes ago'), Text, up to four images of Media, and the counts of Replies, Reposts and Likes (null hides one) with Reposted and Liked. In the text, @mentions and #tags are buttons and links are links; nothing of the text is read as markup. Thread draws the line to the next comment of a thread; the default slot holds the replies. Variant: flat (default: a comment of a list), outlined or elevated (a card). Events: reply, repost ({Reposted, Reposts}), like ({Liked, Likes}), share, mention ({Handle}), tag ({Tag}). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Author | '' | | Handle | '' | | Avatar | '' | | Verified | false | | Time | '' | | Text | '' | | Media | [] | | Replies | null | | Reposts | null | | Likes | null | | Reposted | false | | Liked | false | | Thread | false | | Variant | 'flat' | | ReplyLabel | '' | | RepostLabel | '' | | LikeLabel | '' | | ShareLabel | '' | | VerifiedLabel | '' | Events - reply: The reply button: {Author, Handle}. - repost: The repost button: {Reposted, Reposts}. - like: The like button: {Liked, Likes}. - share: The share button: {Author, Text}. - mention: A @mention of the text was pressed: {Handle}. - tag: A #tag of the text was pressed: {Tag}. Slots default Example

Title: CommitGraph
Text:
The history of a repository as git draws it: Commits, newest first as git log gives them ([{ID, Parents: [ID], Message, Author, Date, Refs: [{Name, Kind: branch, remote, tag or head}]}]), each in a lane of its own color; a merge joins its lanes, a branch leaves one. Lanes are laid out once for the whole list, as git log --graph does. - Layout list (the default): a row for each commit, its graph on the left, then its refs, message, author, date and short ID (Columns: the ones shown, of message, author, date and id). Height is the height of the list in pixels: it shows the rows in view only, so a history of thousands scrolls; 'auto' shows them all. - Layout scheme: the history across, oldest on the left, a lane for each branch, its name at its start (the refs of its tip), the commits as dots with their refs over them (ShowMessages writes the messages under them), as the schemes of git-flow draw it. Selected is the ID of the commit chosen: a press, the arrows, Home and End choose; Enter or a double press opens it. Events: select (the commit), open (the commit). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Commits | [] | | Layout | 'list' | | Selected | null | | Columns | ['message', 'author', 'date', 'id'] | | Height | 360 | | ShowMessages | false | | Label | '' | Events - open: A commit was opened (Enter, a double press): the commit. - select: A commit was chosen: the commit. Example

{{Said}}

Tests - CommitGraph lays its lanes out as git log --graph: a branch leaves a lane, a merge joins it, a lane goes on from row to row — tests/regression/library-graphs.test.js - CommitGraph chooses with a press and its keys, opens with Enter and a double press, and shows only the rows in view of a long history — tests/regression/library-graphs.test.js - CommitGraph as a list is as wide as its place, also in a column that does not stretch its items — tests/regression/library-graphs.test.js - CommitGraph as a scheme scrolls inside its place: it does not widen a column of a grid (a phone) — tests/regression/library-graphs.test.js - CommitGraph as a scheme: oldest on the left, a lane for each branch named by its tip, its refs over the dots — tests/regression/library-graphs.test.js

Title: Consent
Text:
A request for consent, of any kind: cookies and analytics, the terms of a service, mail of news. Key names the consent and Version its text (a new version asks again); Purposes are what it asks for, [{ID, Label, Description, Required}] (a required one is always on). It shows itself while the Consents Service keeps no decision of that version (Open true or false decides instead): Accept all, Reject (only the required ones) and Customize (a switch for each purpose, then Save) keep the decision there and emit change with it. Show() opens it again with the choices kept (a link "Cookie settings"). Placement: bottom (a banner over the bottom of the page), center (a card in the middle) or inline (in its place). Its text is Text, or the content of its tag; Policy links to the full text. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Key | 'default' | | Version | '' | | Purposes | [] | | Title | '' | | Text | '' | | Policy | '' | | PolicyLabel | '' | | Placement | 'bottom' | | Reject | true | | Customize | true | | Open | null | Events - change: A decision was made: {Version, Choices: {purpose: true or false}, Time}. - close: It was hidden after a decision. Slots default Methods - Show() Example

Title: ContextMenu
Text:
A context menu over its content: a right click, the Menu key or Shift+F10 inside the default slot opens a multi-level MenuList at the pointer (or under the focused element). Items: as in MenuList. Before it opens, the open event carries {Target (the element pressed), X, Y}: the owner may change Items for that target then. The select event carries {Item, Target}. MenuItems in its slot items declare items after Items (a declared one emits select on its MenuItem too). Disabled leaves the browser menu alone. Sheet: true, or 'auto' (on a narrow or a touch screen), shows the menu as a sheet from the bottom of the screen with its Title, as on a phone. On a touch screen a press held for Hold milliseconds in place opens it (iOS sends no contextmenu event for a long press). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Items | [] | | Disabled | false | | Sheet | false | | Title | '' | | Open | false | | X | 0 | | Y | 0 | | Target | null | | Hold | 500 | Events - open: It is about to open: {Target, X, Y}; the owner may change Items for that target. - select: A leaf item was chosen: {Item, Target}. Slots default, items Example

Title: Countdown
Text: The time left: to a moment (To: a date, a text of a date or a timestamp) or of a length (Duration, in seconds, that Running counts down and a pause keeps). It shows days, hours, minutes and seconds (Units: auto drops the days and the hours while they are 0; dhms, hms or ms keep them), each with its label under it, or one line with Compact. It emits end once at 0. Methods: Start(), Pause(), Reset(). It counts by the clock of the page, so a tab in the background and a sleep (Cache) show the right time when they come back. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | To | '' | | Duration | 0 | | Running | true | | Units | 'auto' | | Compact | false | | Size | 'medium' | | Label | '' | Events - end: The time ran out. Methods - Reset() - Start() - Pause() Example

Title: CurrencySelect
Text: A searchable select of currencies: every ISO 4217 currency of the Currencies Service, or only the Codes given (['EUR', 'USD']), each with its code, its symbol and its name in the language of the page (Locale changes it). Value is the code ('USD' by default). Placeholder, Size, Shape, Name, Disabled and Invalid as in Select. Events: change (the code). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Value | 'USD' | | Codes | null | | Locale | '' | | Placeholder | '' | | Size | 'medium' | | Shape | 'default' | | Name | null | | Disabled | false | | Invalid | false | Events - change: Another currency was chosen: its code. Example <Field Label="Currency" [hint]="Value"><CurrencySelect Value="EUR" (change)="Changed" /></Field> <script> ({ Value: 'EUR', Changed: function (value) { this.Value = value; } }) </script> Tests - CurrencySelect lists only the Codes given, with their symbols, and shows the one chosen — tests/regression/library-misc.test.js

Title: Dashboard
Text:
A dashboard layout built on elemenx-screen, elemenx-container and elemenx-column. Slots: nav (the sidebar, often a NavList), header, default (the content: a responsive grid of DashboardWidget elements; any element with the class elemenx-dashboard-wide takes a full row), footer. An area shows only while its slot renders something; the sidebar narrows by itself around a collapsed NavList. Slots nav, header, default, footer Example

Title: DashboardWidget
Text: A widget of a Dashboard grid. Span (1 to 4 columns) and Rows (1 to 3) set its size; on a narrow dashboard every widget takes a full row. Slots: default (the body), actions (at the right of the title), footer. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Title | '' | | Icon | '' | | Note | '' | | Span | 1 | | Rows | 1 | Slots actions, default, footer Example

Title: DateInput
Text: A date field with its own calendar. Value is an ISO date ('2024-11-22'), or a month ('2024-11') in Mode 'month'; '' when empty. Format uses DD, MM and YYYY ('DD.MM.YYYY'); by default it follows Locale (the browser language). The text accepts only the digits of Format; Min and Max (ISO) limit both the text and the calendar. FirstDay: the first day of the week of the calendar, 0 Sunday or 1 Monday (the default); 'locale' for the one of Locale. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Value | '' | | Mode | 'date' | | Format | '' | | Locale | '' | | FirstDay | null | | Min | '' | | Max | '' | | Placeholder | '' | | TodayLabel | '' | | ClearLabel | '' | | Size | 'medium' | | Shape | 'default' | | Name | null | | Disabled | false | | ReadOnly | false | | Invalid | false | Events - input: The date changed while typing or in the calendar: Value (ISO, or ''). - change: The date was committed: Value. Example <Field Label="A date" [hint]="Date || 'Type it or pick it'"><DateInput [value]="Date" (change)="Changed" /></Field> <Field Label="A month"><DateInput Mode="month" /></Field> <Field Label="Only the next 30 days"><DateInput [min]="Today" [max]="Later" /></Field> <script> ({ Date: '', Today: new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10), Later: new Date(Date.now() + 30 86400000).toISOString().slice(0, 10), Changed: function (value) { this.Date = value; } }) </script> Tests - DateInput takes the digits of its Format, gives an ISO date, and refuses a date out of Min and Max — tests/regression/library-forms.test.js - DateInput puts the focus on the day of its calendar as it opens, so the next key moves it — tests/regression/library-forms.test.js

Title: DateRangeInput
Text: A range of dates. Value: [start, end] as 'YYYY-MM-DD' (or [] for none). The field shows the range in Locale; its button opens two months side by side: the first press picks the start, the second the end (the range shows while the pointer moves), in either order. Presets on the left pick a whole range at once: [{Label, Value: [start, end]} or {Label, Last: days (today included)} or {Label, Period: 'week', 'month', 'previous-month', 'year'}]. Min and Max bound the days; FirstDay is the first day of the week (0 Sunday, 1 Monday, the default; 'locale' for the one of Locale). Keys in the months: arrows move a day or a week, Page Up and Down a month, Enter or Space pick, Escape closes. Events: change ([start, end]). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Value | [] | | Min | '' | | Max | '' | | Locale | '' | | FirstDay | null | | Placeholder | '' | | Presets | […] | | ClearLabel | '' | | Size | 'medium' | | Shape | 'default' | | Name | null | | Disabled | false | | Invalid | false | Events - change: A range was picked: [start, end]; [] when it was cleared. Example <Field Label="A stay" [hint]="Note"><DateRangeInput (change)="Changed" /></Field> <script> ({ Note: 'Pick the first day, then the last.', Changed: function (value) { this.Note = value.length ? value.join(' → ') : 'Cleared'; } }) </script> Tests - DateRangeInput: the day of the cursor — tests/regression/focus-on-open.test.js - DateRangeInput picks a range by two presses in either order, and a preset picks a whole one — tests/regression/library-misc.test.js

Title: DesignerCanvas
Text: The canvas of a designer of pages (the Designer Service): the page of the document running as a component of its own (made again on every change), at the width of a desktop, a tablet or a phone (Width). A layer over it takes the pointer, so the components of the page stay still while they are built: it marks the element under the pointer and the selected one, selects what is pressed, and takes the kinds of a DesignerPalette dropped on it and the elements moved by the grip of the selection, with a line where they go and words that say it (In Screen, after Row). Near the edge of a container a drop goes beside it, in its parent; Shift held takes it one level up. Shift held without a drag measures, as the designers of pictures do: from the selected element to the one under the pointer (to the sides of the one around it, when that is under the pointer), or to the edges of the canvas when the pointer is on it or on nothing (the element under the pointer to them, with nothing selected). A press on a tab of a component of declared children (Tabs, Ribbon) selects the child it shows, and the canvas shows the child the selection is in. While a drag goes on, a bar over the canvas names the container the drop goes into and those around it: a drop on one of them puts the element at its end, whatever the edges. The canvas is the body of the page: as high as the room it has (a screen with Sizing fill fills it), as wide as Width says. It is the frame of a Board (Bounds frame): the wheel moves the view of a page taller or wider than the room, Ctrl with the wheel zooms it (Controls: the buttons of the zoom), and every mark, distance and ruler is in pixels of the page at any zoom. Outlines draws the frame of every container, Gaps gives the containers without a padding of their own some room to drop into (8 pixels); neither is in the page. Preview takes the layer away, the outlines and the places to drop with it: the page works as it will. Inspect (in a preview) shows the box of the element under the pointer as the tools of a browser do: its margin, its padding, its size; a press keeps one, and Shift held measures the distance from it to the one under the pointer (to the edges of the canvas without one). Lines draws the outlines in a preview too. Rulers (Ruler) run along the top and the side of the canvas, the pointer and the selected element marked on them. Empty is the text of an empty container (the phrase of the language of the page by default). Events: select (the ID of an element, or null), drop ({Kind or Node, Parent, Index, ID}). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Width | 'desktop' | | Preview | false | | Outlines | true | | Gaps | true | | Inspect | false | | Lines | false | | Rulers | true | | Controls | true | | Empty | '' | | Note | '' | | Size | {Width: 0, Height: 0} | Events - select: An element was pressed: its ID, or null for the page. - drop: A kind or an element was dropped on the canvas: {Kind, Node, Parent, Index, ID}, ID the element made or moved. Example

Title: DesignerDocument
Text: The document a designer of pages edits (the Designer Service), what the inspector shows with no element selected: a page has its Name and its Title, and in an application lists its routes (set in the settings of the Application); a component its Name, its Description, its public props (a row each: name, type, default value, the options of a choice, description; added, removed) and its slots, those its Slot elements make. Those props and slots are what the inspector offers where the component is used. A name or a route that cannot be (taken, or not the name of a Component) is said under its field. Remove takes the document away, unless it is the last one or another one holds it (then it names them). Example

Title: DesignerInspector
Text: The selected element of a designer of pages (the Designer Service), in blocks of their own: on top its layout, what every element has (DesignerStyle: its box, its sizes, its flex), its rules of CSS by their context (DesignerRules; Style false leaves both out), then its props, what its kind has: a field for each prop (a text, a number, a switch, a choice, the modifiers of its class, an expression of JavaScript), with the description its Component declares in $Meta as the hint; its slot in its parent and its text when its kind has one. A list prop whose $Meta gives the Schema of its items is a list of them, each a row of fields, that adds, moves and removes items ({ } edits it as an expression again). A component of declared children (Tabs and Tab) has a button to add each kind of them. The actions on the element: up and down among its siblings, its parent, a copy, removal. Every change goes to the Designer at once. A prop its Component declares Body (the Value of a Markdown) is a field of many lines. With no element selected, a component or an application shows the document being edited (DesignerDocument). Events: select (the element selected after an action, or null). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Style | true | Events - select: Another element was selected from it (its parent): its ID, or null. Example

Title: DesignerMap
Text:
The map of the pages of an application of the Designer Service: each page a frame on a Board (Bounds content), as it runs (its template as the canvas shows it in a preview; the pointer does not reach it), in the order of the routes, at the width of a desktop, a tablet or a phone (Width). Over the board each frame is named with its paths, and an arrow goes from every element whose Href a route of another page matches (a link, a button) to that page: the ways through the application. A press on a frame or on its name opens the page (open, its ID). Controls shows the buttons of the zoom. The map follows the project as it changes; it starts with all of it in view. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Width | 'desktop' | | Controls | true | Events - open: A frame or its name was pressed: the ID of its page. Example

{{Text}}

Title: DesignerPalette
Text: The palette of a designer of pages (the Designer Service): the kinds it can place, by group, with a search. A kind pressed goes into the selected element when that is a container, after it otherwise, and at the end of the page without a selection, and is selected; a kind dragged (draggable, type elemenx-designer-kind) goes where a DesignerCanvas takes it. Its tip (tip) is its name in bold and the description its Component declares in $Meta. Events: add (the new ID). Events - add: A kind was placed on the page: the ID of the new element. Example

Title: DesignerProject
Text: The project of a designer of pages (the Designer Service), as the explorer of an editor of code: the settings of the Application on top, then its pages (with their routes) and its components, each pressed to edit it, and a button to add a page or a component. Settings marks the settings as the open item, in place of the document being edited. Events: open ({ID}, a document opened), settings (the settings pressed). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Settings | false | Events - open: A page or a component was opened: {ID}. - settings: The settings of the Application were pressed. Example

Title: DesignerRules
Text: The rules of CSS of the selected element of a designer of pages (the Designer Service), by their context: who (this element, every element of its kind, or those inside an element of the kind around it), when (always, :hover, :focus-visible, :active, :disabled), where (every width, a tablet, a phone) and in which scheme (both, light, dark). The properties of the rule of the context are rows of a name and a value (a token of the theme, var(--elemenx-accent), is offered as one, with the value it takes on the canvas: in the scheme of the context, or in the light and the dark one; a value that holds a token shows what it comes to under it); a property added makes the rule, the last one taken away removes it. The rules that reach the element in other contexts are listed under them, a press goes to one. The rules go into the template as a

Title: DesignerSettings
Text: The settings of the Application a designer of pages makes (the Designer Service), as the properties of a project in an editor of code. General: its Name (of its files), its Title (of the window), its Language, its Theme (as the system, light or dark), how its Router keeps the route (the address, after # or in the history only), its Icon and its Description. Structure: the component of the Application (a component of the project around the pages, with the place of the page; said when it has none) and the page of a path no route has. Routes: a row each, its path (/product/:id), its page, its guards (asked in their order), the page shown when one refuses; added and removed. Guards: their names, descriptions and code (the body of the function of each), added and removed. Every change goes to the Designer at once; a name or a path that cannot be is said under its field. Example

Title: DesignerStyle
Text: The layout of the selected element of a designer of pages (the Designer Service), what every element has whatever its kind: its margin and its padding on a box of the box model, a field for each side (12 gives 12px; the four sides become one shorthand: 8px, 8px 16px...), its width and height with their least and greatest, and in a flex container the direction, the wrap, the alignment of the items across (align-items) and along (justify-content) as buttons with icons, and the gap. A choice pressed again is taken away. Every change goes to the Designer at once (SetStyle). Example

Title: DesignerTree
Text: The structure of the page of a designer of pages (the Designer Service): every element in a Tree, with the text it shows when it has some, the selected one marked. An element pressed is selected; an element dragged moves before or after another, or into it when that is a container (the Tree is Movable); a kind of a palette or of a gallery dragged there (draggable, type elemenx-designer-kind) makes a new element the same way. Events: select (the ID, or null), move ({ID, Target, Position, Type}). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Label | '' | Events - select: An element was pressed: its ID, or null. - move: An element or a kind was dragged in the tree: {ID, Target, Position, Type}. Example

Title: Diagram
Text: A diagram written as text (the Diagrams Service, a subset of the language of Mermaid): a flowchart, a sequence, the states, the entities (ER), a Gantt chart, the classes or a mind map, by its first line. Without Value the text is the body of the element (flowchart LR ...), without the indentation its lines share. A text it cannot read shows the reason and emits error (its Line is the number of the line). In a page it takes the colors of the theme; SVG() returns it as the text of an SVG (its own colors, out of a page), Png(scale, callback) as a data URL of a PNG, Download(name, format) saves it as name.png or name.svg; ready gives the component itself, to call them. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Value | '' | | Label | '' | Events - error: The text cannot be read: the error, its Line the number of the line. - ready: It is made: the component itself, to call Download, Png or SVG. Slots default Methods - SVG() - Png(scale, callback) - Download(name, format, callback) Example

Title: DialPad
Text:
A dial pad: the number in a field over a grid of keys, a key that erases and a key that calls. Value is the number. Keys is the layout, row by row in Columns columns: [{Value, Label, Sub, Hold, Icon, Class}]: Value goes into the number, Label shows on the key (Value when empty) with Sub under it (the letters of a phone), Hold goes in place of Value after a long press (+ on 0), Icon draws the key, Class gives it a look of its own. Without Keys it is the pad of a phone: 1 to 9, , 0 and #. ShowInput shows the field (the keys of the keyboard and a paste go in too, of the characters of the keys), ShowCall the key that calls, CallLabel its name; Disabled locks it. The key that erases takes the last character back, and the whole number when held. Events: input (the number), press ({Value}): a key pressed, call (the number): the key that calls, or Enter. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Value | '' | | Keys | null | | Columns | 3 | | ShowInput | true | | ShowCall | true | | CallLabel | '' | | Label | '' | | Hold | 500 | | Disabled | false | Events - input: The number changed: the number. - press: A key was pressed: {Value}. - call: The key that calls (or Enter): the number. Example

{{Note}}

Tests - DialPad puts the keys pressed into the number, erases the last one, and calls with it — tests/regression/library-controls.test.js

Title: Dialog
Text: A modal dialog. Open shows it; the close event (with the reason: 'close', 'escape' or 'backdrop') asks the owner to set Open back to false. Slots: default (the body), footer (the actions). Size: small, medium, large or full. Dismissible: false keeps it open on Escape and backdrop presses, which shake it (for flows that need an explicit answer). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Open | false | | Title | '' | | Description | '' | | Icon | '' | | Size | 'medium' | | Closable | true | | Dismissible | true | | Padded | true | Events - close: It asks to close (the owner sets Open to false): the reason, close, escape or backdrop. Slots default, footer Example

Title: DialogHost
Text: Shows the confirmations and alerts of the Dialogs Service, one modal Dialog each, the last one on top: place one in the layout of the Application. Escape and a press on the backdrop dismiss a dialog unless it is not Dismissible. Example

Title: DiffView
Drawer
Text: A panel that slides in from an edge of the window over the page (modal: the page behind is inert). Open shows it; the close event (with the reason: 'close', 'escape' or 'backdrop') asks the owner to set Open back to false. Side: right (default), left, top or bottom. Size: small, medium, large or full (the width, or the height for top and bottom). Slots: default (the body), actions (beside the title), footer. Dismissible: false keeps it open on Escape and backdrop presses, which shake it. Title: Drawing
Text:
A vector drawing (SVG): shapes, lines, arrows, freehand strokes of brushes and texts, on layers, grouped or not. Value is its model, as JSON keeps it: {Width, Height, Background, Layers: [{ID, Name, Visible, Locked, Items}]}, an item {ID, Type, Stroke, Fill, Width, Opacity} with, by its Type: rect and ellipse {X, Y, W, H}, line and arrow {Points: [{X, Y}, {X, Y}]}, path {Points: [{X, Y}], Brush}, text {X, Y, Text, Size} and group {Items}; the points are in the units of the drawing (Width by Height), whatever its size on the screen. change emits the model after each action, select the IDs of the items selected. Tool is the one in hand: select (a press selects an item, Shift adds one, a drag on the empty drawing selects the ones it covers, a drag moves them, the handles resize the one selected), rect, ellipse, line, arrow, path (freehand with Brush: pen, marker, highlighter or calligraphy), text (a press writes a text there; a double press edits one) and eraser (the items it passes over go). Stroke, Fill ('none' for no fill) and StrokeWidth paint the new items and the ones selected. Layer is the ID of the layer the new items go into (the first one without; a DrawingLayers shows and orders the layers). Toolbar shows the tools, the colors and the actions over it. ReadOnly shows the drawing alone. The keys on the drawing: Delete removes the selection, the arrows move it (Shift: by 10), Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z) undo and redo, Ctrl+A selects the items of the layer, Ctrl+G groups, Ctrl+Shift+G ungroups, Escape leaves the selection. Methods: Undo(), Redo(), Delete(), Group(), Ungroup(), Forward(), Backward() (the selection up or down its layer), Select(ids), Selected(), Add(item, layer), Clear(), SVG() (the text of the SVG, without the hidden layers) and PNG(callback, scale) (callback(error, data URL of the picture)). Methods - Undo() - Redo() - Selected() - Select(ids) - Add(item, layer) - Clear() - Delete() - Group() - Ungroup() - Forward() - Backward() - SVG() - PNG(callback, scale) Example

Title: Experiment

Title: FacetFilter

Title: Field
Text: A label, a hint and an error around a control; the label names the control for a screen reader (aria-labelledby, unless the control has a name of its own). Error shows an error of its own. In a form it shows the errors of a control of the Forms Service once the control is touched (left once, or the form submitted): - Control: a control made in code (Forms.Control, or Model.Get('email') of a Group); - or Name, inside a Form: the Field asks the Form for the control of that name; when the Model of the Form has none, it is made of the Field: its first value (Value, or the value of the control inside), and its validators Required, Email, Min, Max, MinLength, MaxLength, Pattern and Match (the name of a field whose value it must repeat). The value comes from the control inside: a native one (input, textarea, select: its value, or checked for a check box) or a Component of ElemenxUI (its change); the control is touched when the focus leaves the field, and a value set in code goes back into a native control. Messages ({required: 'text'...}) give the errors texts of their own, otherwise they are the phrases of the Forms Service. Title: FindBar
Text:

Title: Form
Text:
A form: a
that collects its fields into Model, a Group of the Forms Service, and validates them. Model is a Group made in code (Forms.Group, Forms.Control and their validators), or, without one, a Group the Form makes of its Fields: a Field with a Name and its validators (Required, Email, Min, Max, MinLength, MaxLength, Pattern, Match) adds its control to it; a Field whose Name is in the Model takes the control of the Model. A Name of parts, as the forms of a server read them (user[address][city], items[2][name], tags[] for the next item of a list, or user.address.city), nests its control in groups and arrays: Value is {user: {address: {city}}, items: [{name}], tags: [...]}, and the groups a Field leaving empties go with it. On submit (a button of type submit, Enter in a field, or Submit()) every field is touched, so their errors show, and once nothing is pending the form emits submit with {Value, Model} if it is valid, or invalid with {Errors, Model} and the focus goes to the first field in error. A reset (a button of type reset, or Reset()) brings the Model back to its first values; event reset. Disabled disables the fieldset of the form. Title: Gallery
Text:
A gallery: one picture at a time out of Items [{ID, Image, Thumb, Alt, Title, Description, Tags}], with buttons to the previous and the next one, dots, a counter and thumbnails. Index is the picture shown; change emits the new one, select the item of a press on the picture. - What shows: ShowTitle, ShowDescription, ShowTags (the caption: Caption 'overlay' over the picture, the default, or 'below' it), ShowArrows, ShowDots, ShowCounter, ShowThumbs. A caption with nothing to show is left out. - Autoplay goes to the next picture (Direction 'next') or the previous one ('previous') every Interval milliseconds; it waits while the pointer or the focus is on the gallery and while the page is hidden, and a button pauses and plays it. Loop (true) goes round at the ends. - Effect: slide (the default) or fade. Fit: cover (the default) or contain. Ratio: the shape of the picture ('16 / 9'). - The arrows (Home, End) change the picture when the gallery has the focus; the picture follows a finger across, or the mouse that drags it (swipe), and a swipe goes to the next or the previous one (held back at the ends without Loop). Text:

Title: GameInventory
Text:
An inventory: a grid of Slots cells (Items.length by default) in Columns columns. Items are by cell (null for an empty cell): {ID, Name, Icon or Image, Count, Stack (the most a pile holds), Rarity (common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary: the frame of its cell), Color, Badge (a mark in a corner: '+5'), Class (more classes of its cell and its card, for a look of their own), Active (an item in use, as one worn: the active look of the theme), Type, Description, Stats: [{Label, Value}]}. The selected cell wears the mark of the theme around it. Name names the inventory in the places of a drag. The pointer or the focus on an item shows its card. - Arrows move between the cells (a gamepad too); Enter or a double press uses an item (use); Space picks an item up and Space again puts it into the cell at the focus (Escape puts it back); Delete discards it (discard). - The pointer drags an item (a draggable of Type 'game-item' with Data {Item, From}; From is the place it comes from, {Kind: 'inventory', ID, Name, Index}). Onto a cell of the same inventory it moves there: piles of the same item join up to its Stack (the GameItems Service), other items swap. An item that comes from anywhere else (another inventory, a GameSlot, any draggable of the game) emits receive ({Item, From, To, Current}: Current is what the cell holds), and the owner moves it: GameItems.Move(Item, Current) tells what the cell and the place it came from hold then. An item of this inventory dropped elsewhere also emits give ({Index, Item, From, Target}). - move carries {From, To, Items}: Items is the list with the two cells swapped, for the owner to keep. select carries {Index, Item} as the focus moves. Label names the grid for screen readers. A cell with an item takes its Color (or the color of its Rarity) under the gloss of the theme. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Items | [] | | Slots | 0 | | Columns | 6 | | Label | '' | | Name | '' | Events - select: Another cell was selected: {Index, Item}. - use: An item was used (Enter or a double press): {Index, Item}. - move: An item moved to another cell: {From, To, Items}, the cells after the move. - discard: An item was discarded (Delete): {Index, Item}. - receive: An item came from another inventory or slot: {Item, From, To, Current}. - give: An item was dropped on another place: {Index, Item, From, Target}. Title: GameItemCard
Text:
The card of an item of a game: its Name in the color of its Rarity, its Rarity and Type, its Stats [{Label, Value}] and its Description, on the panel of the theme. Item is the item; Place is where it shows: a style that fixes it to the viewport (GameItems.Place(element) gives the one beside an element). GameInventory and GameSlot show it for the item under the pointer or the focus; any place of the items of a game may show it the same way. Its markup is phrasing content, so it fits inside a button. Title: GameKey
Text:
The prompt of a control: "[A] Continue". It shows the button of the gamepad in use (Button: a, b, x, y, lb, rb, lt, rt, select, start... drawn the way that kind of pad names it: A, ✕, B) and, without a gamepad, the key of the keyboard (Keyboard: 'Enter', 'E', 'Escape'). Label is the text after it. It follows the pad: plug one in or switch pads and it changes. Pad (xbox, playstation, nintendo, generic) shows the buttons of that kind of pad whatever is plugged in (a page of help). The button is drawn as on its pad: the colors and the symbols of the face buttons, the shoulders, the triggers, the sticks, the d-pad with its arm lit, the buttons of the menus. Title: GameObject
Text:
An object of a game, of any kind, declared in a GameScene (or a GameWorld): Kind names its kind (the Kinds Service: what it extends, what it can do, its Traits, and what it is made of, its Parts), and every other attribute is a field of it or of one of its Traits, in any case (Radius, Distance, Speed, Team: whatever its kind has). ID, Name, Team. A GameObject declared inside another goes round it when its kind moves (an Orbit, a Mover: a moon in its planet), and is a part of it otherwise (a module of a station); Part="dock" changes the part of that name that the kind of its parent gives it, Parent names what it goes round instead of its place. For a GameWorld (the map of cells) it is a thing on a cell: X and Y, Width and Height (1 by 1), Color, Image, Blocks (no way through it), Opaque (it hides what is behind it), Kind tree (the default there), rock or a name of your own. It shows nothing by itself. Title: GameScene
Text: The scene of a game in three dimensions on WebGL2 (the Graphics3D Service): objects of any kind (the Kinds Service), each made of what its kind extends, what it can do (its Traits, each run by a system of the scene) and what it is made of (its Parts, objects of their own placed in it). The setting space (the default) brings the kinds of a star system and its systems: stars and planets on Kepler orbits (the Astronomy Service), lit by their stars (night sides, the shadows of moons and planets on each other and on rings), their surfaces of noise baked once into cube textures, belts and rings, stations of modules, fleets of ships that hold their place by a body and travel to another. Kinds of space: star (Star: Mass, Radius, Temperature, Luminosity, Color), planet (Orbit: Distance, Eccentricity, Inclination, Node, Periapsis, Anomaly, Period; Body: Radius, Mass, Day, Tilt, Albedo; Surface: Type, Colors, Water, Ocean, Ice, Clouds, Atmosphere, Seed), moon (a planet, small, one face to its planet), belt (Belt: Inner, Outer, Count, Inclination, Colors), ring (Ring: Inner, Outer, Inclination, Colors), station and outpost (an Orbit in radii of what they go round, a Model and parts: modules, a dock), fighter, cruiser and freighter (ships: Model, Health), fleet (Mover: Speed; Formation: Count, Ship, Spacing: its ships are parts). An application defines its own (Kinds.Define) and systems of its own for traits of its own (Systems: {Trait: {Update(object, scene), Draw(object, scene)}}). The objects: System ({Objects: [{ID, Kind, Parent, Values, Traits, Parts, Children}]}), Seed (a whole system of it: Astronomy.Generate) and GameObject declared inside (a GameObject in another goes round it when it moves, an Orbit or a Mover, and is a part of it otherwise; Part="dock" changes a part of the kind of its parent). Every attribute of a GameObject is a field of it or of a Trait, in any case. Time is the day (0), Speed the days of it a second (1), Paused holds it; Scale compressed (the default: large bodies, short distances) or real. The view: a drag turns it round the object in focus, the wheel or two fingers zoom, a click selects an object (or its label; a part of an object near enough), a double click flies to it (from its day side), Escape goes back, the arrows turn, + and - zoom, Enter flies to the selected one, Space holds the time. Orbits, Labels, Details (a card of the selected object), Background (the far stars), Team, the slot hud. Without WebGL2 it says so (and emits error). The surface: Land(id, {Latitude, Longitude, Altitude}) goes down to the ground of a body (not of a giant of gas), the very ground its baked surface shows (Terrain.Sphere), in patches finer near the eye, under its sky (its atmosphere and its star); a drag looks round, the wheel rises and comes down, WASD and the arrows walk, Escape or TakeOff() goes back up. The time runs SurfaceSpeed days a second there (1/120). Kinds of the ground (the setting terrain): ground (Terrain: Size, Height, Water, Scale, Ridges, Seed: a ground of noise, Terrain.Flat, in chunks finer near the eye, with its sea), sun (Sun: its light from far), unit (Walker: Speed, MaxSlope, Swim; a Model), tree, rock and house (Model, Blocks: what stands in the way). An object of it stands at X and Y of the ground; Move(id, [x, y]) walks a walker round what cannot be walked, a right click sends the selected one; the view turns round a point of the ground and the keys move it. Every model of the Models Service is a kind of the same name (knight, mech, wolf, oak, tower, reactor...), of the kind that fits it. The models stand in the light of their sun and cast shadows on each other and on the ground (Shadows); a Model plays clips of its pieces (Clip: the one it plays when idle): walk on a way by itself, Play(id, clip, callback) the others (attack, cast, work, die); the wind bends what grows. Events: ready (the scene, for its methods), select ({ID, Object, Info}: ID empty when none is), focus ({ID}), arrive ({ID, At}), land ({ID}), takeoff ({ID}), error ({Reason: webgl2}). Methods: Add(kind, props), Change(id, changes), Remove(id), Attach(parent, object), Detach(id), Get(id), Objects(filter), Describe(id), Position(id), Select(id), FocusOn(id), Move(id, target), Now(), SetTime(days), Play(id, clip, callback), ToScreen(id), Pick(clientX, clientY), Save(), Load(saved), Land(id, options), TakeOff(), Surface(), Supported(). Title: GameSlot
Text:
A slot of an action bar (hotbar): a button with an Icon or an Image, a Label for the hint and screen readers, Count and Rarity (common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary). Key binds a shortcut through the Hotkeys Service ('1', 'Q') and shows it (a control of the game, not a command: the lists of shortcuts leave it out). Pressing it (or its key) emits use while it is ready; with Cooldown (milliseconds) it then cools down: a sweep runs over it with the seconds left, and ready is emitted at the end. Cool(milliseconds) starts a cooldown from the code (a shared cooldown, for example); Active marks a toggled action; Disabled, Size (small, medium, large). Several slots in a row:
. Color tints the glass under its icon (by default the color of its Rarity; Rarity frames it too); Badge is a mark in a corner ('+5'), Classes more classes for a look of their own. Data is what the slot holds (an item of the game: {ID, Name, Icon, Count, Stack...}, or a skill). The slot is a place of the drags of the game: it is dragged (Draggable, true by default; a draggable of Type 'game-item' with Data {Item, From}, From {Kind: 'slot', Key, Name: Group}) and takes what is dropped on it (Accept: the Types it takes, ['game-item'] by default; [] takes nothing): drop carries {Item, From, To, Current} (Current is Data) and the owner moves the item, with GameItems.Move. The pointer or the focus on a slot whose Data has more than a name (Description, Type, Rarity, Stats) shows its card (GameItemCard), as in an inventory; it follows the slot when the page scrolls. Title: GameWorld
Text:
The world of a strategy game, seen from above (Projection orthogonal) or at an angle (isometric): a map of cells drawn on a canvas, its buildings, units and things, the selection of the units of the player, their orders and their ways round what blocks them, the fog of war. The map: Map (its JSON, or the URL of a JSON of its own or of Tiled, .tmj: see the GameMaps Service), and what is declared inside it: GameTerrain (a kind of ground), GameLayer (rows of ground), GameBuilding, GameUnit and GameObject (a tree, a rock). Team is the team of the player: its units are selected (a click, Shift for more, a frame drawn with the mouse, a double click for all of their Type, Ctrl+A for all) and ordered (a right click, or a tap on a touch screen: they find their way, A, and spread round the goal); Fog hides what they do not see, and keeps what was explored. The view moves as the one of Board (X, Y, Zoom, MinZoom, MaxZoom; the wheel zooms at the pointer, a drag with the middle button or with Space held moves it, so do the arrows; + and - zoom), Grid draws the lines of the cells, Minimap the whole map in a corner, Paused and Speed hold and hurry the time. The slot hud takes the HUD of the game over the world. Events: ready (the world, for its methods), load ({Width, Height}), select ({IDs, Objects}), order ({Kind: move, attack or stop, IDs, X, Y, Target}), arrive ({ID, X, Y}), cell ({X, Y, Button, Object}: a press that is not a selection nor an order), view ({X, Y, Zoom}), error. Title: Image
Text:
A picture that is easy to place. Src and Alt; Lazy (on by default) loads it when it comes near the viewport. Fit is the fit of the picture in its box (cover, contain, fill, none, scale-down) and Position the point it keeps in view (center, top, '30% 20%'...). Its box: Width and Height (a number of pixels or a length), Ratio ('16/9', '4:3', 1.5) and Stretch, how it follows its container: none (its own size, shrunk to the width of the container), width (as wide as the container), height (as high as it) or both (it fills it). Shape rounded or circle. While it loads a shimmer holds its place (Placeholder); a picture that does not load gives way to Fallback, then to the icon of a picture. Events load and error with {Src}. Title: ImageCropper
Text:

Title: Input
Text:
A text field. A password field has an eye button: Guarded asks before it shows the password, HideAfter hides it again (see the Reveal Service). Preset: a format of the FieldFormats Service (email, url, semver, ipv4, ipv6, uuid, iban, postal-code, integer, decimal, or one the Application registers): the field gets its keyboard and autofill, keeps only the characters the format holds, and checks the value when it is committed: it normalizes it, looks invalid when it is wrong and emits validate with {Valid, Value, Message} (put Message in the Error of a Field); the change event carries the normalized value. Country is the country of a postal-code, Min and Max bound an integer or a decimal. Title: Jog
Text:
The jog wheel of a DJ: a platter with a record on it that turns as the track plays (Playing, at Rpm turns a minute: 33.3 by default), its marker where Time is (a turn is 60 / Rpm seconds). A hand on the record holds it and scratches: touch (true, then false when it lets go) and scratch ({Delta, Time}: the seconds the record was turned, forward positive) while it turns it. The ring around it bends the pitch: a drag on it, or the wheel, emits nudge ({Delta}, from -1 to 1 for a quarter turn). Keys: the arrows nudge, with Shift they scratch by a twentieth of a turn. Title and Subtitle are written on the label of the record; Size is its width in pixels. The track is the application's: Time follows it, and the platter turns between its updates by itself while Playing. Title: Keyboard
Text:
A keyboard of a computer, drawn key by key (the look and the controls): to show hotkeys, the keys held, or to take presses on a screen. Layout: 'full' (with the number pad), 'tkl' (without it) or 'compact' (the main block alone). Keys are named by their code (KeyboardEvent.code: KeyA, Digit1, ShiftLeft, ArrowUp, Numpad7...). - Pressed: the codes shown pressed; Live also shows the keys held on the keyboard of the user while the page has the focus (class held: a key that goes down or up changes its own button, not the whole keyboard), but for the keys a control in the focus takes for itself (a Piano that plays them, a hotkey: they prevent the default of the key). Marks: {code: class} marks keys (a hotkey, a group of keys of a game), true for the mark of the theme. - Labels: {code: text} names keys of their own; Native names the keys of characters as the keyboard layout of the user writes them (navigator.keyboard, Chrome and Edge), US English otherwise. - Alternate: a second layout on the keys of characters, as on the keyboards of countries with another alphabet: the first one large in the top left corner of a key, the second one smaller in its bottom right corner. A name of a layout of the Library ('ru' Russian, 'uk' Ukrainian, 'el' Greek, 'he' Hebrew), 'native' (the layout of the user, as Native reads it), or {code: text} for any other. - Clickable: a press of a key emits press ({Code, Label}); a key of the screen keyboard is a button. Title: Knob
Text:
A knob: a rotary input with the look of the dial Meter, an open ring of three quarters around a cap with a pointer. Value between Min and Max, in steps of Step. The ring fills from Origin (Min when null; the middle of a range from -100 to 100 for a pan, say) to the value. Ticks puts that many ticks along the ring; ShowValue shows the value and Unit under the cap. Dragging up or to the right turns it up (Sensitivity pixels for the whole range); the arrows (Step), Page Up/Down (ten steps), Home and End turn it from the keyboard, and so does the wheel while it has the focus. A double click sets it back to Default, when there is one. Events: input while turning, change on release. Title: Markdown
Text: A document written in Markdown, shown: Value is read by the RichText Service (CommonMark with the tables, the strike and the fenced code of GitHub) and kept to its schema, so nothing in it runs. The code of a fence that names its language (js) is highlighted by the Syntax Service (Highlight, on by default). Look: 'document' (the default) looks as the text of a RichEditor (the classes of elemenx-document); 'interface' takes the classes of the interface of the Library instead, as a page of an Application: a table is an elemenx-table, a list an elemenx-ul or an elemenx-ol, a quote an elemenx-callout, a link an elemenx-link, code (a block or in a line) an elemenx-code, a rule an elemenx-divider. Without Value the text is the body of the element (## A title), without the indentation its lines share: the body follows its changes. The plugins of the RichText Service draw what Markdown has no element for: mermaid a Diagram, chart a Chart, ::: warning a callout... (RichText.Extend adds more). Title: MediaCard
Text:
The card of a title of a collection: a film, a show, an album, a game, a book. Image is its poster (or cover), Ratio its shape ('2:3' a poster, '1:1' a cover, '16:9' a frame of a game or an episode), Title and Subtitle (a year, an artist, a platform) under it, Kind a word on it (Film, Album, Game), Badge another (New, 4K; BadgeVariant its tone), Rating a score from 0 to Max (10 by default; 5 shows stars), Progress the part seen or played (0 to 1, a bar on the poster), Tags its genres. Playable shows a play button over the poster, Favorable the heart (Favorite). A press opens it, as Href does. Item is what its events give back (the item of a list it shows; {Title} without). Title: Menu

Title: MenuBar
Text:
A bar of menus, as at the top of the window of a program: File, Edit, View... Items are the menus ([{ID, Label, Icon, Disabled, Items}]), then the ones its MenuItem children declare (a MenuItem with MenuItems inside is a menu of the bar, its MenuItems the items of that menu). It behaves as the bar of a program: while a menu is open, the pointer on another one opens that one in its place; the left and right arrows go from menu to menu (and between the buttons of the closed bar), the down arrow opens one; F10, or Alt pressed alone, takes the first bar of the page to its first menu and gives the focus back. Caret shows the arrow of a menu by its label (none by default, as in a program). The select event carries the chosen leaf item (a declared one emits select on its MenuItem too). Title: MenuList
Text: One level of a Menu. Items: [{ID, Label, Icon, Shortcut, Disabled, Danger, Checked, Items, Separator, Group}]. Open shows it: a popup under the closest elemenx-popup-anchor around it (a button of your own and the list in one element of that class), placed by Placement ('bottom-start'; 'right-start' for a submenu), as wide as the anchor with MatchWidth. A press outside it or Escape emits "dismiss" with the reason: the owner sets Open back to false. An item with Items opens a nested MenuList to the right; a leaf item emits "select" with the item. Sheet shows the menu as on a phone: a sheet from the bottom of the screen over a shade, with large rows, its Title, and a Cancel row; an item with Items opens its items in the same sheet, with a row back. The sheet follows a finger that drags its top (the grabber and the title) down, and a swipe down there closes it. Title: Meter
Text: A measurement within a known range, like : Value between Min and Max. Low and High split the range into zones; Optimum tells which zone is good. The good zone shows success, the next one warning, the far one danger. Shape 'bar' draws a bar, across or upwards (Orientation 'vertical'); Shape 'dial' an open ring of three quarters, with a Needle, Ticks along it, and its middle the default slot (or the value when the slot is empty). Marks shows the marks of Low and High (not the Ticks), ShowRange the Min and the Max at the ends, ValuePlacement puts the value on a plate below the meter or in its corner (over the end of a bar; a dial gives the corner up: its ring is shorter, of five eighths). Title: Mixer
Text:

While a channel is on Solo, the others are left out of the mix and dim (Silenced). The mixer keeps what its strips change in their channels. Title: MixerChannel
Text:
A channel strip of an audio mixer (the look and the controls; the sound is the application's): its Label, Knobs (an equalizer, sends: [{Label, Value, Min, Max, Origin, Default, Unit}]), the Pan (-100 left to 100 right), the buttons Mute and Solo, the fader of its Volume in decibels between Min and Max, and the meter of its Level beside it: a level in decibels, or [left, right] for stereo, with the Peak held over it. Master is the strip of the master bus (no Solo); Silenced dims a strip another one's Solo leaves out (the Mixer sets it); Color marks the strip. Title: Mosaic
Text:
Items laid out in a box by the Layouts Service, as Layout says: bento (a grid of cells packed without holes, the items of Width and Height cells), masonry (columns of one width, each item into the shortest one: Height in pixels, or the Ratio of its picture), justified (rows of one height filling the width, each picture keeping its Ratio) or treemap (rectangles of areas by their Value, Children inside their parent). The width comes from the room the Mosaic has: Columns (bento, masonry) or as many columns as fit ColumnWidth; CellHeight is the height of a cell of a bento (its width by default), RowHeight the wanted height of a justified row (MaxRowHeight, LastRow), Height the one of a treemap. Gap is the room between the items. Items: [{ID, Title, Text, Image, Color, Width, Height, Ratio, Span, Value, Row, Column, Children, Class, Element, Render}], or declared inside it: MosaicItem (its content is the content of the item, a MosaicItem in it a child). An item shows its Image (covering it), its Title and Text over it, or its own content (Element, Render(container, item), the content of its MosaicItem). Selectable makes the items buttons: a press or Enter emits select with the item. The items move to their new places when the layout or the room changes. Arrangement() returns the places as the Layouts Service gives them. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Layout | 'bento' | | Items | [] | | Columns | 0 | | ColumnWidth | 0 | | CellHeight | 0 | | RowHeight | 200 | | MaxRowHeight | 0 | | LastRow | 'left' | | Height | 360 | | Gap | 8 | | Selectable | false | | Label | '' | Events - select: A Selectable item was pressed: the item. Slots default Methods - Arrangement() Example

Title: MosaicItem
Text: The declaration of an item in the template of a Mosaic: <MosaicItem ID="sea" Title="The sea" Image="sea.jpg" Ratio="1.5" />. It takes the props of an item of Mosaic (ID, Title, Text, Image, Color, Width, Height, Ratio, Span, Value, Row, Column, Class); markup inside it becomes the content of the item and keeps its bindings; MosaicItem inside another one is its child in a treemap. It shows nothing by itself: Mosaic reads it. Title: MultiSelect
Text: A select of several options. Options: [{Value, Label, Hint, Icon, Group, Disabled}]; Value is the list of the Values selected. Display: chips (the chosen options as removable tags in the field) or count ("3 selected"). Searchable (on by default) adds a filter field; SelectAll adds an option that toggles every enabled option. The list stays open while options are toggled. Placeholder, Empty, Size, Shape, Disabled and Invalid as in Select. Events: change (the list). Example <Field Label="Colors" [hint]="Colors.join(', ') || 'None'"><MultiSelect Placeholder="Pick colors" [options]="Options" [value]="Colors" SelectAll="true" (change)="Changed" /></Field> <Field Label="As a count"><MultiSelect Display="count" [options]="Options" [value]="Colors" (change)="Changed" /></Field> <script> ({ Colors: ['red', 'blue'], Options: [ {Value: 'red', Label: 'Red', Group: 'Warm'}, {Value: 'orange', Label: 'Orange', Group: 'Warm'}, {Value: 'yellow', Label: 'Yellow', Group: 'Warm'}, {Value: 'green', Label: 'Green', Group: 'Cold'}, {Value: 'blue', Label: 'Blue', Group: 'Cold'}, {Value: 'violet', Label: 'Violet', Group: 'Cold', Disabled: true} ], Changed: function (value) { this.Colors = value; } }) </script> Tests - MultiSelect toggles its options and gives the list of the Values chosen — tests/regression/library-forms.test.js

Title: NativeMenu
Text:
The menu of a program declared as a menu of the page: with MenuItem children, as in a Menu (a MenuItem with MenuItems inside is a submenu). Target window (by default) is the menu of the window, its top-level items the menus of a bar (File, Edit...); Target tray is the menu of the icon in the tray, opened by its right button. Look: elemenx (by default) draws them with ElemenxUI: the menu of the window a MenuBar where the layout places the NativeMenu (Caret, Variant and Size as in MenuBar; a program has no menu of the system without one), the menu of the tray a window of the Application at the pointer (Platform.TrayPopup, a NativeMenuPanel); system has the system draw them (Platform.Menu, Platform.TrayMenu). Both follow the template. A MenuItem with a Role (undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, selectAll, reload, toggleDevTools, resetZoom, zoomIn, zoomOut, togglefullscreen, minimize, close, quit) does what the system does for it (Platform.Role), with the usual shortcut of the role when it names none; its Shortcut is a hotkey of the program (Ctrl+N, Mod+N for Ctrl or Cmd). A choice is the select of its MenuItem, as in the page, and the select of the NativeMenu with the item. On the web the menu of a window is the bar without the items of the system, their shortcuts hotkeys of the page; a menu of the tray shows nothing. Events: select (the item chosen), apply ({Error} when the system refused the menu). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Target | 'window' | | Look | 'elemenx' | | Caret | false | | Variant | 'ghost' | | Size | 'small' | Events - apply: The menu was given to the system: {Error}, null when it went well. - select: An item was chosen in the menu of the program: the item. Slots default Example

Title: NativeMenuPanel
Text:
The menu of the tray of a program drawn by ElemenxUI: the list a NativeMenu of the tray puts in its window (Platform.TrayPopup), as a MenuList draws it. Items: [{ID, Label, Icon, Shortcut, Disabled, Danger, Checked, Items, Separator, Group}]; an item with Items opens them in its place, with a row back; Choose(item) is called with a leaf chosen, and the window hides. The window is see-through and takes the size of the list, so the list has the corners and the shadow of a menu of the page. The pointer and the arrows light an item (Enter or the right arrow takes it, the left arrow goes back a level); Escape hides the window, or goes back a level. The menu of the tray of a program, as its window shows it. Chosen: {{Chosen}}

Title: NavList
Text:
A navigation list or tree. Items: [{ID, Label, Icon, Badge, Items, Disabled}]; Value is the ID of the current item. Items with Items are groups that open and close (Expanded lists the open ones). Searchable filters the tree and opens the branches that match. Collapsed shows only the icons (for a narrow sidebar). The select event carries the item. Keys: arrows move, Enter selects, Right opens a group, Left closes it. Title: NotificationHost
Text: The notifications of the Application drawn by ElemenxUI (Platform.Notify with Look elemenx): cards of Items ([{ID, Title, Text, Icon, Image, Variant, Actions: [{ID, Label}], Progress, Duration, Stamp, Component, Props, Bare}]), the newest next to the corner, in the window by the corner of the screen of a program or in the corner of the page on the web (Page, Corner). A card with a Duration shows the time it has left, held while the pointer is over it (Hold(item), Release(item)); Progress (0 to 1) draws a bar of a task. A card of a Component of the Application holds it with its Props and Notification ({ID, Choose(action), Close()}): an invitation to a call, say (CallInvite); Bare leaves it without the frame of a card. More is the number of the cards past the limit. Choose(item, action) is called with a press on a card (action null) or on one of its buttons, Close(item) with its close button. The theme draws them: the elemenx-notification classes and the tokens of the surface. Title: NumberInput
Text:
A number field. Value is a number or null. Min and Max bound it, Step is the step of the arrows (Shift: ten steps) and of the buttons beside the field (Controls false hides them), Precision the number of decimals it keeps. Only digits, one point (a comma becomes one) and a leading minus can be typed; the value is bounded and rounded when it is committed. Prefix and Suffix stand inside the field ('$', 'kg'). Size, Shape, Placeholder, Name, Disabled, ReadOnly and Invalid as in Input. Events: input (Value, while typing), change (Value, when committed). Example
