Title: OTPInput
Text: A one-time code of Length characters. Value holds the characters only. Variant: 'split' (one cell per character, Group puts a separator after every Group cells) or 'single' (one field). Both are one real <input> (the cells of 'split' are drawn over it), so typing, paste, undo, selection and the one-time codes that a phone offers from a message all work as in any field. Pattern says which characters are taken: 'digits', 'letters', 'alphanumeric' or a character class ('[0-9A-F]'); Case 'upper' or 'lower' changes letters as they come. Anything else typed or pasted is dropped ('123-456' gives '123456'), and the code never grows past Length (a character typed over a filled cell takes its place); a pasted code fills from the caret, or replaces all of it when long enough. Masked hides the characters (an eye button shows them, Revealed) and keeps them from being copied; Guarded asks before the eye shows them, HideAfter hides them again (see the Reveal Service). Events: input (Value), change (on leaving the field), complete (Value, when the last character comes), validate ({Value, Complete, Valid}). Invalid marks the field; a field left incomplete is marked too. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Value | '' | | Length | 6 | | Pattern | 'digits' | | Case | '' | | Variant | 'split' | | Group | 0 | | Masked | false | | Revealed | false | | Guarded | false | | HideAfter | 0 | | MaskChar | '•' | | Placeholder | '' | | Label | '' | | Size | 'medium' | | Shape | 'default' | | Name | null | | Disabled | false | | AutoFocus | false | | Invalid | false | Events - input: The characters changed: Value. - validate: The code was checked: {Value, Complete, Valid}. - complete: All Length characters are in: Value. - change: The code was committed: Value. Example <Field Label="The code from the message" [hint]="Note"><OTPInput Length="6" Group="3" (complete)="Completed" (input)="Typed" /></Field> <Field Label="A key, masked"><OTPInput Length="8" Variant="single" Pattern="alphanumeric" Case="upper" Masked="true" /></Field> <script> ({ Note: 'Type or paste 123-456.', Typed: function (value) { this.Note = value.length + ' of 6'; }, Completed: function (value) { this.Note = 'Checking ' + value + '...'; } }) </script> Tests - OTPInput drops what its Pattern refuses, changes the case, never grows past Length, and tells once it is complete — tests/regression/library-inputs.test.js

Title: Pagination
Text:
Pages of a list of Count items, PageSize (10) on each: the range shown ('11–20 of 57'), a choice of PageSizes (none when empty), and the buttons of the first page, the previous one, the numbers (the first, the last and the ones around Page, with gaps between), the next one and the last. Page is from 1. Used by Table; works under any list. ShowRange, ShowPages, ShowFirstLast and ShowPrevNext switch the range, the numbers, the buttons of the first and the last page and those of the previous and the next one. Siblings is how many numbers show on each side of Page (1), Boundaries how many at each end (1); a gap that would hide a single page shows that page. Events: page ({Page, PageSize}). Title: PhoneInput
Text: Value is the international number: "+" with the dialling code and the local digits ("+79991234567"). The field shows it in the country of Country, or, when the code of that country does not start it, in the country its code names (Value "+447911123456" shows the United Kingdom whatever Country says). Countries defaults to every country of the Countries Service, named in Locale and sorted by code; it may be replaced by [{Code, Name, Dial, Mask}], where Mask describes the national part (# is a digit). Guide keeps the whole template visible ('+7 (99) --'); Backspace 'skip' moves over a separator instead of deleting the digit before it. Only digits that fit the mask of the selected country are accepted, by typing, paste, drop or autofill. Title: Piano
Text:
The keys of a piano (the look and the controls; the sound is the application's). From is the first note (C3), Octaves how many octaves follow it (and their last C). A press plays a note, a slide over the keys plays the ones it crosses, several fingers play a chord; the lower on a key the press, the louder (Velocity from 1 to 127). While it has the focus, the keys of the computer play it too: A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P ; ' from the first C on, Z and X shift them an octave down and up. - Pressed: notes shown played (a song, a MIDI keyboard); Marks: {note: class} marks notes (a scale, a chord), true for the mark of the theme. Notes are written as C4, C#4, Db4 or MIDI numbers. - Labels: what the keys show. 'none'; 'c' (the name of every C, the default); 'notes' (the name of every note, without its octave: C, C#, D...); 'all' (with its octave: C4, C#4...); 'keys' (the key of the computer that plays it, as it is now, Z and X included); 'both' (the note and that key). Size: small, medium or large. Events: noteon ({Note, Midi, Velocity}), noteoff ({Note, Midi}). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | From | 'C3' | | Octaves | 2 | | Pressed | [] | | Marks | {} | | Labels | 'c' | | Size | 'medium' | | Label | '' | | Disabled | false | Events - noteon: A note started: {Note, Midi, Velocity}. - noteoff: A note ended: {Note, Midi}. Example

{{Note}} · the marked notes are the C major scale; with the focus, A W S E D... play it, Z and X shift an octave.

Tests - a piano plays the key pressed, louder lower on it, slides over keys, takes the keys of the computer and marks notes — tests/examples/ui-kit.spec.js

Title: PianoRoll
Text:
The notes of a part, to see and to edit: the keys of a piano down the left (Low to High, MIDI numbers: C3 to C6 by default), the beats across (Bars of Beats). Notes: [{ID, Note (MIDI), Start, Length (beats), Velocity (0 to 1)}]. A press on the grid puts a note there (as long as the last one, drag to make it longer), a drag moves the notes selected (in time and in pitch), a drag of the end of a note resizes it; a double press takes a note away. Times snap to Snap beats (a quarter: a sixteenth note). A press selects a note, Shift adds to the selection. Keys: Delete takes the selected notes away, the arrows move them (a Snap, a semitone; Shift and Up or Down an octave), Shift and Left or Right resize them, Mod+A selects every note, Escape none. Position is the playhead (beats; -1 for none), Loop ({Start, End}) is marked on the ruler; a press on the ruler seeks. A press on a key of the piano emits key. Events: change (Notes), select (the IDs selected), key (its MIDI number), seek (a beat). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Notes | [] | | Low | 48 | | High | 84 | | Bars | 4 | | Beats | 4 | | Snap | 0.25 | | Position | -1 | | Loop | null | | ReadOnly | false | | Label | '' | Events - change: The notes changed: Notes. - select: The selection changed: the IDs of the notes. - key: A key of the piano was pressed: its MIDI number. - seek: The ruler was pressed: the beat. Example

Press the grid to put a note, drag it to move it, drag its end to resize it; a double press takes it away. Delete, the arrows and Shift edit the notes selected.

Title: Pipeline
Text:
A pipeline of CI, as GitHub and GitLab show one: its stages in columns, the jobs of each as cards with their status, their name, their time and an action, the links between them. Only the view: where the data comes from is the owner's. Stages: [{ID, Name, Status, Jobs: [{ID, Name, Status, Duration, Started, Needs, Group, Text, Href, Actions, Element, Render}]}], or declared inside it: PipelineStage with its PipelineJob (the content of one is the content of its card). Status is created, pending, scheduled, running, success, failed, warning (failed, allowed to), canceled, skipped or manual; the one of a stage, without its own, is the one of its jobs (a failed job first). Duration is in seconds; a running job with Started (a date, or milliseconds) counts its time as it goes. Needs are the IDs of the jobs a job waits for. The jobs of one Group (a matrix) are one card, its count and its status, opened by a press. Links: needs (from the jobs of Needs; the default when a job has some), stages (from each stage to the next one, as GitLab joins them) or none. Over a job its needs and the jobs that need it are marked, the others fade. A press or Enter on a job emits select ({Job, Stage}), the arrows go from job to job; Actions (true) shows the action of a job: retry (failed, canceled, success, warning), cancel (running, pending) or play (manual), which emits action ({Action, Job}); a job may list its own Actions ([{ID, Icon, Label}]). Title and Summary (true) show the name of the pipeline, its status and its time above it. Title: PlanCard
Text:
The card of a plan of a subscription: Name and Description in a header (in Color, as a tile of the Metro style), Popular (the label of the plan to point out: 'Most popular'), the Price of a month in Currency (0 is Free) or of a year (Period 'year': YearlyPrice, otherwise twelve months), a Note, the Features ([{Label, Included, Hint}] or labels; Included false crosses one out) and the button (Action) that chooses it. Selected and Current (the plan of the user) mark it. Selectable makes it a radio of a group (PlanPicker); Tabbable makes it the one the Tab key reaches. Variant as in Card. Events: select ({ID}). Title: PostCard
Text:
The card of a post of a blog: Image, Category, Title, Excerpt, Tags, the Author (Avatar, or initials), its Date and ReadTime (minutes), and the counts of Likes and Comments (null hides them). Layout: vertical, horizontal (the image beside the text) or overlay (the text over the image). DateBadge shows the day and the month on the image, as a tile of the Metro style. Variant and Href as in Card. The default slot adds content under the excerpt. Events: like ({Liked, Likes}), comment, share. Title: QRCode
Text:
The QR code of a text (the QR Service): an address, a contact, the details of a payment. Level of error correction: L, M (the default), Q or H (a code with a logo over it needs H). Size in pixels, Margin in modules (4, the quiet zone a reader needs), Dark and Light its colors (black on white reads best; Light transparent for none). - Its style: Modules (square, dots, rounded or diamond), Eyes (the three corners: square, rounded, circle or leaf) and EyeColor, Gradient ({From, To, Angle}), Logo (a picture in the middle, LogoSize of its width: 0.22) or Text (a word there); with them the level is H, so the code still reads. - SVG() returns it as the text of an SVG; Image(size) as a data URL of a PNG at once (the modules square, no logo); Png(size, callback) as a data URL of a PNG of its whole style, callback(error, url); Download(name, format) saves it as name.png (format png, the default) or name.svg (svg): a download on the web, the dialog of the system in a program; ready gives the component itself, to call them. A text too long for a code shows nothing and emits error. Text: Reads QR codes (and other barcodes, Formats) from the camera: the picture of the camera at the back of a phone in a frame, and scan with {Value, Format} for each code read. Active starts and stops the camera (Start() and Stop() too). The browser reads the codes (BarcodeDetector: Chrome and Edge on Android, ChromeOS and macOS, Safari): elsewhere, and when the camera is refused, it says so and emits error ({Reason: 'unsupported', 'denied' or 'camera'}); the content of its tag shows then (a field to type the code). Title: Quiz
Text:
A quiz or a survey: its questions one at a time, a bar of the progress, the score at the end. Questions: [{ID, Text, Type, Options: [{ID, Text, Correct, Next}], Points, Answer, Tolerance, Explanation, Image, Next}], or declared inside it: QuizQuestion with its QuizOption (the text of an option is what it holds). Type: single (one option), multiple (all the right ones, no wrong one), text (one of the texts of Answer, without case and spaces round it), number (Answer, give or take Tolerance) or order (the options in the order they are given; shown mixed). Points (1) count a right answer. Next leads to another question (its ID, or end): the one of the option chosen first, else the one of the question, else the next one; Back goes back the way it came. Mode quiz scores the answers; survey only gathers them (no right one). Feedback: instant (the answer is checked before the next question, with its Explanation), end (in the review at the end, the default) or none. PassScore is the percent that passes (70). TimeLimit gives the whole of it seconds (0: no limit): at 0 it ends. Shuffle mixes the options. Title and Intro make a screen to start from (Start). Events: start, answer ({Question, Value, Correct, Points}), finish ({Score, Max, Percent, Passed, Answers}). Methods: Start(), Restart(). Title: Ribbon
Text:
A ribbon of commands, as in Microsoft Office: tabs of RibbonTab, each with RibbonGroup groups of RibbonButton, RibbonGallery and any other controls, declared in the template: ... Slots: quick (the quick access toolbar, before the tabs), end (after them: a search, a share button) and backstage (a RibbonBackstage: the File button opens it over the Workspace of the Ribbon, or over the window without one). Tab is the current tab (the first one that is not contextual by default). A narrow Ribbon shrinks its groups step by step (see RibbonGroup). Collapsed shows only the tabs: a tab then opens its panel over the page until a command runs; a double click on a tab, the pin button or Ctrl+F1 collapse and pin it. When even the narrow bar has no room for the tabs, a button with the title of the current tab takes their place and lists them. Key tips: Alt (or F10) shows a letter on every tab, the File button and the quick access commands; a letter opens its tab and shows the letters of its commands; a letter of a command runs it; Escape goes back a level. Events: tab ({ID}), command ({ID, Item}) for every RibbonButton, RibbonGallery and command page, collapse ({Collapsed}), backstage ({Open}). Title: RibbonGallery
Text:
A gallery of a RibbonGroup: a strip of samples (styles, layouts, colors) that scrolls row by row, and a button that shows all of them. Value is the chosen ID; Columns the samples in a row of the strip. Labels writes the Label of each sample under it in the strip too. Drag names a type of drags (draggable): a sample pulled away is dragged with its ID as the Data, to where a droppable of that type takes it (a canvas, a list). Events: select ({ID, Item}); the Ribbon reports it as command ({ID: the ID of the gallery, Item}). Keep never shrinks the group (a search field, what the tab is for): the panel scrolls instead once the others are one button each. Title: RichEditor
Text:
An editor of rich text (WYSIWYG). Value is the HTML of the document, kept to the schema of the RichText Service (paragraphs, headings, quotes, code, lists, tables, images, links and the inline styles); paste and drop go through it too. It has no toolbar: the controls of an Application call Command, and a small menu over a selection gives the quick styles (Menu false hides it). - Value, Placeholder, ReadOnly, Disabled, Label, Rows (the least height in lines) and MaxRows (the most, then it scrolls; 0 grows with the text), Menu. - Command(name, value): bold, italic, underline, strike, code; paragraph, heading (value 1-4), quote, codeblock; bullets, numbers, indent, outdent; link (value: the URL; empty removes it), unlink; image (value: {Src, Alt} or the URL), table (value: {Rows, Columns}), row, column, row-delete, column-delete, table-delete; rule; clear; undo, redo; plugin (value: the name of a plugin of the RichText Service, or {Name, Text, Attributes}: a diagram, a chart, a callout..., its Insert data by default). It returns false for a name it does not know or while it cannot edit. - A plugin in the document is one block the caret does not enter, drawn by its Component; a double press edits its text in place (its own editor when it has Edit), Mod+Enter or leaving it keeps the text, Escape leaves it as it was. - Typing Markdown at the start of a paragraph makes blocks: '# ' to '#### ' headings, '- ' a list, '1. ' a numbered list, '> ' a quote, ' ' code. Keys: Mod+B, Mod+I, Mod+U, Mod+E (code), Mod+K (the link event), Tab and Shift+Tab in a list nest its items. - Methods: Focus(), Formats() (what the selection has: {Bold, Italic, Underline, Strike, Code, Block, Level, List, Link, Table}), Insert(html), Markdown(), SetMarkdown(text), Text(), Print(options, callback), Find(query, {Case, Word, RegExp}) (returns the count of matches, marks them by the Find Service and shows the one at the caret or after it), FindNext(), FindPrevious(), ReplaceCurrent(text), ReplaceAll(text), ClearFind(). - Mod+F opens its find bar (a FindBar over its corner), Mod+R (or Mod+H) with the replace row; FindBar: false leaves it out. - Events: input and change (Value), formats (Formats() as the selection moves), link ({Href, Text}: Mod+K, for a dialog of the Application), files (the files pasted or dropped: the Application uploads them and inserts images by Command), ready (the editor). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Value | '' | | Placeholder | '' | | ReadOnly | false | | Disabled | false | | Label | '' | | Rows | 8 | | MaxRows | 24 | | Menu | true | | FindBar | true | Events - ready: The editor is ready: the component itself, to call Command. - input: The document changed: its HTML. - formats: The styles at the caret changed: {Bold, Italic, Underline, Strike, Code, Block, Level, Quote, List, Link, Table}, to light the buttons of a toolbar. - link: A link was pressed: {Href, Text}. - files: Files were pasted or dropped: a list of File, for the Application to upload. - change: The document was committed when the focus left: Value. A press on the ruler pulls a guide out of it: pull ({Value, ClientX, ClientY}) asks the owner to follow the pointer with one. Title: Sampler
Text:
The pads of a sampler, as on a drum machine: Pads [{ID, Label, Color, Key, Sample, Note}] in Columns (4). A pad plays its Sample (a sound as the Audio Service decodes it: a URL, a Blob, an ArrayBuffer or an AudioBuffer), or its Note on the Instrument (an Instrument of the Audio Service) when it has none. A press plays it, harder near its top (or by the pressure of a pen); its Key of the keyboard plays it too. Mode oneshot (the default) plays a sample to its end, hold stops it when the pad is let go. A sound file dropped on a pad is its sample from then (load tells it). Trigger(id, velocity) plays a pad from code; Output() is the GainNode of its sound (a Spectrum hears it there). Events: play ({ID, Velocity}), release ({ID}), load ({ID, File}), error (a sample it cannot read). Title: SettingsMenu
Text:
A menu of settings as on a phone: rows in groups, each with an Icon on a tile of its Color, a Label, a Description under it, a Value and a chevron to the submenu of its Items. A row with Toggle is a switch (Checked); a row with Checked and no Toggle shows a check, as the choices of a submenu do. Badge is a count on the row. The submenu of a row with Choice is a choice of one: a press checks the row pressed, and its Label becomes the Value of the row. - Items: [{ID, Label, Description, Icon, Color, Value, Badge, Items, Choice, Toggle, Checked, Disabled, Danger}]; an item {Group, Note} starts a group of rows: its title above them (empty for none), its Note under them. - Title is the large title of the top menu; a submenu takes the Label of its row, under a button back to the menu above. Path is the IDs of the open submenus. - Variant: 'auto' (ios on an Apple device, material on the others), 'ios' (rows on rounded cards, as in the Settings of an iPhone) or 'material' (rows across, with round tiles, as in the Settings of Android). - Searchable shows a field that finds rows on every level by their Label and Description; a found row shows where it is, and pressing it does what pressing it in its menu does. - The arrows move between the rows, Enter and Space press one, the right arrow opens a submenu; the left arrow, Escape and Backspace go back. - Events: select ({ID, Item, Path}) for a row without Items, toggle ({ID, Item, Checked}), navigate ({Path}). Title: SignaturePad
Text:
A field to sign with a pen, a finger or the mouse: the strokes are smoothed, thinner where the pen moves fast or presses less. Value is the strokes ([[{X, Y, P}]] in pixels of the field, P the pressure), which redraw it at any size; change emits them after each stroke. Color and Width draw them; Clear() and Undo() (the buttons under it, unless Controls is false) take them away. Image(type) returns the signature as a data URL of a picture (image/png by default), SVG() as the text of an SVG; both are empty for no signature. ReadOnly shows a signature that cannot change. A point keeps T too, the milliseconds from the start of the signature (its rhythm, for a comparison). Reference compares the signature with one on file after each stroke (the Signatures Service): a signature, several of them (the samples of a person, enrolled), or a reference of Signatures.Enroll. compare emits {Score, Parts, Match, Threshold}; ShowResult (true) says under the field whether it looks like the one on file. Threshold is the score it must reach (by default the one of the reference, else 0.75). Compare(reference) returns the same at any time. It is a help for an interface, not a check of security: a check that matters runs on a server. Title: Tab
Text: A tab of a Tabs, declared in its template with its content: .... ID, Label, Icon, Badge, Closable and Disabled describe its tab in the strip (as the items of Tabs); the Tabs shows the content of the current tab under the strip and hides the others. Title: TabGroup
Text:
A group of tabs: their strip and the content of the current one, as the tabs of the files of an editor. The tabs are declared in it with their content (...), or given by Items ([{ID, Label, Icon, Badge, Closable, Disabled, Pinned}]: the owner puts the content in its body, as a TabSplit does). Active is the ID of the current tab (the first one while it names none). A Pinned tab stays first in the strip, has no cross, and a close of all the tabs, of the others, or of the ones to a side leaves it. The menu of a tab (its right button, a long press, the key of the menu or Shift+F10) closes it, the others, the ones to its right or its left, or all of them, pins it or unpins it; in a TabSplit (Splittable) it also splits the group to a side with a copy of the tab (Split), or with the tab itself (Split and move). A tab is dragged to another place of its strip, and in a TabSplit to another group, or to an edge of a group to split it there: the edge it would take shows while it is over it. Keys in the strip: the arrows, Home and End move between the tabs, Delete closes one, the key of the menu opens its menu; Ctrl+Page Down and Ctrl+Page Up anywhere in the group go to the next tab and the one before. Events: select (the ID), close (the ID, once a tab: the owner takes its Tab away), pin ({ID, Pinned}), and with Items, for its owner: order ({ID, Index}), move ({ID, From, Index}: a tab of another group put in its strip), drop ({ID, From, Side: left, right, top, bottom or center}) and split ({ID, Side, Move}: Move true takes the tab there, false puts a copy of it there). Each detail has Group, its name. In a TabSplit it is also a part of a layout declared in the template: .... Title: TabSplit
Text:
Groups of tabs side by side and one over another, as the editors of a code editor: a TabGroup in each part, the dividers between them dragged to share the room. The tabs are declared in it with their content (Tab); their layout is declared too, or comes from Layout: ... ...... Tabs declared out of a TabGroup go to the first group. Layout is the same as a model, and change tells it each time it changes, so an Application keeps it and gives it back: {Split: 'row' or 'column', Sizes: [percents], Children} of {Group, Tabs: [IDs], Active, Pinned: [IDs]}. A tab declared later opens in the group of the focus, current. A tab is dragged to another group, or to an edge of one to split it there; the menu of a tab splits its group to a side with a copy of it (Split: its Tab made again with $Copy, the same content and a state of its own, an ID of CopyID(id, n), :2 by default), or with the tab itself (Split and move: a group of one tab stays as it is). A copy closes at once (the owner has no Tab of it); the layout keeps the copies of each group in its Copies ({ID, Of}) and a Layout given makes them again. A group left with no tab goes, and its room goes to the others. Its parts keep their content as they move: their panels go from group to group, never made again. Events: change (the layout), select (the ID of the tab opened), close (the ID of a tab that asks to close: the owner takes its Tab away; until it does the tab stays out of the groups), copy ({ID, Of, Group}: a copy of a tab made in a new group). Methods: Open(id), Close(id), Split(id, side, move), Model(). Title: Table
Text:
A data table. Columns: [{Key, Title, Width, MinWidth, Align (left, center, right), Sortable, Resizable, Format, Filter, Options}], where Format(value, row) returns the text of a cell. Rows are objects identified by RowKey. Sort is {Key, Direction} ('asc' or 'desc'); SortLocal sorts Rows here, otherwise the owner sorts on the sort event. Selectable: none, single or multiple; Selected holds the selected keys and the select event reports them. Filters: a column with Filter ('text': the text holds it; 'select': one of Options, or of the values found; 'number': '10', '>10', '<=5', '5..10') gets a field under its title. Filters holds {Key: text}; FilterLocal filters here, otherwise the owner filters on the filter event. Pages: PageSize (0: one page) and Page (from 1) show a part of the rows, with a Pagination under the table; PageSizes offers other sizes. PageLocal pages here; otherwise Rows is the page itself and Total the number of all the rows. Tree: a row may hold child rows in Items (ChildrenKey); the first column shows a button that opens it (Expanded holds the open keys; Arrow Right and Left too). Sorting keeps the children under their parent; a filter keeps the parents of the rows it finds, open. Events: sort ({Key, Direction}), select (keys), activate (row: double click or Enter), resize ({Key, Width}), filter (Filters), page ({Page, PageSize}), expand (the open keys). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Columns | [] | | Rows | [] | | Label | '' | | RowKey | 'ID' | | Sort | null | | SortLocal | true | | Selectable | 'none' | | Selected | [] | | Caption | '' | | Empty | '' | | Height | '' | | Compact | false | | Striped | false | | Bordered | false | | Sticky | true | | Filters | {} | | FilterLocal | true | | Page | 1 | | PageSize | 0 | | PageSizes | [10, 25, 50, 100] | | PageLocal | true | | Total | null | | Tree | false | | ChildrenKey | 'Items' | | Expanded | [] | | OfLabel | '' | Events - sort: A sortable title was pressed: {Key, Direction}. - filter: A filter of a column changed: {Key: text}. - page: Another page or page size was chosen: {Page, PageSize}. - expand: A row was expanded or folded: the keys of the expanded rows. - select: The selection changed: the keys of the selected rows. - activate: A row was opened (a double press or Enter): the row. - resize: A column was resized: {Key, Width}. Example

Title: Tabs
Text:
A strip of tabs. Tabs: [{ID, Label, Icon, Badge, Closable, Disabled}]; Value is the ID of the active tab. Variant: line (an underline, the default), pill (rounded buttons) or editor (the tabs of the files of an editor). A Closable tab (or every tab, with Closable on the strip) has a cross; the middle button, Delete and Ctrl+W close it too. Keys: the arrows, Home and End move between the tabs. The owner renders the content of the active tab; content in the default slot goes after the tabs (an action, a button that adds a tab). Size; Label names the strip for screen readers. Tabs may be declared in the template too, with their content: ... in the default slot (see Tab). Their tabs follow the ones of Tabs in the strip, and the Tabs shows the content of the current one under the strip (the first tab that is not Disabled while Value names none). Orientation vertical stands the strip on a side of the content, Placement left (the default) or right, the text of its tabs turned on its side (read from the bottom up on the left, from the top down on the right, as the tool windows of an editor); Rotate false keeps it level (a list of sections, as in the settings). Its keys are then Up and Down. Events: change (the ID), close (the ID). Title: TagInput
Text:
A field of tags. Value: the tags (strings). Typing and Enter (or a Separator: ',' and ';' by default) adds a tag; a pasted list ('a, b; c' or one per line) adds each one; Backspace in an empty field removes the last tag; the cross of a tag removes it. Suggestions (strings) open under the field while typing (arrows and Enter pick one); AllowNew: false takes suggestions only. Pattern (a regular expression a tag must match, as '^[^@]+@[^@]+$'), Unique (true) and Max limit what is taken; a refused text stays in the field, marked, and emits invalid with {Text, Reason: 'pattern', 'duplicate', 'max' or 'unknown'}. Case 'lower' or 'upper' changes the tags. Events: change (the tags), add (a tag), remove (a tag), invalid. Title: Terminal
Text:
A terminal: a scrolling output above a command line. Lines: [{ID, Kind, Text}] where Kind is input, output, error, info or success. Enter emits command with the text; Arrow Up and Down walk the history of this terminal; Ctrl+L emits clear. Busy makes the command line read-only: it keeps the focus, so the next command can follow at once. Slots: actions (in the title bar, shown with Title or actions). The output follows new lines while the reader is at its end. Mod+F (or Ctrl+Shift+F) finds in the output: a FindBar under the title marks the matches (the Find Service) and goes from one to the next; Escape closes it. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Lines | [] | | Title | '' | | Prompt | '$' | | Placeholder | '' | | Busy | false | Events - command: Enter on the command line: the text of the command. - clear: Ctrl+L: clear the output. Slots actions Example

Title: TileGrid
Text:
Groups of tiles on a grid of 48px cells, like a start screen. Groups: [{ID, Title, Tiles, Locked, Actions, Element, Render}]. A group header shows Actions ([{ID, Icon, Label, Title, Run}], buttons that emit groupaction with {Group, Action} and call Run(group)) and custom content: Element (a DOM node) or Render(container, group). A Locked group keeps its tiles and takes no others. A tile is {ID, Title, Icon, Size (small 1x1, medium 2x2, wide 4x2, tall 2x4, large 4x4, xlarge 6x4), Width and Height (any number of cells, over Size), Row, Column, Color, Badge, Text, Class, Locked, Element, Render}. Row and Column place the tile on the cells of its group (from 0); a tile without them takes the first free place. Element or Render(container, tile) replace the icon and the text with custom content, Class adds classes, Locked keeps the tile in its place. Columns is the width of a group in cells; a group may have its own Columns and Rows (its least height), and while Editable the handles on its right edge, its bottom edge and its corner stretch it (pointer or arrow keys, whole cells, from its widest tile up to MaxColumns (0: no limit), from its lowest tile down), reported by change. Fit gives a group no more columns than the grid has room for: on a narrow screen the tiles that do not fit take free places below, and come back as it widens. Direction 'horizontal' puts the groups in one row, as on a start screen; 'columns' stacks them in columns, as the Start menu of Windows: a group has the Stack (a number) of its column, and the columns wrap to a new row when the grid is narrower than they are, each whole; a tile dragged above or below a group, or beside a column, starts a group there (unless GroupPolicy is 'none'). In wrap (the default) the stacks wrap the same way, a group a stack of its own until another goes above or below it: with GroupPolicy 'between' a tile dragged above or below a group starts a group in its stack (the room under its lowest tile stays the group's), and beside a stack a new stack. Scroll makes the grid scroll on its own (give it a height), and a tile dragged to its edge scrolls it. On a touch screen a finger scrolls over the tiles, and a press held still takes a tile. Arrangement() returns the places of the tiles and the sizes of the groups ([{ID, Title, Columns, Rows, Stack, Tiles: [{ID, Row, Column, Size, Width, Height}]}]); Restore(arrangement) brings them back (tiles and groups it does not name stay as they are); Persist (a key) keeps the arrangement in the storage of the browser and restores it on the next visit. A tile dragged past the right edge of a group widens it by a column after GrowDelay milliseconds there (the edge shows it), again while it stays. Events: open (the tile, on click or Enter). Editable lets the user move tiles by dragging: the tile goes to the cell under the top left corner of its ghost and pushes down the tiles in its way, while it moves, as the grid will look after the drop; places left empty stay empty. GroupPolicy decides where a dragged tile may start a new group: 'end' (beside the last group), 'between' (also between the groups) or 'none'; the new group is named NewGroupTitle and reported by groupcreate ({Group, Tile}). A group left empty by a drag goes away. The change event carries the new Groups, every tile of a changed group with its Row and Column; Escape puts everything back. The groups and tiles may also be declared in the template: with children that take the props of a tile; the markup inside a is its custom content, bound to the page like any markup. Declarations add to Groups (a with the ID of a tile of Groups gives it its props and content) and follow the template: a new joins its group, a removed one leaves, a changed prop shows; the places of the tiles stay with the grid once they are set. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Groups | [] | | Editable | false | | Columns | 4 | | MaxColumns | 12 | | Fit | false | | Direction | 'wrap' | | Scroll | false | | Persist | '' | | GrowDelay | 500 | | GroupPolicy | 'end' | | NewGroupTitle | '' | Events - open: A tile was pressed: the tile. - groupaction: An action of a group header was pressed: {Group, Action}. - change: The tiles or the groups were moved or resized: Groups, as they are now. - groupcreate: A tile dropped beside the groups made a new group: {Group, Tile}. Slots default Methods - Arrangement() - Restore(arrangement) Example

Title: Timeline
Text:
A line of time: its scale (ticks with their labels, chosen for the span in view: seconds to centuries, or numbers), its marks (a moment with a label above or under it: the labels of marks close together stack in rows instead of covering each other, a thin leader to their point), its ranges (from a moment to another, in lanes with their labels at the start, as a Gantt chart has them; the ones that overlap in rows of their lane), its progress (filled up to a moment, and a lighter Buffer) and a playhead, and the line of now. Start and End are the whole line; From and To the part in view (all of it by default). Scale: time (dates: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, a Date, milliseconds) or number (seconds of a video, steps: Unit names them, Format writes them); by default the one of Start. Orientation horizontal or vertical. Marks [{ID, At, Label, Text, Icon, Tone, Side, Element, Render}], Ranges [{ID, From, To, Label, Tone, Color, Lane, Element, Render}], Lanes [{ID, Label}], Progress (a moment, or {To, Buffer}), Playhead (a moment; Seekable shows it and lets it be moved), Now (the line of now). The same declared inside it: TimelineMark, TimelineRange (any content inside them is their label), TimelineLane, TimelineProgress. Interaction: Ctrl (or ⌘) with the wheel, a pinch or the buttons (Controls) zoom at the pointer, between MinSpan and the whole line; Shift with the wheel, a sideways wheel, a drag of the empty line or the middle button move it; the arrows move it too, + and - zoom, 0 shows it all; a press on the axis seeks (Seekable: the playhead follows the pointer). Marks and ranges are buttons: a press or Enter selects them, the arrows go from one to the next, a tip shows them whole. Overview shows a strip of the whole line beside it, its marks and ranges small, a frame on the part in view: a drag of the frame moves the view, a drag of an edge of it zooms, a press elsewhere on the strip centers the view there. Editable: a mark or a range is dragged in time, a range by its edges too, a new range drawn on an empty lane; Alt with the arrows moves the one with the focus, by Snap (minute, hour, day, week, month, year, or a number: milliseconds or units of the scale; by default the step of the ticks). Escape cancels a drag. The Timeline does not change its data itself: its events ask the owner to. Events: select ({Kind: mark or range, ID, Item}), seek ({At}), view ({From, To}), move ({Kind, ID, Item, At} of a mark, {Kind, ID, Item, From, To} of a range), resize ({ID, Item, From, To}), create ({Lane, From, To}). The moments it tells are of the kind of Start: a date (YYYY-MM-DD when its snap is a day or more) or a number. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Start | '' | | End | '' | | From | '' | | To | '' | | Scale | '' | | Orientation | 'horizontal' | | Marks | [] | | Ranges | [] | | Lanes | [] | | Progress | null | | Playhead | null | | Seekable | false | | Now | false | | Editable | false | | Snap | '' | | MinSpan | 0 | | Unit | '' | | Format | null | | Controls | true | | Overview | false | | Label | '' | Events - view: The part in view changed: {From, To}. - select: A mark or a range was pressed: {Kind (mark or range), ID, Item}. - seek: The line or the playhead was pressed or dragged: {At}. - create: A range was drawn on a lane: {Lane, From, To}. - move: A mark or a range was dragged: {Kind, ID, Item, At} for a mark, {Kind, ID, Item, From, To} for a range. - resize: An edge of a range was dragged: {ID, Item, From, To}. Slots default Example

Title: TitleBar
Text:
The title bar of a window of a program drawn by the Application (Native.Desktop.Frame hidden, none or transparent), the header of the page on the web. Its empty places move the window (elemenx-native-drag; a double click maximizes it there), what it holds stays clickable. Icon (a name of an icon) or Image (the URL of a picture) and Title; the default slot holds its content after the icon (a NativeMenu or a MenuBar, a search...), the actions slot buttons before the buttons of the window. Controls: auto (by default) draws the buttons of the window (minimize, maximize or restore, close) where the system draws none (Frame none or transparent), true in every program, false never. With Frame hidden the buttons of the system stay over the bar, its content clear of them (env(titlebar-area-)), and they take the colors of the bar, which follow the theme. Window: the ID of the window of OpenWindow it is the bar of (the first window without). Title: Toggle
Text:
A switch: a check box drawn as a track with a thumb (role switch). Checked is its state, Label and Description the text beside it; Size: small or medium; Orientation: horizontal (on to the end of the line) or vertical (on at the top, as the switch of a light). Name and Disabled as in a check box. Events: change (Checked). - States 3: a switch of three positions (role slider), Value false, null (the middle: auto, inherit, either) or true, from the start (the bottom when vertical) to the end. Labels names them ([off, middle, on]; by default Off, Auto and On in the language of the page) for screen readers, and ShowLabels writes them along the track. A press on the track takes the position under the pointer, a press on the text or Space the next one; the arrows, Home and End move it. With a Name, a form gets 'false', 'null' or 'true'. Events: change (Value). - Values: the values of its positions, two ([off, on]) or three ([off, middle, on]: three positions without States), any values (texts, numbers, objects); Value is then the one of the position, change gives it and a form gets its text. A Value that is none of them stands at off (at the middle of three). Title: Tour
Text:
A guided tour: the page is shaded except the element of the current step, and a card next to it explains it. Steps: [{Target (a CSS selector or an element), Title, Text, Placement (bottom, top, right, left; the side with room wins)}]. Open shows it at Step. Back, Next and Done move; Skip, Done and Escape close it. A step whose target is missing shows its card in the middle. The page behind does not take presses while the tour is open. Events: change (the new Step), close (the reason: 'skip', 'escape' or 'done'), finish (after the last step). Title: TrackList

Title: Tree
Text:
A tree. Items: [{ID, Label, Icon, Badge, Items, Disabled, Lazy}]; Value is the ID of the selected item; Expanded holds the open IDs. A Lazy item without Items asks for its children with the load event (the item): the owner gives it Items (Loading holds the IDs being loaded, shown with a spinner). Checkable adds check boxes: a parent is checked when all its children are, mixed when some are; checking it checks all of them. Checked holds the checked IDs (parents included). Filter (or a search field with Searchable) keeps the items that match and their parents, open. Keys: arrows (Right opens or goes to the first child, Left closes or goes to the parent), Home, End, Enter selects, Space checks, '' opens the siblings, a letter goes to the next item that starts with it. Movable lets the pointer drag an item onto another: before it (the upper part of its row), after it (the lower part) or into it (the middle), never into itself or one of its own items. The tree does not change Items itself: the move event ({ID, Target, Position: 'before', 'after' or 'inside'}) asks the owner to. Accept names other types of drags (draggable) the rows take the same way, a kind of a palette dropped in a structure: their move carries the Type and the Data of the drag as ID. Events: select (the item), expand (the open IDs), check (the checked IDs), load (the item), move. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Items | [] | | Value | null | | Expanded | [] | | Checkable | false | | Checked | [] | | Loading | [] | | Searchable | false | | Filter | '' | | Label | '' | | Empty | '' | | Movable | false | | Accept | [] | Events - check: The check boxes changed: the IDs of the checked items. - expand: An item opened or closed: the IDs of the open items. - load: A Lazy item was opened: the item, which asks for its Items. - select: An item was selected: the item. - move: An item was dragged onto another (Movable): {ID, Target, Position (before, after or inside), Type}. Title: VideoTimeline
Text:
The timeline of a video editor (its interface: it plays nothing itself). Tracks [{ID, Kind, Name, Muted, Locked, Hidden, Clips}] of a Kind video, audio or text, each with its Clips [{ID, Name, Start, Duration, In, Length, Color, Thumbnail, Peaks, Text}]: Start and Duration in seconds on the timeline, In the second of its source it starts at, Length the length of its source (a trim stops there), Thumbnail a picture repeated along a video clip, Peaks the levels (0 to 1) drawn along an audio clip, Text the words of a text clip. Time is the playhead, FPS the frames of a second (30: the timecode HH:MM:SS:FF and a step of the arrows), Scale the pixels of a second (zoomed between MinScale and MaxScale), Markers [{ID, Time, Label, Color}] the marks over the ruler, Snap draws a moved edge to the edges near it, the playhead and the marks. Follow keeps the playhead in view as Time changes. The pointer: a press on the ruler or on an empty track seeks (a drag scrubs), a press on a clip selects it (Shift adds one) and a drag moves the clips selected (one clip goes to another track of its kind too), its edges trim it. The keys: Space asks to play or pause (the play event), the arrows move the playhead by a frame (Shift: a second), Alt with the arrows moves the clips selected, S splits at the playhead, Delete removes the selection, + and - zoom, Home and End go to the start and the end, Escape leaves the selection; Ctrl (or ⌘) with the wheel zooms at the pointer. The heads of the tracks mute, hide and lock them. A locked track keeps its clips as they are. Methods: Split() (the clips selected, or the ones under the playhead, cut at it), Delete(), Select(ids), Selected(), Zoom(scale), Fit(), Timecode(seconds). Events: change (Tracks), seek ({Time}), select (the IDs), play, zoom ({Scale}). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Tracks | [] | | Time | 0 | | Duration | null | | Scale | 40 | | MinScale | 2 | | MaxScale | 400 | | FPS | 30 | | Markers | [] | | Snap | true | | Follow | true | | ReadOnly | false | | Label | '' | Events - select: The selection changed: the IDs of the clips. - change: The tracks changed: Tracks. - seek: The playhead was moved: {Time}. - zoom: The scale changed: {Scale}. - play: Space: play or pause. Methods - Timecode(seconds) - Selected() - Select(ids) - Zoom(scale, anchor) - Fit() - Split() - Delete() Example

Title: Window
Text: A window over the page or over its container: a header with its Title (and an Overline above it, an Icon), the body (the default slot) and a footer (slot footer); the slot header puts controls into the header. - The header moves it (Draggable), the edges and the corners resize it (Resizable; MinWidth, MinHeight, MaxWidth, MaxHeight). The focus on the header takes the arrows: they move it, Shift with them resizes it. - Minimize folds it to its header (Minimizable; again unfolds it), Maximize fills its bounds (Maximizable; a double press on the header too), Close hides it (Closable; the close event, Open false). - X, Y, Width and Height place it (pixels); without X and Y it goes into a cascade of the new windows. Bounds: 'parent' (the positioned element it is in; the default) or 'viewport' (fixed to the window of the browser). Persist names a window whose place, size and state are remembered. - A press or the focus puts it over the other windows (the Windows Service) and makes it active (class active). - Variant: 'default', or 'game' for the look of the game theme (the --elemenx-game- tokens). Level: 'primary' (the main windows), 'secondary' (the smaller ones) or 'plain' (a dialog, a message): a theme draws each its way. - HeaderShape 'trapezoid' makes the window a folder: the Icon and the titles on a tab as wide as the title, its end sloping down to the body; the slot header and the buttons stand beyond the slope, and the header still moves it. - PopOut adds a button that moves the body into a window of its own over the other windows of the system (Document Picture-in-Picture: Chrome and Edge; the PictureInPicture Service), and back; Popped tells it is there. - Events: move ({X, Y}), resize ({Width, Height}), minimize, maximize, restore, close, front, popout, popin. - Methods: Front(), Minimize(), Maximize(), Restore(), Close(), Center(). Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Title | '' | | Overline | '' | | Icon | '' | | Open | true | | X | null | | Y | null | | Width | 360 | | Height | null | | MinWidth | 200 | | MinHeight | 120 | | MaxWidth | null | | MaxHeight | null | | Bounds | 'parent' | | Draggable | true | | Resizable | true | | Minimizable | true | | Maximizable | true | | Closable | true | | Minimized | false | | Maximized | false | | Persist | '' | | Variant | 'default' | | Level | 'primary' | | PopOut | false | | Popped | false | | HeaderShape | 'default' | Events - front: It came to the front of the other windows. - restore: It came back from minimized or maximized. - close: Its close button was pressed (Open becomes false). - resize: Its size changed: {Width, Height}. - move: It moved: {X, Y}. Slots header, default, footer Methods - Front() - Minimize() - Maximize() - Restore() - Close() - Center() Example

Title: Workspace
Text:
An IDE-like application frame built on elemenx-screen, elemenx-container and elemenx-column. Slots: header, ribbon (a Ribbon under the header), top-stripe (a band under them), left-stripe, left, main, bottom, right, right-stripe, bottom-stripe (a band above the status bar) and status. Variant="ribbon" makes the frame of an Office-like Application: the header becomes a slim title bar that joins the Ribbon. The frame does not decide its content: an area shows only while its slot renders something (put if on a tool window to open and close it), and the left, right and bottom areas are resized by their edge; the resize event reports {Panel, Size}. On a narrow screen the main area keeps 320 pixels (--elemenx-workspace-main-min) and the frame scrolls across to the panels; in a frame of 720 pixels or less the main area takes the whole width and the left and right panels open over it (a press on the main area closes the tool windows the frame placed there). Tool windows the user arranges: a WorkspaceToolWindow with an ID in the slot tools is placed by the frame. Its Area (left, right or bottom) is where it starts; a button on the stripe of that side (its Icon, Title and Badge: a count, 'dot', 'busy'...) opens and closes it, one tool window open in an area at a time (Open opens it at first). While Customize is on, the buttons are dragged from stripe to stripe (the lower part of the left stripe is the bottom area) and in their order: the tool window goes with its button. Layout is the arrangement: {Areas: {id: area}, Order: [id], Open: {left, right, bottom: id or null}, Sizes: {left, right, bottom: pixels}}; every change of it (a move, an opening, a resize) emits layout with the new one, and Persist (a key) keeps it in the storage of the browser for the next visit. ResetLayout() goes back to the areas of the tool windows. Properties | Property | Default | | --- | --- | | Variant | '' | | Layout | null | | Persist | '' | | Customize | false | Events - layout: The arrangement of the tool windows changed (moved, opened, closed, resized): Layout, {Areas, Order, Open, Sizes}. - resize: A panel was resized by its edge: {Panel, Size}. Slots header, ribbon, top-stripe, left-stripe, left, main, bottom, right, right-stripe, bottom-stripe, status, tools Methods - ResetLayout() Example

Title: Achievements
Text: The achievements of an Application (a game, a course, a profile...), shown one after another by an AchievementHost (place one in the layout of the Application, as a ToastHost). Show(options) queues one and returns its ID. Options: Title, Text, Icon or Image (a trophy by default), Rarity (common... legendary: the color of the badge), Points, Overline (the line above the title: "Achievement unlocked" by default), Duration (6000 milliseconds, the time it shows, its coming and going included; 0 keeps it until it is dismissed). Title: Astronomy
Text:
The numbers of a star system, as a game needs them: where a body is on its orbit at a time (the laws of Kepler), what a star and a planet are made of and how warm they are, and whole systems made of a seed. Nothing is drawn here. Units: distances in astronomical units (AU), times in days, the masses of stars in the masses of the Sun, the ones of planets and moons in the masses of the Earth, the radii of stars in the radii of the Sun, of planets in km, angles in degrees. Space is the one of the ecliptic: X and Y in its plane, Z to its north. - Length(value): a length in AU, of a number (in AU) or a text with its unit: '384400 km', '2.5 Mkm', '5.2 AU', '4.2 ly', '1.3 pc'. - Period(distance, mass): the days of an orbit round a mass (in masses of the Sun). - Position(orbit, time, mass): where a body is ([x, y, z] in AU from what it goes round) at a time (days). An orbit is {Distance (the half of its long axis), Eccentricity (0 a circle, below 1), Inclination, Node (the longitude of the ascending node), Periapsis (the argument of the periapsis), Anomaly (the mean anomaly at the time 0), Period (days: of the mass by default)}. - Path(orbit, count): count points of the whole orbit (the ellipse to draw). - Star(star): a star {Mass, Radius, Luminosity, Temperature} completed by what is missing (as a star of the main sequence), with its Class (O, B, A, F, G, K, M), Color, Habitable ({Inner, Outer}: the zone of liquid water, AU) and Frost (the line beyond which ice stays). - Describe(body, context): what a planet or a moon {Kind, Radius, Mass, Albedo, Day, Orbit} is: Radius, Mass, Gravity (m/s²), Escape (km/s), Density (g/cm³), Temperature (K, of the light of the star), Period (days), Day (hours), Habitable; context {Star (of Star), Distance (from it, AU), Mass (of what it goes round, Suns)}. - Color(temperature): the color of a star of a temperature (K), as '#rrggbb'. - Kinds: the kinds of planets and their colors (rocky, desert, terran, ocean, ice, lava, gas, ice-giant, dwarf, moon). - Generate(seed, options): a whole system of a seed, always the same for the same seed: {Name, Seed, Bodies: [{ID, Type (star, planet, belt), Parent, Name, Kind, ...}]}, the planets with their moons, rings and belts. Options: Name, Planets (how many, 3 to 9 by default), Moons (false: none), Belts (false: none). The same functions run in Node: they read no page. Methods - Length(value) - Period(distance, mass) - Position(orbit, time, mass) - Path(orbit, count) - Star(star) - Describe(body, context) - Color(temperature) - Generate(seed, options) Example

Title: Audience
Text: Who came to a page and which variant of it they see: a landing for a campaign, a language, a phone, or one of an A/B test, the same one again on the next visit. The same code runs in Node (pass the visitor to Context). - Context(options): the visitor: {URL, Params (of the query), UTM {Source, Medium, Campaign, Term, Content}, Referrer (the host of another site it came from, '' when typed or from the same site), Language, Device (phone, tablet or desktop), Width, Touch, Visitor (an ID kept for it), Visits (1 on the first), Returning}. Options override what the browser tells: URL, Referrer, Language, Width, UserAgent, Touch. - Match(rule, context): whether a visitor is one of a rule; every condition given must hold. Source, Medium, Campaign, Term, Content (the UTM tags), Language (ru matches ru-RU), Device, Referrer (a part of the host, '' for none, or a RegExp): a value or a list of them, without case. Params: {name: value, list, true (given) or false (not)}. Returning: true or false. Test: function (context) of your own. - Choose(experiment, variants, options): the variant of a visitor: [{ID, When (a rule), Weight (1), Default}]. First the one a link forces (?variant=ID or ?variant=experiment:ID, Param names it), then the first whose When holds, then the one kept for the visitor, then one of those without When by their Weight (kept for the next visit), else the Default one. Returns {Experiment, ID, Variant, Reason: forced, rule, remembered, split or default}, or null. Options: Context, Param, Random (a function of 0..1). - Chosen(experiment) the last choice; Forget(experiment) the kept one (all of them without a name). - View(experiment, data) tells that the variant was seen (once for a page), Convert(experiment, goal, data) that its visitor did what it was for (signup, buy...): OnEvent(callback) / OffEvent(callback) get {Type (view or conversion), Experiment, Variant, Reason, Goal, Visitor, Source, Medium, Campaign, Referrer, Language, Device, Data, Time}, to send to the analytics of the site. Goal(element, goal, data) tells a conversion of each Experiment an element of the page stands in (the action of a Landing block with a Goal does), or of the one it names. Methods - Context(options) - Match(rule, context) - Choose(experiment, variants, options) - Chosen(experiment) - Forget(experiment) - View(experiment, data) - Convert(experiment, goal, data) - Goal(element, goal, data) - OnEvent(callback) - OffEvent(callback) Tests - tells who came, from where, in which language and on what, and matches its rules — tests/regression/library-landing.test.js - chooses a forced variant, then a rule, then the one kept, then a split by weight, else the default — tests/regression/library-landing.test.js - shows the Variant chosen, tells its view once and the conversion of an action with a Goal inside it — tests/regression/library-landing.test.js - keeps the variant of a split for the visitor, and a link forces another one — tests/regression/library-landing.test.js - draws the blocks of a landing: a hero with its actions, features, numbers counted up, quotes and questions — tests/regression/library-landing.test.js

Title: Badges

The badges of badge and of the Badge of a Button. Describe(value) reads a value: a number (a count: 0 shows none, more than Max (99) shows 99+), 'dot' (something new), 'busy' (a task that runs), another text, or {Value, Tone, Max, Label}. It returns {Shown, Kind (count, dot, busy, text), Tone (accent, info, success, warning, danger: danger for a count by default, accent otherwise), Text (what the badge shows), Label (what a screen reader says instead: Label, or the phrase of a dot or a ring)}. Title: Barcodes
Text:
Barcodes: the codes of the shelves, the parcels and the tickets, drawn in SVG; QR codes are the QR Service. - Formats(): the names of the formats: code128 (any ASCII text, its sets switched to the shortest), ean13 and ean8 (12 or 7 digits, the check digit added; or 13 and 8, the check digit checked), upca (11 or 12 digits), code39 (the capitals, the digits and - . space $ / + %; Check adds the digit of modulo 43), itf14 (13 or 14 digits, its bearer bars), datamatrix (any text, in UTF-8; the least square symbol it fits, 10 to 144 modules) and pdf417 (any text; Columns 1 to 30, Level 0 to 8 of error correction, by its length when not given). - Register(name, format): a format of its own, {Encode(text, options), Label}: Encode returns a code (below) or throws an Error of what is wrong in the text. - Encode(format, text, options): the code, one of {Kind: 'linear', Modules: '1011...' (1 a dark module), Guards (the same length, 1 a bar drawn longer: the guards of EAN and UPC), Texts: [{Text, From, To}] (the human text, at those modules: less than 0 or past the end in the quiet zone), Quiet: {Left, Right}, Bearer}, {Kind: 'matrix', Modules: [[true, false...]] (rows of dark), Quiet} or {Kind: 'stacked', Rows: ['1011...'], RowHeight, Quiet}. - SVG(format, text, options): its drawing; options Height (of the bars, in modules: 50), ShowText (true), FontSize (in modules: 10), Dark, Light (transparent for none), Round (0 to 1: the ends of the bars round), Shape (of the modules of a matrix: square, dots, rounded or diamond, as the QR Service draws them) and the options of the format. Methods - Formats() - Register(name, format) - Encode(format, text, options) - SVG(format, text, options) Example

A format of its own: each letter a bar and a gap, as wide as its place in the alphabet.

Title: Biometric
Text: The fingerprint, face or PIN of the device (Touch ID, Windows Hello, Android) through WebAuthn: HTTPS or localhost. Every method takes callback(error, result); error.name is the name of the browser error ('NotAllowedError' when the user cancels, 'NotSupportedError' without WebAuthn). - Available(callback): {Supported (WebAuthn), Platform (an authenticator built into the device)}. - Register(options, callback): a new credential of this device. options: {Challenge (from the server: an ArrayBuffer or base64url), User: {ID, Name, DisplayName}, RelyingParty: {ID, Name}, Timeout}. The result, {ID, Type, ClientData, AttestationObject, Transports} in base64url, goes to the server to keep. - Verify(options, callback): the user proves to be there. options: {Challenge, Credentials (the IDs kept by the server), RelyingParty ID, Timeout}. The result {ID, ClientData, AuthenticatorData, Signature, UserHandle} goes to the server, which checks the signature: only that check makes it secure. - Check(callback): the user verification of this device without a server (the first Check registers the device in localStorage, StorageKey). It is a convenience, not a security measure: a script of the page can skip it. - Forget(): drops the registration of Check. - Guard(options): a guard for Reveal.Guard. Without options it uses Check; with options.Challenge(done) (done(error, challenge, credentials)) and options.Confirm(result, done) (done(error, true)) it asks the server. Methods - Available(callback) - Register(options, callback) - Verify(options, callback) - Check(callback) - Forget() - Guard(options) Example

Title: Calculations
Text: Formulas of numbers, read without eval (a page that forbids it runs them too): Price Count (1 - Discount / 100), round(Total / 12, 2), if(Area > 100, 0.9, 1) Rate. - Evaluate(text, variables, options): the value of a formula, its names read from variables ({Price: 12}); throws a SyntaxError with the place of a mistake (its Index), or an Error for a name it does not know. - Compile(text, options): the formula read once, a function (variables) => value, with Names (the names it reads). - Names(text): the names a formula reads, the functions and constants left out. The language: numbers (1.5, 2e3, .5), names (letters, digits, ), + - / % (the rest of a division) ^ or (a power, from the right), unary - and +, < <= > >= == != (1 or 0), && || ! (the first value that decides, as in JavaScript), a ? b : c, parentheses, and the functions abs, round(x, digits), floor, ceil, trunc, sign, min, max, sum, avg, sqrt, cbrt, pow, exp, ln, log (base 10, or log(x, base)), sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, hypot, clamp(x, low, high), if(condition, then, else), factorial, percent(x, of); the constants pi and e. Options: Angle (radians, or degrees for the functions of angles), Functions ({name: function} of your own). Methods - Compile(text, options) - Evaluate(text, variables, options) - Names(text) Tests - reads formulas without eval: precedence, powers, conditions, functions, names, and tells a mistake by its place — tests/regression/library-calculators.test.js - counts on its keys and on the keyboard, a percent as a shop does, and keeps its history — tests/regression/library-calculators.test.js - computes its results from its fields, given and declared, each after the results it reads, and tells a cycle — tests/regression/library-calculators.test.js

Title: Cities
Text: The cities of the world from GeoNames (every city of a thousand people or more, CC BY 4.0: show Attribution where the cities are seen): their names, countries, regions, coordinates and time zones. The data is large and loads once, when it is first needed: data/cities.txt and data/regions.txt (the pack cities), and the names in the language of the page where there is a pack of it (data/cities-ru.txt, the pack cities.ru). A city is {ID, Name, Country, Region, Latitude, Longitude, TimeZone}: Name and Region in the language of the page (English otherwise), Country a code of ISO 3166 (Label adds its name). - Load(callback): loads the data; callback (error, count). - Search(text, options, callback): the cities whose name, or a word of it, starts with the text, in any letters (no case, no diacritics; Latin letters find a Cyrillic name: moskva finds Москва), sorted by name. options: Country (a code), Limit (20). callback (error, cities). - Find(id, callback): the city of an ID, or null. Nearest(latitude, longitude, options, callback): the closest city (options.Country keeps one country). - Clock(city or time zone, date): the time there, {Date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', Time: 'HH:mm', Offset: '+03:00', TimeZone} (now by default). Label(city): 'Name, Region, Country' in the language of the page; Place(city): 'Region, Country'. Methods - Load(callback) - Search(text, options, callback) - Find(id, callback) - Nearest(latitude, longitude, options, callback) - Clock(city, date) - Label(city) - Place(city) Example

Title: Clipboard
Text: The clipboard. Copy(text, callback, options) writes text (with the old way of a hidden field where the Clipboard API is missing or refused); options.Toast shows a toast through the Toast Service (true: 'Copied', or the message). Read(callback) reads the text (the browser may ask the user). callback(error, text). Methods - Copy(text, callback, options) - Read(callback) Example

Title: Consents
Text: The consents the user gave, of any kind: cookies and analytics, the terms of a service, mail of news, the use of the camera. A consent has a Key and a Version, and the choice for each of its purposes: Get(key) is the decision kept ({Version, Choices: {purpose: true or false}, Time}) or null, Granted(key, purpose) whether that purpose is allowed, Set(key, version, choices) keeps a decision, Clear(key) forgets it (the Consent asks again), Valid(key, version) whether a decision of that version is kept. OnChange(callback) / OffChange(callback) report every decision (callback(key, decision or null)), also from another tab of the site. They are kept in localStorage (in memory where the page may not use it), under StorageKey and the key. Methods - Get(key) - Granted(key, purpose) - Valid(key, version) - Set(key, version, choices) - Clear(key) - OnChange(callback) - OffChange(callback) Example

Title: Countries
Text:
Countries and territories with their dialling code, the mask of the national number (# is a digit) and currency. List(locale) returns [{Code, Name, Dial, Mask, Currency}] with names in the locale (Intl.DisplayNames, English otherwise), sorted by code. Find(code) returns one country; Match(digits, preferred) the country of an international number: the longest dialling code, then the preferred country, then the main country of a shared code. Methods - List(locale) - Find(code, locale) - Match(digits, preferred, locale) Example

The number belongs to: {{Match(Digits)}}

  • {{country.Code}} · {{country.Name}} · +{{country.Dial}} · {{country.Currency}}
Tests - Countries: finds a country, and the country of an international number by the longest code, then the preferred one — tests/regression/library-services.test.js

Title: Currencies
Text:
The active ISO 4217 currencies. List(locale) returns [{Code, Name, Symbol, Digits}] with the name and the symbol of the locale (Intl), sorted by code; Find(code) returns one currency; Format(amount, code) formats an amount. Without Intl support a currency still lists with its code as the name and the symbol. Methods - List(locale) - Find(code, locale) - Format(amount, code, locale) Example
  • {{Format(Amount, code)}} {{Name(code)}}
Tests - Currencies: lists the ISO 4217 currencies with their names and digits, and formats an amount — tests/regression/library-services.test.js

Title: DataFormats
Text:
The formats of data and of files: a text read into values and values written into a text, by the name of a format. - Parse(name, text, options) the values of a text; Stringify(name, value, options) the text of values. A text a format cannot read throws an Error that names the place: its Line and Column (from 1), in its message too. - Register(name, format) adds a format of the Application (or replaces one): {Parse(text, options), Stringify(value, options), Extensions: ['.ext'], Mime, Label}. Find(name) returns one, Names() lists them, For(file) the name of the format of a file name (by its extension) or of a type of MIME, or null. Built in, with their options: - json: Indent (2) for Stringify; jsonc reads comments and trailing commas too. - yaml (yml), YAML 1.2 of the core schema: block and flow collections, plain, quoted and block scalars (| and >, with - and +), comments, anchors and aliases (&a, a), the merge key <<, several documents (---: All gives them all). No tags (!!str) and no complex keys (? ). Stringify writes block style, Indent (2). - csv and tsv: Header (true: objects by the names of the first row; false: rows of cells), Delimiter (, or a tab), Types (true: numbers and booleans read as such). Stringify takes rows or objects (their keys the header). - ini: [sections] (with dots: nested), key = value or key: value, ; and # comments, Types (true). - toml (TOML 1.0): tables, arrays of tables, dotted keys, strings (basic, literal, multi-line), integers (with , 0x, 0o, 0b), floats (inf, nan), booleans, dates and times (as their text), arrays and inline tables. - xml: an element as {Name, Attributes, Children} (a text is a string among the Children, its spaces around it gone when elements are beside it); comments, processing instructions and the doctype are left out, CDATA is text. Stringify: Indent (2), Declaration (true). - query: a=1&b=2&b=3&c[d]=4 as {a: '1', b: ['2', '3'], c: {d: '4'}} (a[] adds to a list); Stringify the other way. - base64: Parse gives the text (UTF-8), Bytes true a Uint8Array; Stringify takes a text, a Uint8Array or an ArrayBuffer; Url true is the variant for addresses (- and , no =). Methods - Register(name, format) - Find(name) - Names() - For(file) - Parse(name, text, options) - Stringify(name, value, options) Example

{{Problem || 'Edit the text: it is read in the first format and written in the second.'}}

Title: Designer
Text: The document of a designer of pages, shared by its components (DesignerPalette, DesignerCanvas, DesignerTree, DesignerInspector): a tree of nodes under a root (the page), each a kind of the palette with its props, its text, its layout (Style) and its children, and the selected node. It changes through its methods only, each change kept in the history (Undo, Redo) and in the storage of the browser (StorageKey), and listeners hear of every change (OnChange). - The kinds are the classes of the layouts of ElemenxUI (a screen, a row, a heading, a table...), their modifiers as fields, and every Component of the Library from what it declares in $Meta: data/meta.json of the Library, made by elemenx meta. Load(callback) reads it once (Ready() tells it is there); Use(meta) gives it instead. - A node is {ID, Kind, Props, Text, Slot, Style, Children}: Slot is the named slot of its parent it goes to, '' for the default one; Style holds its layout (padding, margin, the size with its least and greatest and, in a flex container, its direction, its wrap, align-items, justify-content and gap), set inline: on its element, or on a div around a Component. SetStyle(id, property, value) sets one of Layout. - A Component whose $Meta names its Children (Tab in Tabs) holds them as nodes: a child inserted gets an ID and a name (tab-2, Tab 2), and on the canvas the component shows the child the selection is in (its Current prop). - A prop its Component declares Body (the Value of a Markdown, of a CodeView) is a text of many lines, written as the body of the element (indented as the template, a tag in it as <) and read back from it. - Literal(value) writes a value as the source of an expression ({ID: 'a'}); Parse(expression) reads it back. - Kinds() lists the kinds by group; Kind(id) is one: {ID, Group, Icon, Tag, Component, Container, Flex, Text, Description, Props (the first values), Fields ([{Name, Type, Options, Default, Description}]), Slots}. Label(kind) and GroupLabel(group) name them in the language of the page; Slots(id) are the named slots of the parent of a node. - Insert(kind, parent, index), Move(id, parent, index), Remove(id), Duplicate(id), Set(id, name, value), SetStyle(id, property, value), Clear(); Select(id) and Selected() for the selected node. - The rules of CSS of the page, by context: Rules(); Rule(context) the one of {Who: node, kind or within, Node, Class, Parent, State, Width, Theme}; SetRule(context, property, value) sets a property of it (the rule comes with its first property and goes with its last); RootClass(id) is the class of the element of a node (elemenx-button), what a rule of its kind names. A node with rules of its own takes the class page- (on a div around a Component). - Template() is the document as a template of Elemenx, its rules first in a

Title: Diagrams
Text:
Diagrams written as text, in a subset of the language of Mermaid, drawn in SVG by a layout of their own (no library): the colors of the theme in a page, its own in a file. - Types(): flowchart, sequence, state, er, gantt, class, mindmap. - Parse(text): the model of a diagram, {Type, ...}; a line it cannot read throws an Error naming its line (Line). - SVG(text, options): the drawing, its size its own (options.Id names its parts; FontSize 14). The languages, by the first line: - flowchart TD|TB|BT|LR|RL (or graph): nodes id[text], id(text), id([text]), id[[text]], id[(text)], id((text)), id(((text))), id{text}, id{{text}}, id>text], id[/text/], id[ ext\], id[/text\], id[ ext/]; links -->, ---, -.->, -.-, ==>, ===, --o, --x, <-->, ~~~ (more dashes: a longer link), with a text (-->|text| or -- text -->), chained (A --> B --> C) and of several (A & B --> C); subgraph id [title] ... end; classDef name fill:..; class a,b name; id:::name; style id fill:... - sequenceDiagram: participant A as Alice, actor B; A->>B: text (->> -->> -> --> -x --x -) --)), + and - after the arrow activate and deactivate, activate A, deactivate A; Note left of|right of|over A[,B]: text; loop, alt / else, opt, par / and, critical, break, rect ... end; autonumber. - stateDiagram-v2 (or stateDiagram): [] --> A, A --> B : text, state "Text" as A, A : text, state A { ... } (a state of states), state X <>, <>, <>, direction LR. - erDiagram: A ||--o{ B : label (|o || }o }| and o| || o{ |{; -- identifying, .. not), A { type name PK "comment" }. - gantt: title, dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD, section Name, Task : [crit,] [done|active,] [id,] start (a date or after id), end (a date) or duration (3d, 2w, 12h); milestone. - classDiagram: class A { +name String +run(speed) void }, A : +member, <> A; A <|-- B, --, o--, -->, --, ..>, ..|>, .., with "1" and "" at the ends and a : label. - mindmap: a tree by its indentation, its first line the root; id[text], id(text), id((text)), id))text((, id)text(, id{{text}} or a text alone. Methods - Types() - Parse(text) - SVG(text, options) Example

The model of a diagram, as Parse reads it, and its drawing.
