Title: Dialogs
Text: Confirmations and alerts from the code, shown by a DialogHost (place one in the layout of the Application): a modal Dialog without one of its own in a template. Confirm(options, callback) shows a dialog and calls back (id): the ID of the action pressed, or null when it was dismissed (Escape, the backdrop, the close button). It returns the ID of the dialog. Options: - Title, Message, Icon; - Actions: [{ID, Label, Variant}], Cancel and OK by default; Variant: danger paints OK as a dangerous action; - Dismissible: false asks for one of the actions: Escape and the backdrop only shake the dialog, which has no close button. Alert(options, callback) has one action, OK. A string is the Message of the options. Close(id, action) closes a dialog from the code and calls back with action. OnChange(callback)/OffChange(callback) report the list. Methods - Confirm(options, callback) - Alert(options, callback) - Close(id, action) - OnChange(callback) - OffChange(callback) Example

Title: Diff
Text: The differences between two texts (the algorithm of Myers: the shortest list of changes). CodeEditor shows them in its diff view; any component may use them. - Lines(before, after) returns the lines of both texts in order: [{Type: 'same', 'remove' or 'add', Text, Old, New}] (Old and New: the numbers of the line in each text, from 1, or null where it has none). - Words(before, after) returns where two versions of a line differ: {Before: [{Start, End}], After: [{Start, End}]} (offsets in each text; words, spaces and signs are the units). - Hunks(lines, context) groups the lines into the changes with context lines around them (3 by default) and the unchanged runs between them: [{Type: 'change', Lines}] and [{Type: 'fold', Lines}]. - Stats(lines): {Added, Removed}. Methods - Lines(before, after) - Words(before, after) - Hunks(lines, context) - Stats(lines) Example

Title: ElemenxHelpers
Text: The helpers the Components and the Services of ElemenxUI share, so each is written once: the text of a body without the indentation of its template (BodyText), the first day of a week (FirstDay), and a list of listeners that tells each of them apart (Listeners). An Application may use them too; its own Services keep their names. Tests - ElemenxHelpers: the text of a body without its indentation, the first day of a week, and listeners that throw apart — tests/regression/library-services.test.js

Title: Emoji
Text: The emoji of Unicode, drawn by the fonts of the system: their groups, names and keywords for search, skin tones and the emoji used last. The data loads once, when it is first needed: data/emoji.json (the groups of emoji-test.txt of Unicode, with the English names) and the names and keywords of CLDR in English and in the language of the user, data/emoji-.json (Locales lists the ones there are; Locale, the language of the page by default). Load(callback) calls back (error, groups). A group is {ID, Label, Icon, Emoji: [{Char, Name, Version, Tone, Region}]}; Version is the version of Emoji that brought it, Tone is true for an emoji that takes a skin tone, Region is the region of a flag. Name(emoji) is its name in Locale. Search(text, limit) finds emoji by every word of the text: the names and the keywords of the loaded languages (LoadLanguage(locale, callback) adds the keywords of one more language of Locales; Keywords(locale, map) adds any: {'😀': 'words'}). Tone(value) is the skin tone of the user, 0 (none) to 5, remembered; Toned(char, tone) applies it. Recent(limit) lists the emoji used last, Used(char) records one (remembered as well). Supported(char) tells whether the system draws an emoji as one picture: a font without it draws a box or its parts (flags on Windows, the newest emoji on older systems), and the pickers leave such emoji out. Methods - Load(callback) - LoadLanguage(locale, callback) - Keywords(locale, map) - Name(emoji) - Search(text, limit) - Tone(value) - Toned(char, tone) - Recent(limit) - Used(char) - Supported(char) Example

Title: FieldFormats
Text:
Formats of text fields: an Input with Preset="email" (url, semver, ipv4, ipv6, uuid, iban, postal-code, integer, decimal) gets the right keyboard and autofill, drops the characters the format cannot hold while the user types, and checks and normalizes the value when it is committed. A format is {Type, InputMode, Autocomplete, Direction, Filter, Normalize(text, options), Validate(value, options)}: Direction ltr keeps Latin text (an address, a code) from left to right on a right-to-left page; Filter is a RegExp of the characters it keeps; Validate returns '' or the message of the error. Options: {Country} for postal-code, {Min, Max} for integer and decimal. Check(name, text, options) returns {Valid, Value, Message}: Value normalized (an IBAN without spaces, a decimal with a point). Display(name, value) is the text a field shows for a value (an IBAN in groups of four). Register(name, format) adds a format of the Application, Find(name) returns one, Names() lists them. Methods - Register(name, format) - Find(name) - Names() - Check(name, text, options) - Display(name, value) Example
  • {{check.Name}} "{{check.Text}}" → {{check.Result}}
Tests - has the formats of the text fields — tests/regression/formats.test.js - checks and normalizes an email and a web address — tests/regression/formats.test.js - checks versions, addresses and identifiers — tests/regression/formats.test.js - checks an IBAN by its country length and its check digits, and shows it in groups of four — tests/regression/formats.test.js - checks a postal code by its country, and any country by a loose rule — tests/regression/formats.test.js - checks whole and decimal numbers in their bounds; a comma is a decimal point — tests/regression/formats.test.js - keeps while typing only the characters a format holds; an empty value is valid — tests/regression/formats.test.js - takes the formats of the Application — tests/regression/formats.test.js

Title: Find
Text: Finds text in the DOM: what the find bar of a RichEditor or a Terminal looks through. Ranges(root, query, options) returns the matches of the query in the text of root as DOM Ranges (a match may cross elements), options {Case, Word, RegExp}; an expression that does not compile finds nothing. Show(owner, ranges, index) marks them with the highlights of the browser (::highlight(elemenx-find), and ::highlight(elemenx-find-current) for the one at index), so nothing is added to the text, and brings that one into view; Clear(owner) takes the marks of owner away. A browser without highlights selects the current match instead. Methods - Ranges(root, query, options) - Show(owner, ranges, index) - Clear(owner) Example

Title: Format
Text: The formats the cards share, in the language of the page (Locale): Count(12400) is '12K', Date(value, style) a date ('short', 'medium', 'long', or Intl.DateTimeFormat options), Day(value) {Day, Month} for a date badge, Relative(value) the time from now ('5 minutes ago'), Money(amount, code) an amount of a currency, Bytes(size) the size of a file ('1.5 MB', in units of 1024). A value is a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string; an invalid one gives ''. Methods - Count(value) - Date(value, style) - Day(value) - Relative(value, now) - Bytes(size) - Money(amount, code) Example <Properties> <Property Label="Count(12400)" [value]="Text.Count" /> <Property Label="Date(now, 'long')" [value]="Text.Date" /> <Property Label="Relative(an hour ago)" [value]="Text.Relative" /> <Property Label="Money(1234.5, 'EUR')" [value]="Text.Money" /> <Property Label="Day(now)" [value]="Text.Day" /> </Properties> <script> ({ Text: {}, $OnCreate: function () { var format = this.$Service('Format'); var day = format.Day(new Date()); this.Text = { Count: format.Count(12400), Date: format.Date(new Date(), 'long'), Relative: format.Relative(Date.now() - 3600000), Money: format.Money(1234.5, 'EUR'), Day: day.Day + ' ' + day.Month }; } }) </script> Tests - DateInput takes the digits of its Format, gives an ISO date, and refuses a date out of Min and Max — tests/regression/library-forms.test.js - Format: counts in short, dates, the parts of a date badge, the time from now, and nothing of an invalid date — tests/regression/library-services.test.js

Title: Forms
Text: The models of forms: the values a form collects and their validation, as the forms of Angular have them. A model is a tree of plain objects, so a Component that keeps it in its state renders it as it changes: - Control(value, validators): a value. Validators is a list of functions (control) -> null or {key: params} (the ones of Validators), or {Validators, Async, Disabled}: Async are functions (control, callback) that call back (errors or null) later; while they run the control is pending, and only the answer for its present value counts. - Group({name: node}, validators): a named set of controls, groups and arrays; its validators see the whole group (Validators.Equal: two fields that must match). Array([node], validators): a list of them (Push, Insert, RemoveAt). Every node has ID (a number of its own: the key of a list in a template), Value (setting it sets the value: a Group takes an object, an Array a list), Errors (null, or the errors of its own validators), Valid, Invalid, Pending, Status (valid, invalid, pending, disabled), Touched, Dirty, Disabled; Get(path) ('address.city', 'items.0' or a list of names), SetValue(value), Patch(value) (the names given only), Reset(value) (back to the first value, or to this one: untouched and clean), Touch() (with all inside: the errors show), Disable(), Enable(), Error(key), Message() (the phrase of its first error), Validate(callback) (calls back (null, {Valid, Errors}) once nothing is pending: errors by the path of each invalid node), OnChange(listener) and OffChange(listener) (listener(node) after a change of a value or a state inside). A disabled node is left out of the value of its group and of its validity. - Validators: Required, RequiredTrue, Email, Min(number), Max(number), MinLength(length), MaxLength(length), Pattern(expression or text), Equal(name, other) for a group, and Custom(key, test(value, control)). - Message(errors): the phrase of the first error (ui.forms., ui.forms.invalid for a key without one), or the text an error gives itself ({key: 'text'}). - The names of fields, as the forms of a server read them: Path(name) gives the parts of user[address][city] (or user.address.city), items[2][name] and tags[] (['tags', '']: the end of an array). Get takes them too. Place(group, path, node) puts a node at such a path, making the groups and arrays on the way (an array where the next part is an index or []): Value is then nested, {user: {address: {city}}, items: [{name}], tags: [...]}, an array without the places no field filled (items[5] alone is [value]). Detach(node) takes a node out (an array keeps the places of the others), and the groups and arrays Place made that are empty then. Form and Field use these models: a Form gives Fields their controls by Name and validates them on submit. Methods - Control(value, validators) - Group(controls, validators) - Array(controls, validators) - Place(group, path, item) - Detach(item) - Path(name) - Message(errors) Example

Title: Formulas
Text:
Formulas written as in LaTeX, drawn by the browser as MathML. MathML(text, display) returns the markup of a (display: true for a formula on a line of its own); a text it cannot read returns the text in an . The part of LaTeX it reads: numbers, letters (italic) and words of functions (\sin, \log, \lim...), the operators (+ - = < > ( ) [ ] | ! , and \cdot imes \div \pm \mp \le \ge e \approx \equiv o \infty \partial abla \in otin \subset \cup \cap orall \exists \ldots \cdots...), the Greek letters (\alpha... \Omega), groups { }, ^ and (powers, indices, both), rac and \dfrac, \sqrt and \sqrt[n], \sum, \prod, \int, \oint and \lim with their limits (under and over in a display), \left and ight, \hat, ar, \vec, \dot, ilde, \overline, \underline, ext, \mathrm, \mathbf, \mathbb, spaces (\, \: \; \quad \qquad), and the matrices egin{matrix}, pmatrix, bmatrix, vmatrix and cases (& between the cells, \ between the rows). Methods - MathML(text, display) Example
Tests - Formulas: LaTeX as MathML, a fraction, a root, powers and indices, a display formula, and an error for what it cannot read — tests/regression/library-services.test.js

Title: GameItems
Text:
The rules of moving the items of a game: what lies where after an item is moved onto a place. An item is an object with an ID and a Count; Stack is the most a pile of it holds (more than 1: it stacks). - Stacks(a, b) tells whether b piles onto a: the same ID, a Stack over 1, and room left on a. - Move(item, current) returns {To, From}: what the target place holds after item comes onto it (current is what it held), and what goes back to the place the item came from. Piles join (up to Stack, the rest stays where it came from); other items swap. To and From are new objects (or null): the old ones are not changed. - Take(item, count) returns the item with count less (null when none is left), for an item that is used up. - Place(element) is where the card of an item (GameItemCard) shows beside an element: a style that fixes it to the viewport, on the side with room. Carded(item) tells whether an item has more to show than its name. Methods - Stacks(a, b) - Move(item, current) - Take(item, count) - Place(element) - Carded(item) Example

A potion (5 of 20) dropped on a pile of 18: {{Result}}

Title: GameLoop
Text: The loop of a game: its world updated in steps of the same time whatever the speed of the screen, drawn once a frame. Create({Step, Update, Render, Speed, MaxSteps, Window}) returns a loop: - Update(step, loop) is called for every Step of the time of the game (1000 / 60 ms by default), Render(alpha, loop) once a frame, alpha (0 to 1) the part of a step past the last Update, to draw between two states; - Start(), Stop(), Pause(), Resume(), Advance(elapsed) (time given by hand: a test, a loop of your own; returns the number of steps run), Running, Paused, Time (the time of the game, ms), Ticks (the steps run), Fps; - Speed (1: real time; 2: twice as fast) and MaxSteps (5: the most steps a frame catches up; a tab back from the background does not run its lost minutes). Methods - Create(options) Example

Title: GameMaps
Text:
The maps of GameWorld: its own JSON, or a map of Tiled (.tmj), made into one form. - Normalize(map) returns the map GameWorld draws: {Width, Height, Projection (orthogonal or isometric), TileWidth, TileHeight, Terrain: {key: {Name, Color, Cost, Opaque, Image, SourceX, SourceY, SourceWidth, SourceHeight}}, Layers: [{Name, Cells (Width Height keys of Terrain, null where empty)}], Objects: [{ID, Kind, X, Y, Width, Height, Team, ...}]}. A layer of the JSON gives Rows (lines of text, a character a key of Terrain: '.' grass, '~' water...) or Data (the keys, row by row). - FromTiled(data, base) reads a map of Tiled: its tile layers (each tile a key of Terrain, drawn with the picture of its tileset; the properties cost and opaque of a tile, Color for a picture missing), its object layers (the class or type of an object its Kind: unit, building or anything else, its properties its fields) and its orientation. base: the URL the pictures of the tilesets are relative to. - Load(url, callback): fetches a map (JSON of its own or of Tiled) and calls back (error, map). Positions are in cells: X across, Y down (on an isometric map, along its two edges). Methods - Normalize(map) - FromTiled(data, base) - Load(url, callback) Example

Title: Gamepad
Text:
Gamepads (the Gamepad API, standard mapping): they work the page the way the keyboard does. Every component that follows the keys follows a gamepad too. - The d-pad and the left stick send the arrow keys to the focused element; when no component takes an arrow (none prevents its default), the focus moves to the nearest control on that side (Move). A held direction repeats. - A sends Enter and X Space, and either presses the focused control when no component took the key (a button, a check box, an option...; A follows a link too); B sends Escape, and cancels the dialog on top when no component took it (an open popup closes first); Y sends Delete; the other buttons are events only. - Every press is the button event ({Button, Pad}): a, b, x, y, lb, rb, lt, rt, select, start, ls, rs, up, down, left, right, home; on a pad without the standard mapping, whose buttons mean nothing known, b0, b1... (the stick still moves). connect and disconnect report pads ({Pad}); change reports a new Kind. - A pad reported twice (XInput and HID, Steam) presses once; the stick goes the way it leans most; the pad drives the page only while the page is shown and has the focus, and one Elemenx drives it when several Applications or widgets use pads (the first to start: window.ElemenxGamepad); the events reach all of them. On(name, callback) / Off(callback). Pads() lists [{Index, ID, Kind}]; Kind() is the kind of the pad used last (xbox, playstation, nintendo, generic, or '' when there is none); Label(button, kind) the name of a button on that kind of pad (A, ✕, B...). Navigate (true) turns the keys and the focus off when false (the events stay). Move(direction, scope) moves the focus to the nearest control left, right, up or down (inside the open dialog, or scope); the keyboard may call it too. Browsers report a pad once a button of it is pressed on the page. Methods - Pads() - Kind() - Label(button, kind) - Move(direction, scope) - On(name, callback) - Off(callback) Example

{{Kind ? 'A ' + Kind + ' pad is connected.' : 'Connect a gamepad and press a button.'}} Last button: {{Last}}

The pad works the page as the keys do: the d-pad moves the focus, A presses.

Title: Graphics3D
Text:
The graphics of three dimensions on WebGL2, with no library: the numbers of space (matrices, vectors, a camera, a ray), the shapes made of triangles (geometry) and a renderer that draws them with the shaders given to it. The numbers and the shapes run in Node too (they read no page): - Matrices of 4 by 4 are arrays of 16 numbers, column by column, as WebGL reads them: Identity(), Multiply(a, b), Invert(m), Translation(x, y, z), Rotation(axis, angle) (radians), Scaling(x, y, z), Compose(position, rotation, scale) (rotation a matrix, or null), Perspective(fov, aspect, near, far) (fov in degrees), Orthographic(left, right, bottom, top, near, far), LookAt(eye, target, up), NormalMatrix(m) (the 3 by 3 one of the normals), Apply(m, point) (a point [x, y, z] moved by it). - Vectors are arrays [x, y, z]: Vectors.Add(a, b), Subtract, Scale(a, k), Dot, Cross, Length, Normalize, Lerp(a, b, t), Distance. - Camera(options) returns a camera ({Position, Target, Up, Fov, Near, Far}): View(), Projection(aspect), Matrix(aspect) (both), Orbit(target, yaw, pitch, distance) (it looks at target from round it), Ray(x, y, width, height) ({Origin, Direction} through a point of the screen), Project(point, width, height) ({X, Y, Depth, Visible}: where a point of space is on the screen). - Hit(ray, center, radius): how far along the ray it meets a ball (-1: it does not). - Geometry is {Positions, Normals, UVs, Colors, Indices} (flat arrays: 3, 3, 2 and 3 numbers a vertex): Sphere({Radius, Segments, Rings}), Icosphere({Radius, Detail}), Ring({Inner, Outer, Segments}) (flat, round the axis Y), Box({Width, Height, Depth}), Cylinder({Radius, Top, Height, Segments, Caps}) (a cone when Top is 0), Torus({Radius, Tube, Segments, Sides}), Plane({Width, Depth, Segments}), Lathe({Points: [[radius, y]...], Segments}) (a line turned round the axis Y), Wedge({Width, Height, Depth}) (a roof of two slopes); Transform(geometry, matrix), Merge(parts) (each a geometry or {Geometry, Matrix, Color}), Displace(geometry, amount) (each vertex moved along its normal by amount(position, normal)), Normals(geometry) (made again from the faces), Facets(geometry) (each face flat, of vertices of its own). - Noise(seed) returns a smooth noise of space: Value(x, y, z) (0 to 1), Fbm(x, y, z, octaves) (several of it, each finer and fainter) and Ridge (the folds of mountains). Without a seed it is the very noise of the shaders, Chunks.Noise (noise3, fbm3, ridge3), to the float: a heightmap of the CPU matches a surface the GPU baked. Chunks.Lights is the light of up to 4 points on a surface, with the shadows of up to 4 balls (lighting(position, normal, view, shine, specular); the global lightShade dims its first light). Chunks.Shadow reads a shadow map (sunShadow(position, normal): 0 in the shadow, 1 in the light; uniforms uShadowMap, uShadowMatrix, uShadowBias, uShadowOn). Create(canvas, options) returns a renderer, or null where there is no WebGL2 (options: Alpha, Antialias, Ratio): - Program(vertex, fragment): the shaders compiled (each one once), their uniforms found; an error of GLSL is thrown with its log. The attributes have fixed places: aPosition, aNormal, aUV, aColor, aInstance (and aInstance2 to aInstance5, one of each copy of an instanced mesh). - Mesh(geometry) returns a mesh: Update(geometry), Instance(data, count) (data {aInstance: {Size, Data}, ...}: the copies of the mesh drawn at once), Destroy(); Lines(points, loop) and Points(positions, extra) (extra {aColor: {Size, Data}}) make meshes of lines and of points. - Texture(source, options) (a canvas, a picture, or {Width, Height, Data}; options Repeat, Nearest) returns a texture for a uniform sampler2D; Cube(size) a cube of six faces for a samplerCube, which Bake(cube, program, uniforms) draws once: the program is Shaders.Quad with a fragment shader that takes the direction of each texel from cubeDirection(uFace, vQuad) (Chunks.Cube): a surface of noise computed once, sampled at every frame. - Shadow(size) returns a shadow map, a depth texture for a uniform sampler2DShadow: between its Begin() and End() the draws write only its depth, as seen from the light; Destroy(). - Draw(mesh, program, uniforms, settings): settings Mode (triangles, lines, line-strip, line-loop, points), Blend (alpha, add or none), Depth (test, true), DepthWrite (true), Cull (back, front or none), Instances (the copies). The value of a uniform is a number, an array (of a vector, a matrix or a list of them), true or false, or a texture. - Resize(width, height, ratio), Clear(color) ([r, g, b, a], 0 to 1), Lost (the context was taken by the browser), Destroy(). Methods - Identity() - Multiply(a, b) - Invert(m) - Translation(x, y, z) - Rotation(axis, angle) - Scaling(x, y, z) - Compose(position, rotation, scale) - Perspective(fov, aspect, near, far) - Orthographic(left, right, bottom, top, near, far) - LookAt(eye, target, up) - NormalMatrix(m) - Apply(m, point) - Camera(options) - Hit(ray, center, radius) - Sphere(options) - Icosphere(options) - Ring(options) - Box(options) - Cylinder(options) - Torus(options) - Plane(options) - Lathe(options) - Wedge(options) - Transform(geometry, matrix) - Merge(parts) - Displace(geometry, amount) - Facets(geometry) - Normals(geometry) - Noise(seed) - Create(canvas, options) Example

Title: Hotkeys
Text:
Keyboard shortcuts of the page. Bind(keys, callback, options) returns the ID of the binding; Unbind(id) removes it. keys: modifiers and a key joined by '+' ('Mod+K', 'Ctrl+Shift+P', 'Alt+ArrowUp', 'Escape', 'F2', '?'); Mod is Ctrl, or Command on macOS. A space makes a sequence pressed one after another ('g i', within a second). Letters and digits also match by their place on the keyboard, so 'Mod+K' works with any keyboard layout. Options: Scope (an element: the binding works only while the focus is inside it, and wins over the bindings without a Scope), Inputs (true: also while typing in a field; by default a shortcut without Ctrl, Alt or Command does not fire in a field), Prevent (false keeps the default action of the key), Description and Group (shown by List and by CommandPalette). callback(event, binding). List() returns the bindings [{ID, Keys, Label, Description, Group}]; Format(keys) is the label of keys on this system ('Ctrl+K', '⌘K'). Trigger(id) runs a binding as if its keys were pressed (callback(null, binding)). Pause() and Resume() turn every binding off and on (a nested Pause counts). OnChange(callback) / OffChange(callback): callback() after a binding is added or removed (a part of the page that renders later, lazy, binds its keys then). Methods - Bind(keys, callback, options) - Unbind(id) - OnChange(callback) - OffChange(callback) - List() - Trigger(id) - Pause() - Resume() - Format(keys) Example

Press {{Keys}} or the sequence g h: {{Note}}

Title: Icons
Text: The icon sets of the page. The library sprite (index.svg) is the set without a name: . Another set is named before the icon name: . The library sets 'brands', 'files', 'music', 'weather', 'sport', 'racing', 'science', 'art', 'cinema' and 'games' are known already; Register(name, source) adds a set from a sprite file (a URL, relative to the page) or from the markup of a sprite (''). A set is a sprite of elements; a symbol keeps its own fill and stroke attributes, so a filled or a colored set draws as it is made. A set loads once, when an icon first needs it (or by Load). Its symbols are copied into the hidden

Title: Idle
Text: The inactivity of the user, as a banking application that signs out after some minutes. Start(options) watches: options {Timeout (milliseconds without a key, a press, a wheel or a move), Warning (milliseconds before Timeout when OnWarn is called), OnWarn(remaining), OnIdle(), OnActive()}. Activity in another tab of the same site counts too (localStorage, StorageKey). Reset() counts from now, Stop() ends the watch, Remaining() is the time left, State() is 'active', 'warning', 'idle' or 'stopped'. OnActive is called when the user comes back after a warning or after going idle. Methods - Start(options) - Stop() - Reset() - State() - Remaining() Example

Title: Kinds
Text:
The kinds of the objects of a game, made of three axes: what a kind extends (Extends, one base), what it can do (Traits: {Name: params}, each the data of a system of the scene: Orbit, Surface, Model, Mover...) and what it is made of (Parts: [{ID, Kind, Position, Rotation, Traits...}], each an object of its own, placed in its parent). The same rules merge them as the Components of the framework merge their layers: the later wins a value, Traits merge by their name and then by their fields, Parts by their ID. - Define(name, kind) registers a kind {Extends, Traits, Parts, Values} (Values: the plain fields of its objects: Name, Team, Radius...); Get(name) returns it as it was given, Has(name), Names(). - Resolve(name) returns a kind made whole: {Name, Chain (its bases, the farthest first), Traits, Parts, Values}. - Make(kind, props) makes an object of a kind: {ID, Kind, Values, Traits, Parts: [objects]}; props are fields of its own ({ID, Name, Team...}), Traits of its own over the ones of its kind and Parts of its own over the parts of the kind (by ID; a part {ID, Removed: true} takes one away). A part of an object has the address parent/part. - Field(object, name) finds a field in any case (radius is Radius) among its Values and the params of its Traits, or the name of a trait and its field together (surfacetype is the Type of Surface): {Trait, Name} or null; Fields(kind) lists them. - Diff(object) is what a saved game keeps: the kind and what differs from it ({ID, Kind, Values, Traits, Parts}); Restore(saved) makes the object again. Kinds that are not defined throw: 'Elemenx Kinds: unknown kind '; a kind that extends itself through others: 'Elemenx Kinds: extends itself: a, b, a'. The same functions run in Node: they read no page. Methods - Define(name, kind) - Get(name) - Has(name) - Names() - Resolve(name, chain) - Make(kind, props) - Fields(kind) - Field(object, name) - Diff(object) - Restore(saved) Example 
{{Text}}
Tests - makes a kind whole of its base, its Traits by their fields and its Parts by their ID, and tells its fields in any case — tests/regression/library-scene.test.js - makes an object of a kind with parts of its own, and keeps of it only what differs: restored the same — tests/regression/library-scene.test.js - puts planets on their orbits and makes shapes of three dimensions with the Services of ElemenxUI — tests/regression/headless.test.js

Title: Layouts
Text: The places of tiles, cards and pictures in a box: four ways of laying them out, as numbers (nothing is drawn here). - Pack(items, options): a grid of cells packed without holes (a bento, a start screen). An item is {ID, Width, Height} in cells (1 by default, no wider than the grid), with Row and Column to keep it in its place (when it fits and is free); the others take the first free place, row by row (Dense false: never before the place of the one before). Options: Columns (the width of the grid in cells). Returns {Items: [{ID, Item, Row, Column, Width, Height}] in the order of the items, Rows}. - Masonry(items, options): columns of one width, each item into the shortest one (a wall of cards). An item is {ID, Height} in pixels, or {ID, Ratio} (its width over its height), with Span (columns it takes, 1 by default). Options: Width (of the box), Columns, or ColumnWidth (the least width of a column: as many columns as fit), Gap. Returns {Items: [{ID, Item, Column, X, Y, Width, Height}], Columns, ColumnWidth, Height}. - Justified(items, options): rows of one height filling the width, each picture keeping its shape (a gallery of photographs). An item is {ID, Ratio}. Options: Width, RowHeight (wanted, 200), MaxRowHeight (a row of few items grows no taller: 1.5 times RowHeight), Gap, LastRow ('left': at RowHeight, the default; 'justify': filling the width; 'hide'). Returns {Items: [{ID, Item, Row, X, Y, Width, Height}], Rows: [{Y, Height, Count}], Height}. - Treemap(items, options): rectangles of areas by their Value (squarified: as square as they can be), Children in the rectangle of their parent (Value the sum of theirs without one). An item is {ID, Value, Children}. Options: Width, Height, Gap (between siblings), Padding (inside a parent around its children), Header (room on top of a parent for its name). Returns {Items: [{ID, Item, Depth, Parent, X, Y, Width, Height, Value, Leaf}], Width, Height}, the parents before their children. The same functions run in Node: they read no page. Methods - Pack(items, options) - Masonry(items, options) - Justified(items, options) - Treemap(items, options) Tests - packs a grid of cells without holes, keeping the items in their places — tests/regression/library-layouts.test.js - lays masonry into the shortest column, a picture by its ratio, an item over several columns — tests/regression/library-layouts.test.js - fills justified rows of one height, each picture keeping its shape, the last one at the wanted height — tests/regression/library-layouts.test.js - makes a treemap of areas by value, children inside their parent, the parents first — tests/regression/library-layouts.test.js - draws a Mosaic of items given and declared, follows its width, and selects an item by a press or Enter — tests/regression/library-layouts.test.js - compares signatures and lays out items with the Services of ElemenxUI — tests/regression/headless.test.js - themes switch the tokens and the rules of the Components, keep to their schemes and are remembered — tests/examples/ui-kit.spec.js - layouts: dashboard, settings, master-detail and centered pages — tests/examples/ui-kit.spec.js

Title: Menus
Text: The items of a menu declared in a template with MenuItem (Menu and ContextMenu use it). Read(container) returns the items its MenuItems declare, nested ones as Items: [{ID, Label, Icon, Shortcut, Disabled, Danger, Checked, Separator, Group, Role, Items, Source}], Source the declaration. Watch(container, callback) calls back with the items again whenever a declaration inside comes, goes or changes, and returns the function that stops it. Pick(item) tells the MenuItem of a declared item that it was chosen (its select). Methods - Read(container) - Watch(container, callback) - Pick(item) Example

Title: Models
Text:
The models of a game, made of code: no files, the same shape for the same seed. A model is a tree of pieces that move on their pivots (a body, its arms, a turret, the sails of a mill), each a geometry of Graphics3D, about 1 tall (or 1 wide when it is a building); the Size of a kind makes it as large as it should be. - Names(filter) lists the models: filter {Group: fantasy, scifi, nature, space; Type: unit, animal, vehicle, plant, rock, building, ship}; Has(name), Info(name) ({Name, Group, Type, Size, Speed, Variants, Clips}). - Define(name, recipe) adds one or replaces it: recipe {Group, Type, Size (in a game), Speed (a second), Variants, Sway (how far the wind bends it), Matte (false: it shines), Smooth (no flat faces), Clips, Build(tools, random)}. Build returns its pieces, tools.Piece(id, parts, {Parent, Pivot, Team}), of parts made by tools.Box(width, height, depth, at, color, turn), Cylinder(radius, top, height, at, color, turn, segments), Ball(radius, at, color, scale), Blob(radius, at, color, rough, scale), Lathe(points, at, color, segments) and Wedge(width, height, depth, at, color, turn); at is [x, y, z] in the space of the model, turn degrees round x, y and z, a piece with Team takes the color of its team; tools.Graphics and tools.Rigs (Biped, Quadruped, Tracked: clips to reuse) are at hand. - Make(name, {Variant}) returns a model, made once: {Name, Key, Group, Type, Size, Speed, Sway, Matte, Clips, Pieces: [{ID, Parent, Pivot, Team, Geometry}]}. - Pose(model, clip, time, {From, FromTime, Fade}) returns the matrix of each piece at a second of a clip, in the space of the model; Fade (0 to 1) mixes it from the pose of the clip From. Length(model, clip) is the seconds of a clip. A clip is {Length, Loop, Hold, Stride, Tracks: {piece: [[time 0 to 1, rx, ry, rz, mx, my, mz]...]}, Spins: {piece: [x, y, z] degrees a second}}; Hold keeps the last pose when it ends, Stride is how far a walk goes in one cycle, in sizes of the model. The same functions run in Node: they read no page. Methods - Define(name, recipe) - Has(name) - Names(filter) - Info(name) - Make(name, options) - Length(model, clip) - Pose(model, clip, time, options) Example

Title: NFC
Text:
NFC tags through Web NFC: Chrome on Android, HTTPS. Every method takes callback(error, result); error.name is the name of the browser error ('NotAllowedError' when the user refuses, 'NotSupportedError' without Web NFC). - Supported(). - Scan(callback): reads the tags held to the device until Stop(); callback(error, tag) for each one, tag {Serial, Records: [{Type, Text, URL, Data (a Uint8Array), MediaType, ID, Language}]} (Text for a text, URL for a link). Stop() ends it. - Write(message, options, callback): writes a tag held to the device. message: a text, {URL}, {Text, Language} or {Records: [{Type, Text, URL, Data, MediaType, ID}]}; options: {Overwrite (true)}. - Lock(callback): makes the tag held to the device read only, for good. Methods - Supported() - Scan(callback) - Stop() - Write(message, options, callback) - Lock(callback) Example

Web NFC here: {{Supported ? 'yes' : 'no (Chrome on Android, HTTPS)'}}

Title: Panels
Text: The panels a component declares in its template, as the tabs of a Tabs (Tab) and of a Ribbon (RibbonTab): a child component renders an element of a class (its panel) whose data- attributes describe it, and the owner reads them. Read(root, selector, owner) returns the panels of root (an element of selector inside it, not inside another element of the owner selector inside it: the panels of a nested Tabs are its own). Data(panel) gives the data- attributes of a panel as {Name: text}, the names in PascalCase (data-key-tip is KeyTip). Watch(root, selector, callback) calls back whenever a panel comes, goes or one of its data- attributes changes, once a frame at most, and returns the function that stops it. Methods - Read(root, selector, owner) - Data(panel) - Watch(root, selector, callback) Example

Title: Pathfinding
Text:
The ways across a map: on a grid of cells, or on a graph of your own. - Grid(width, height, cost) returns a grid of cells, each of a cost to enter (1 by default; Infinity: blocked). Grid(rows, legend) makes it of rows of text: '.' costs 1, '#' blocks, a digit is its cost, legend {char: cost} says more. A grid: Width, Height, Get(x, y) (Infinity outside), Set(x, y, cost), Block(x, y), Free(x, y), Passable(x, y), Clone(). - Path(grid, from, to, options): the cheapest way from {X, Y} to {X, Y} (A), [{X, Y}] from the start to the goal, or null. Options: Diagonal (true: eight ways), Corners (false: no diagonal step past a blocked side), Nearest (true: to the reachable cell nearest the goal when the goal cannot be reached: a unit sent into a building), Limit (the most cells looked at). The costs are 1 or more. - Distances(grid, targets, options): the cost from every cell to the nearest of the targets (Dijkstra), a list of Width Height numbers (Infinity: no way). - Flow(grid, targets, options): a flow field to the targets, for many units at once: {Distances, Next(x, y) (the next cell, or null), Direction(x, y) ({X, Y} of the step: -1, 0 or 1)}. - Search({Start, Goal, Key, Neighbors, Heuristic, Limit}): A on a graph of your own (Dijkstra without a Heuristic): Goal(node) is true at the goal (or is the goal, compared by Key), Key(node) its text, Neighbors(node) [{Node, Cost}]; returns {Path: [nodes], Cost} or null. - Smooth(grid, path): the path without the cells it passes in a straight line: its corners only. Methods - Grid(width, height, cost) - Path(grid, from, to, options) - Distances(grid, targets, options) - Flow(grid, targets, options) - Search(options) - Smooth(grid, path) Example

Title: Permissions
Text:
The permissions of the browser. Query(name, callback) tells the state: 'granted', 'denied', 'prompt' or 'unsupported'. Request(name, callback) asks the user the way that permission is asked (a notification permission, a position, a camera or microphone stream that is stopped at once, a read of the clipboard, persistent storage) and tells the state that follows. Watch(name, callback) reports each change of the state and returns the ID for Unwatch(id). Names: notifications, geolocation, camera, microphone, clipboard-read, clipboard-write, persistent-storage. callback(error, state). Title: PictureInPicture
Text:
Picture-in-Picture: a video, or any part of the page, in a small window of its own that stays over the other windows of the system. - Supported(kind): whether the browser has it, for kind 'video' (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox with its own button) or 'document' (any element: Chrome and Edge). - Video(video, callback): the video in its window, or back when it is there already; callback(error, {Active}). - Document(element, {Width, Height, Title}, callback): the element moves into a window of its own, with the styles, the theme and the direction of the page; a frame in its place tells where it is and brings it back. It comes back when the window closes. callback(error, {Window}). - Close(callback): the video or the element back in the page. Active(): {Kind, Element} or null. - OnChange(callback) / OffChange(callback): callback(Active()) when something goes into a window or comes back. The browser lets a window open only after a press or a key of the user. Title: Platform
Text:
The platform the Application runs on, one API wherever it runs: its windows, its icon, the taskbar, the tray, the dialogs, the notifications and the other features of the system. In a program of elemenx build --native (desktop: Electron, mobile: Capacitor) it asks the system through the bridge of the program (window.ElemenxNative); in a browser it does what the web can: a file picker, a download, confirm, a new tab, the full screen. Every call takes callback(error, result); a feature the place lacks calls back an error. Available() is true in a native program, Platform() 'electron', 'capacitor', 'android' (the ElemenxView of an Android program of its own: elemenx build --native android-library) or 'web', Has(feature) tells whether a feature works here (window, dialogs, menu, tray, external, taskbar, hotkeys, autostart, links, power, update, notifications; files in a mobile program). - Window(action, callback, id): minimize, maximize, restore, toggle-maximize, fullscreen, focus, close, show (a window hidden in the tray comes back) and quit (the program quits, even with CloseToTray); the result is the state {Maximized, Minimized, Fullscreen, Focused}. id is a window of OpenWindow (its own buttons); the first one without. Title(text, callback): the title of the page and of the windows (Elemenx.Title; a program follows every change of it, $Title of the Components too). - Frame(id): the frame of the windows of the program (Native.Desktop.Frame), or of the window id of OpenWindow: system, hidden (the title bar of the system hidden under the page, its buttons over it, their place in env(titlebar-area-)), none or transparent (the Application draws its title bar: an element with elemenx-native-drag moves the window; a TitleBar of ElemenxUI); web on the web. holds it in data-elemenx-frame, and the Material in data-elemenx-material. TitleBarOverlay({Color, Symbol, Height}, callback): the colors of the buttons of the system over a page with Frame hidden (a TitleBar gives them its own), true when the system took them. Scheme(scheme, callback): the scheme of the parts of the system (dialogs, menus, the buttons of the window): system, light or dark; the Theme Service gives it its own. - Open({Accept, Multiple, Read, Title}, callback): files chosen by the user, [{Name, Path, Size, Text or Data}]; Read 'text' (by default), 'data' (base64) or 'none'; [] when the user cancels. A mobile program picks them as the web. - Save({Name, Text or Data, Accept, Title}, callback): a file written where the user says, {Path} (null on the web, where it is a download), null when the user cancels. A mobile program writes it in the Documents of the device (Name a path there; @capacitor/filesystem), {Path} its URI. - Message({Title, Text, Buttons, Kind}, callback): a message with buttons, the index of the one pressed. - Menu(items, callback): the menu of the program ([{Label, Items: [{ID, Label, Hotkey, Disabled, Checked, Separator, Items, Role}]}]; null removes it); a click is the menu event {ID}. ContextMenu(items, callback): a menu at the pointer, the ID chosen or null. - Tray({Icon, Tooltip, Items}, callback): an icon in the tray (Icon a path in the Application; null removes it); the tray event {ID, Kind}: an item of its menu (Kind menu), or the icon itself (ID null, Kind click, double or right). With Native.Desktop.CloseToTray, closing the window hides the program in the tray and a click on the icon brings it back. With Window ({Component, Props, Element, Width, Height}, 320 by 420) a click on the icon opens a small window of the Application by it, as the tray windows of programs do (no frame, not on the taskbar, hidden when it loses the focus), and the menu opens with the right button; TrayWindow(show, callback) shows it (true) or hides it (false), after a choice in it say. TrayMenu(items, callback) puts the menu of the icon in place, the icon and its window staying (a NativeMenu with Target tray does). TrayPopup({Component, Props, Element, Width, Height}, callback) is a menu of the tray drawn by the Application: a window of it that the right button of the icon opens at the pointer, in place of the menu of the system (ShowTrayPopup(show) shows it, hides it, or sizes it with {Width, Height}). TrayIcon({Icon or Image, Tooltip}, callback) changes the picture of the icon (and its tooltip) in its place: Icon a path in the Application, the text of an SVG, a data URL or {Light, Dark} (drawn into a PNG), Image a data URL of a PNG (online, offline...). - Icon(icon, callback): the icon of the Application (Elemenx.Icon): the favicon on the web, the icon of the windows of a program (the taskbar, the title bar, the dock on macOS; drawn into a PNG). icon is a URL (or a path in the Application), the text of an SVG, a data URL, or {Light, Dark}, one for each scheme of the system; null brings back the icon of the page (and the one a program was built with). A program follows every change of Elemenx.Icon, $Icon of the Components too. ResetIcon(callback): the icon of the page, no badge, no progress. IconState() is {Icon, Badge, Progress}. - Role(role, callback): what the system does for an item of a menu with that role (undo, copy, reload, zoomIn, togglefullscreen, quit...), for a menu the Application draws. - External(url, callback): opens an http, https or mailto link in the browser of the system. - Notify({ID, Title, Text, Icon, Image, Variant, Actions: [{ID, Label}], Silent, Urgency, Tag, Timeout, Look}, callback): a notification, callback(error, {ID}). Look system (by default) is the one of the system: Electron in a program (Icon a path in the Application; Silent; Urgency low, normal or critical; Actions on macOS), the Notification of the browser on the web (it asks the user first). Look elemenx is a card of ElemenxUI (NotificationHost: Image, Variant info, success, warning or danger, Actions everywhere), drawn as the theme says: in a program by the corner of the screen, in a window of its own over the others that takes no focus, on the web in the corner of the page; it closes after Timeout milliseconds (6000; 0: when the user closes it; held while the pointer is over it). A card of the same ID takes the place of the one before (Progress, 0 to 1, of a task); Component and Props of the Application draw a card of its own (an invitation to a call: CallInvite), the Component getting Notification {ID, Choose(action), Close()}, Bare leaving out the frame of a card; Priority high keeps it next to the corner past the limit; Sound (a URL; Loop) plays until it goes. Notifications({Limit, Corner}): how many cards show (4; the others told as +N) and in which corner (bottom-right, bottom-left, top-right, top-left). CloseNotification(id) takes one away. The notification event {ID, Kind, Action}: click (the notification pressed), action (a button of it, Action its ID), close (closed by the user) or timeout. - Badge(count, callback): a number on the icon: the badge of the system in a program (on Windows a small picture over the icon, drawn here) and in an installed web Application, and a red disc with the number drawn over the favicon (99+ past 99; 'dot' a disc alone; 0 removes it). Progress(value, callback): a progress from 0 to 1 on the button of the window and a ring around the favicon (null removes it), or {Value, State} with State normal, indeterminate (no value: it runs), paused or error. - Attention(on, callback): the button of the window flashes (the dock bounces) until the window comes to the front; on the web the title of the page and the favicon blink while the page is hidden. - Thumbar(buttons, callback): the buttons under the thumbnail of the window on Windows ([{ID, Icon, Tooltip, Disabled}], seven at most; [] removes them); a press is the thumbar event {ID}. - Tasks(callback): the tasks of the jump list of the program (Native.Desktop.Tasks: [{ID, Label, Description}], on Windows) that started it or came since the last call; a task chosen later is the task event {ID}. - Shortcuts(keys, callback): the global hotkeys of the program, heard even when another program has the focus (['CommandOrControl+Shift+K']; [] removes them); the result lists the ones the system gave (another program may hold one); a press is the shortcut event {Keys}. - Autostart(enabled, callback): starts the program when the user signs in (true), or not (false); without enabled it only tells; the result is {Enabled} (Windows and macOS). - Links(callback): the links of the scheme of the program (Native.Desktop.Protocol: myapp://...) that opened it or came since the last call; a link that comes later is the link event {URL}, and starts no second program. - Power(callback): {OnBattery, Idle (seconds without input), State (active, idle, locked, unknown)}; the power event {State}: suspend, resume, lock-screen, unlock-screen, on-ac, on-battery, shutdown. Awake(on, callback) keeps the screen from sleeping (on the web through the Screen Wake Lock), the result {Awake}. - Update(callback): asks the feed of the versions (Native.Desktop.Update: a JSON {Version, URL, Notes}) whether a newer version is out: {Current, Latest, Available, URL, Notes}; External(URL) then opens the download. - OpenWindow({ID, Component, Props, Element, Title, Width, Height, Frame}, callback): one more window of the same Application: its Component (with its Props), or an Element, lives in a window of its own, with the styles, the theme and the direction of the page, the state and the Services of the one Application. A link of the Application pressed there routes the page. An ID open already comes to the front. callback(error, {ID, Window}); a browser opens one only after a press or a key of the user. Windows() lists the IDs open, FocusWindow(id) brings one to the front, CloseWindow(id) closes it; a window closed (by the user too) takes its Component away and is the closed event {ID}. In a program the windows close with the first one; Frame is its own frame (as Frame() names them). - On(name, callback) / Off(name, callback): the events menu, tray, window ({Maximized, Minimized, Fullscreen, Focused}), shortcut, link, task, thumbar, closed and power. Methods - Available() - Platform() - Has(feature) - Window(action, callback, id) - Frame(id) - TitleBarOverlay(colors, callback) - Scheme(scheme, callback) - Title(text, callback) - Open(options, callback) - Save(options, callback) - Message(options, callback) - Menu(items, callback) - ContextMenu(items, callback) - Tray(options, callback) - TrayMenu(items, callback) - TrayPopup(options, callback) - ShowTrayPopup(show, callback) - Role(role, callback) - TrayIcon(options, callback) - Icon(icon, callback) - ResetIcon(callback) - IconState() - TrayWindow(show, callback) - External(url, callback) - Badge(count, callback) - Progress(value, callback) - Attention(on, callback) - Thumbar(buttons, callback) - Tasks(callback) - Shortcuts(keys, callback) - Autostart(enabled, callback) - Links(callback) - Power(callback) - Awake(on, callback) - Update(callback) - OpenWindow(options, callback) - Windows() - FocusWindow(id) - CloseWindow(id) - On(name, callback) - Off(name, callback) - Notify(options, callback) - Notifications(settings) - CloseNotification(id) Example

Title: Print
Text:
Printing of a part of the page: the browser prints a frame of its own with a copy of that part and the stylesheets of the page (and of the shadow root the part is in), so the rest of the page stays out. A PDF comes from the print dialog of the browser (Save as PDF). There is no button for it: components and Applications call it. - Element(target, options, callback) prints target: a DOM node (copied, it stays where it is) or a text of HTML. Options: Title (of the document: the name a PDF gets), Theme ('light' by default; another name of the Theme Service, or false for the theme of the page), Class (classes of the body of the frame), Style (more CSS), Margin (of the page, '16mm' by default) and Language (the lang of the document; the page's by default). callback(error) once the dialog of the browser closes. - Document(target, options) returns the HTML of the document Element prints. Methods - Document(target, options) - Element(target, options, callback) Example

Title: Push
Text: Web Push: the server of the Application sends messages that reach the user even while the page is closed (a Service Worker shows them as notifications). HTTPS or localhost. Every method takes callback(error, result); error.name is the name of the browser error ('NotAllowedError' when the user refuses, 'NotSupportedError' where the browser has no push). - Supported(): whether the browser has Web Push. Permission(): 'granted', 'denied' or 'default'. - Subscribe({Key, Worker}, callback): asks the user, then subscribes; the result {Endpoint, Keys: {P256dh, Auth}, ExpirationTime, JSON} goes to the server, which sends to it (with the private key of the pair of Key: a VAPID public key in base64url). Worker is the URL of the Service Worker that receives the messages, registered when the page has none of its own (docs/LIBRARIES.md has one to copy: it shows {Title, Text, Icon, URL, Tag} as a notification, a press opens URL, and it tells the open pages). - Subscription(callback): the subscription of this browser, or null. Unsubscribe(callback): true when it went. - Notify(title, {Text, Icon, Tag, URL}, callback): a notification from the page itself (no server). - On('message', callback) / Off('message', callback): the messages the worker passes to the open pages ({Type: 'push' or 'click', Data}). Methods - Supported() - Permission() - Subscribe(options, callback) - Subscription(callback) - Unsubscribe(callback) - Notify(title, options, callback) - On(name, callback) - Off(name, callback) Example

Title: QR
Text:
QR codes (ISO/IEC 18004): Encode(text, level) returns the modules of the code of a text, {Size, Version, Level, Modules: rows of true (dark) and false}: the text in UTF-8 (byte mode), the least version (1 to 40) it fits, level L, M (the default), Q or H of error correction (a code still reads with 7, 15, 25 or 30% of it damaged), and the mask with the least penalty. A text too long for version 40 throws. SVG(text, options) is the text of an SVG of it ({Level, Margin (4 modules), Dark, Light}), styled by Modules (square, dots, rounded or diamond), Eyes (the three finder patterns: square, rounded, circle or leaf), EyeColor, Gradient ({From, To, Angle}) and Logo (a URL in the middle, LogoSize: 0.22) or Text (a word there): with a Logo or a Text the level is H (LevelFor(options)), and the modules under them are left out. Raster(svg, width, height, callback) draws an SVG into a PNG, callback(error, data URL), a Logo of another place read in first. ModulePath(x, y, shape) is the path of a module of a shape. Methods - Encode(text, level) - LevelFor(options) - ModulePath(x, y, shape) - SVG(text, options) - Raster(svg, width, height, callback) Example

Text:

Title: Reveal
Text:
Showing what a field hides: a password (Input), a card number (CardNumberInput), a security code (CVVInput) or a one-time code (OTPInput). Their eye buttons call Toggle(field, kind). Hiding needs nothing; showing a Guarded field first asks: the field emits reveal with a request {Kind ('password', 'card', 'cvv' or 'code'), Element (the root of the field), Allow(), Deny()}, and the guard of the page, set with Guard(callback), gets the same request, as in a banking application that asks for a fingerprint before it shows a card number. The eye spins until Allow or Deny; an answer that comes after the field was hidden again or destroyed counts for nothing. HideAfter (milliseconds) on the field hides it again by itself. Guard(null) removes the guard. Methods - Guard(callback) - Toggle(field, kind) Example

Title: RichText
Text: The document of rich text: the HTML RichEditor keeps and the Markdown it reads and writes. - Sanitize(html) keeps only the schema of the document: paragraphs, headings h1-h4, quotes, preformatted code, lists, rules, tables, images and links, with strong, em, u, s, code and line breaks inside. Other tags give their text (b becomes strong, i em, strike and del s, h5 and h6 h4); scripts, styles, frames, forms and their content go. Attributes go too, but href and title of a link (http, https, mailto, tel or a relative URL), src and alt of an image (also a data: URL of a picture), colspan and rowspan of a cell and start of a list. Text outside a block goes into a paragraph. - ToMarkdown(html) and FromMarkdown(text): the document as Markdown (CommonMark with the tables, the strike and the fenced code of GitHub) and back. Underline has no Markdown: it stays . - Text(html) is the plain text of a document, a line for each block. - Plugins: what the schema has no element for, drawn by a Component or a function of its own. Extend(plugin) adds one (see Extend below); in Markdown it is a fence of its language (mermaid), a block of a directive (::: warning title="Careful" ... :::) or an inline (:name[text]{key=value}), in the HTML a node of its data (data-elemenx-plugin, data-elemenx-data) that Sanitize keeps and ToMarkdown writes back as it was. Mount(container, options) draws the plugins of a document (Markdown and RichEditor do), {Destroy()} takes them away. Built in: diagram (mermaid or diagram, the Diagram Component), chart (chart, a JSON of the props of Chart), qrcode (qr), barcode (barcode format=ean13) and callout (::: info, note, tip, success, warning, danger; title=...). Plugins() lists their names. The HTML is read in an inert template: nothing of it runs or loads while it is read. Methods - Extend(plugin) - Plugins() - Mount(container, options) - Sanitize(html) - Text(html) - ToMarkdown(html) - FromMarkdown(text) Example

Title: Serial
Text:
Serial ports (COM ports, UART: Arduino, GPS, scales, printers...) through Web Serial: Chrome and Edge on the desktop, HTTPS or localhost. Every method takes callback(error, result); error.name is the name of the browser error ('NotFoundError' when the user picks no port, 'NotSupportedError' without Web Serial). - Supported(). Request({Filters: [{VendorID, ProductID}]}, callback): the user picks a port (from a press: the browser asks for a gesture); the result is a port. Ports(callback): the ports the user already allowed. - A port: Info {VendorID, ProductID}; Open({BaudRate (9600), DataBits, StopBits, Parity, FlowControl, Text}, callback) opens it and starts reading: the data event carries what comes (a text with Text: true, the default, or a Uint8Array), the line event each line of text; Write(data, callback) sends a text or bytes; Signals({DTR, RTS, Break}, callback); Close(callback); On(name, callback) / Off(name, callback) for data, line, error and close; Opened(). - On('connect' or 'disconnect', callback): a port of the page joins or leaves ({Port}). Methods - Supported() - Request(options, callback) - Ports(callback) - On(name, callback) - Off(name, callback) Example

Title: Signatures
Text: How much a signature looks like another, or like the samples of a person: a help for an interface (a hint that a signature is not the one on file, a second look for a person), not a check of security: a signature drawn in a browser can be copied, and a page can be made to say anything. A check that matters runs on a server, the same code in Node, against samples the client never sees. A signature is its strokes, [[{X, Y, P, T}]] as SignaturePad gives them (P the pressure, T the milliseconds from the start of the signature; both may be missing). It is compared without its place and its size: centered, scaled, every stroke resampled into points evenly apart. - Compare(a, b): {Score (0 to 1), Parts: {Shape (the paths, by dynamic time warping), Strokes (their number and lengths), Proportions (its width over its height, the directions it goes), Dynamics (its rhythm and its pressure: null without T)}}. b may be a reference of Enroll: a against each of its samples, the best of them. - Enroll(samples): a reference of several signatures of one person ({Samples, Mean, Spread, Threshold}): how alike its samples are to each other gives the score a signature of the person should reach (Threshold, 0.5 to 0.85). - Match(signature, reference, threshold): {Score, Parts, Match (Score >= threshold: the one given, the Threshold of a reference, or 0.75), Threshold}. - Normalize(signature): the signature as it is compared ({Points: [{X, Y, S, P, T}] (S the number of its stroke), Strokes, Ratio, Length, Duration}), null without a point. Methods - Normalize(signature) - Compare(a, b) - Enroll(samples) - Match(signature, reference, threshold) Tests - scores a signature against another and against the samples of a person, its parts told — tests/regression/library-signatures.test.js - compares what is drawn with its Reference after each stroke, tells compare and says whether it looks like it — tests/regression/library-signatures.test.js - compares signatures and lays out items with the Services of ElemenxUI — tests/regression/headless.test.js

Title: Spatial
Text:
Where things are on a plane, found fast: a grid of buckets (a spatial hash). The units of a map under a selection frame, the enemies in the range of a tower, the nearest tree. - Create({Cell}) returns an index (Cell: the side of a bucket, 64 by default; about the size of the things): - Set(id, x, y, width, height): puts a thing in it, or moves it (width and height 0: a point); - Remove(id), Has(id), Get(id) ({ID, X, Y, Width, Height}), Count(), Clear(), Each(callback); - Rect(x, y, width, height, filter): the IDs of the things that touch the rectangle; - Radius(x, y, radius, filter): the IDs of the things within radius of the point, the nearest first; - Nearest(x, y, max, filter): {ID, Distance} of the nearest thing (within max, when given), or null. filter(id, thing) keeps a thing when it returns true. - Distance(x, y, thing): from a point to a thing ({X, Y, Width, Height}): 0 inside it. Methods - Distance(x, y, thing) - Create(options) Example

Title: Stickers
Text:
The sticker packs of the Application. Register({ID, Title, Icon, Items: [{ID, URL, Title, Keywords, Emoji}]}) adds a pack (again with the same ID: replaces it); Icon is an icon name or the URL of an image. A sticker is any image a browser draws, animated ones too (GIF, WebP, APNG, SVG). Emoji are the emoji the sticker means (a text or a list): a message of one of them suggests it, ByEmoji(char) lists those stickers (the starred and the recent ones first; skin tones and variation selectors do not count). Search(text) finds stickers by title, keywords and emoji. Recent() lists the stickers sent last and Used(sticker) records one; Favorite(sticker) stars or unstars a sticker and Favorites() lists them; both are remembered. OnChange(callback) reports the changes of the packs. Methods - Register(pack) - ByEmoji(char, limit) - Search(text) - Recent() - Favorites() - Used(sticker) - Favorite(sticker) - OnChange(callback) Example

Title: Suprematist
Text: Pictures in the manner of Suprematism (Malevich, 1915-1920s): flat figures of pure color on a light ground, set along one diagonal, a dominant figure, bars that cross it, small elements in the free space. A picture is made of a seed, always the same for the same seed: covers, placeholders of pictures, avatars, empty states. - Generate({Seed, Width, Height, Palette, Density, Background, Title}): the SVG as text. Width and Height (400) are its size; Palette 'classic' (red, black, blue, yellow, ochre on the ground of the paper), 'theme' (the colors of the theme, var(--elemenx-): for a picture in the page) or a list of CSS colors; Density 0 to 1 (0.5) the number of figures; Background a color of its own; Title the text of its role img. - DataURL(options): the same picture as a data: URL, for an or a CSS background. - Figures(options): the figures it is made of, [{Kind (rect, circle, triangle, line, arc), X, Y, Width, Height, R, Turn, Fill}], to draw them otherwise. Methods - Figures(options) - Generate(options) - DataURL(options) Example

Title: Syntax
Terrain
Text:
The ground of a game, continuous: heights of noise anywhere (no cells), its meshes in chunks, and ways over it. - Flat(options) returns a field of a flat map: options Size (of the map, 1000), Height (of its highest hills, 60), Water (the level of the sea, 0 to 1, 0.35), Scale (the size of its hills, 180), Ridges (0 to 1: how much of it is folded into mountains, 0.4), Seed; it has Size, Top (its Height) and Water. Its methods: Height(x, z) (the height of the ground; below 0 under the sea), Normal(x, z), Slope(x, z) (0 flat, 1 a wall), Walkable(x, z, options) (MaxSlope 0.45; Swim: the sea too; Blocked(x, z): true where a thing stands in the way), Chunk(x, z, size, resolution) (a geometry of a square of it, its positions relative to its middle, with Colors of its heights and slopes and a skirt under its edges so chunks of other sizes leave no gap) and Path(from, to, options) (a way of points {X, Y, Z} round what cannot be walked, made straight where it can be; null when there is none; options Step, the finest it looks, MaxSlope, Swim). - Sphere(options) returns the ground of a planet, the very one its baked surface shows (the noise of Graphics3D, as the shader of a GameScene bakes it): options Radius (units), Height (its relief), Seed (the number of its pattern), Ocean (0 to 1), Type (rocky, desert, terran, ocean, ice, lava, dwarf, moon). Its methods: Land(direction) (the ground of the noise: below 0 the sea), Elevation(direction) (above the radius), Point(direction) (on the ground), Altitude(point) (above the ground under it), Patch(face, u, v, size, resolution) (a geometry of a square of a face of its cube, from u and v of -1 to 1, its positions relative to its Center, the land in UV.x, the sea in UV.y). The same functions run in Node: they read no page. Methods - Flat(options) - Sphere(options) Example

Title: Theme
Text: The theme of the page: a policy of the color scheme and a named theme. The policy is 'system' (follows the operating system), 'light' or 'dark'. The theme is 'default' (index.css) or a named one: the Library brings 'contrast', 'darcula', 'soft', 'fantasy', 'scifi' and 'glassy' (themes/), and Register adds the themes of the Application. A theme is plain CSS whose rules start with its attribute: [data-theme][data-theme='ocean'] { ... } for both schemes, [data-theme][data-theme='ocean'][data-scheme='dark'] { ... } for the dark one; such a rule is more specific than the rule of a Component it overrides, so the order of the stylesheets does not matter. body[data-theme] holds the policy under the default theme (so index.css applies it before any script runs) and the name of a named theme; body[data-scheme] always holds the scheme shown, 'light' or 'dark'. Scope(element, name, callback) themes one part of the page: the element and everything in it take a named theme or a policy ('light', 'dark', 'system') of their own, whatever the page shows; null gives the element back to the page. The policy and the theme are remembered in localStorage (StorageKey, Persist) and changes are reported, including system changes under 'system'. The first policy comes from localStorage, then from the data-theme of the page, then from Default. In a native program the parts of the system (dialogs, menus, the buttons of the window) take the scheme too (Platform.Scheme). Methods - Scope(element, name, callback) Example <Properties> <Property Label="Policy" [value]="State.Policy" /> <Property Label="Scheme shown" [value]="State.Scheme" /> <Property Label="Theme" [value]="State.Theme" /> </Properties> <RadioGroup Variant="segmented" [options]="[{Value: 'system', Label: 'System'}, {Value: 'light', Label: 'Light'}, {Value: 'dark', Label: 'Dark'}]" [value]="State.Policy" (change)="Policy" /> <script> ({ State: {}, $OnCreate: function () { var self = this; var theme = this.$Service('Theme'); this.Read = function () { self.State = {Policy: theme.Policy(), Scheme: theme.Resolved(), Theme: theme.Theme()}; }; theme.OnChange(this.Read); this.Read(); }, $OnDestroy: function () { this.$Service('Theme').OffChange(this.Read); }, Policy: function (value) { this.$Service('Theme').Policy(value); } }) </script> Tests - ThemeSwitch shows the policy of the Theme Service and sets it — tests/regression/library-controls.test.js - a part of the page takes a theme of its own, by its attribute or Theme.Scope, whatever the page shows — tests/examples/ui-kit.spec.js - keeps Local and Session in memory, one store for every facade — tests/regression/headless.test.js - knows the references of a template (#Name): completes, tells and finds them from $Ref, and marks a $Ref of none — tests/regression/language-server.test.js - gives the parts of the system in a program the scheme of the theme: its policy, or the one scheme of a theme — tests/regression/title-bar.test.js - themes switch the tokens and the rules of the Components, keep to their schemes and are remembered — tests/examples/ui-kit.spec.js

Title: Toast
Text:
Notifications shown by a ToastHost (place one in the layout of the Application). Show(options) returns the ID of the toast. Options: - Title, Message, Variant (info, success, warning, danger), Icon (a name, or false for none), Class (extra classes); - AutoHide and Duration (milliseconds): the toast closes by itself unless AutoHide is false or Duration is 0; - Actions: [{Label, Run, Variant}] (Action: one of them); Closable: false hides the close button; - Element (a DOM node, for example the element of a Component) or Render(container, toast) for custom content. Configure({Duration, AutoHide, Limit}) changes the defaults. Dismiss(id), Clear(); Pause(id) and Resume(id) hold the timer while the toast is hovered or focused. OnChange(callback)/OffChange(callback) report the list. Methods - Configure(options) - Show(options) - Dismiss(id) - Clear() - Pause(id) - Resume(id) - OnChange(callback) - OffChange(callback) Example

Title: USB
Text:
USB devices through WebUSB (Chrome and Edge; HTTPS or localhost): devices with a driver of their own, not the ones the system keeps (keyboards, disks). Every method takes callback(error, result); error.name is the name of the browser error ('NotFoundError' when the user picks no device, 'NotSupportedError' without WebUSB). - Supported(). Request({Filters: [{VendorID, ProductID, ClassCode}]}, callback): the user picks a device (from a press); the result is a device. Devices(callback): the devices the user already allowed. - A device: Info {VendorID, ProductID, Name, Manufacturer, Serial}; Open({Configuration (1), Interface (0)}, callback) opens it and claims the interface; TransferIn(endpoint, length, callback) reads (a Uint8Array); TransferOut(endpoint, data, callback) writes a text or bytes (the count written); Control({Type, Recipient, Request, Value, Index}, data or length, callback): a control transfer, in with a length, out with data; Close(callback); Opened(). - On('connect' or 'disconnect', callback): a device of the page joins or leaves ({Device}). Methods - Supported() - Request(options, callback) - Devices(callback) - On(name, callback) Example

Title: Visibility
Text:
What can be seen on a grid: lines, the line of sight, the field of view and the fog of war. opaque is a function (x, y) that is true where a cell hides what is behind it, or a grid of Pathfinding (its blocked cells hide). - Line(x0, y0, x1, y1): the cells of the straight line between two cells, [{X, Y}] (Bresenham). - Sight(opaque, x0, y0, x1, y1): whether one cell sees the other: nothing hides between them. - Field(opaque, x, y, radius): the cells seen from a cell within radius (shadowcasting; the walls that hide are seen): {Cells: [{X, Y}], Count, Has(x, y)}. - Fog(width, height): the fog of war of a map, each cell unknown (0), explored (1) or seen now (2): Get(x, y), Seen(x, y), Explored(x, y), Show(field) (the cells of a Field seen, and explored for good), Hide() (all that is seen goes back to explored: before the fields of a new frame), Reveal(opaque, x, y, radius) (Show of a Field), Reset(), Width, Height, State (the list of the states, row by row). Methods - Line(x0, y0, x1, y1) - Sight(opaque, x0, y0, x1, y1) - Field(opaque, x, y, radius) - Fog(width, height) Example

Title: Windows
Text:
The windows of the page (the Window component): their order and the active one. Front(window) puts a window over the others and makes it active; Active() is the active window, List() the open ones from the back to the front; Place() gives the next place of a new window without a place of its own (they go down and right in a cascade). OnChange(callback) / OffChange(callback) report a new order. The geometry of a window with Persist is remembered in localStorage under StorageKey. Methods - Front(entry) - Active() - List() - Place() - OnChange(callback) - OffChange(callback) Example

Title: *badge
Text: badge="value" puts a badge over the corner of any element: an item of a toolbar, of a list, a picture. The value is read by the Badges Service: a number (a count), 'dot' (something new), 'busy' (a task that runs: a ring that turns), another text, or {Value, Tone, Max, Label}; a false or an empty value shows none. The element keeps its layout (it is positioned, unless it is already). A Button takes its badge by its own Badge. Example

Title: *blur
Text:
blur makes an element a surface of frosted glass: what is behind it blurred (backdrop-filter) and seen through the tint of the surface of the theme. blur alone takes the tokens of the theme (--elemenx-blur-radius, -saturate, -tint); blur="12" blurs 12 pixels; blur="{Radius: 24, Saturate: 1.4, Tint: 0.5}" sets each (Saturate: 1 keeps the colors, Tint: 0 clear glass, 1 the surface itself). Where the browser cannot blur, or the reader asks for less transparency (prefers-reduced-transparency), the element has the surface, solid. The class is elemenx-blur. Example

Title: *copy
Text:
copy="text" copies text when the element is clicked (or copy="{Text, Toast}": Toast true or a message shows a toast). For a moment after the copy the element has the class copied and data-copied="true" (a check icon in a Button, for example). Uses the Clipboard Service. The element dispatches "copied" with {Text, Error}. Example {{Token}}

Title: *draggable
Text:
draggable="{Data: item, Type: 'task', Handle: '.grip'}" (or just draggable="item") lets the element be dragged with the pointer onto droppable elements that accept Type. A ghost copy follows the pointer; Escape cancels. The element dispatches "dragbegin" and "dragfinish" ({Dropped, Target}); the target dispatches "dropmove" (once a frame while the item is over it) and "dropped". Over a target with Sort, Index in their detail is the place the item would take among the draggable items of that target (the dragged item left out), and a line marks it. OffsetX and OffsetY are the point of the element that the pointer holds, so ClientX - OffsetX is the left edge of the ghost. Disabled turns dragging off; Handle limits where the drag may start. Hold (milliseconds) leaves a finger to the page: on a touch screen a move scrolls it, and a press held still that long takes the element (it shows held). A drag outlives a new rendering of its element (a list that moves the item to another place while it is dragged): it ends on the release of the pointer. Example

Title: *droppable
Text:
droppable="{Accept: ['task'], Files: true, Text: true}" makes the element a drop target. Accept lists the Types of draggable items it takes (true takes every item). Files and Text accept files and text dragged from outside the browser (native drag and drop). During a drag the element gets the class drop-target when it accepts the item and drop-over while the item is over it. Sort ('vertical', 'horizontal' or 'grid') makes the element an ordered list of its draggable items: a line marks the place a dragged item would take (Marker: false hides it) and Index in the detail tells it. The element dispatches "dropenter", "dropleave", "dropmove" (items only) and "dropped" with {Kind ('item', 'files' or 'text'), Type, Data, Files, Text, Source, ClientX, ClientY, Index (-1 without Sort)}. Title: *glyph
Text:
glyph="reference" draws a sprite symbol inside an

The symbols are those of the page: the reference waits for Icons.Ready(''), as Icon does, and draws once the sprite of the library is in.

Title: *hotkey
Text: hotkey="'Mod+S'" (or hotkey="{Keys: 'Mod+S', Scope: 'local', Description: 'Save', Group: 'File'}") clicks the element when the keys are pressed, unless it is disabled or hidden, and sets its aria-keyshortcuts. Scope 'local' limits the shortcut to the focus inside the closest section, dialog or form of the element. Uses the Hotkeys Service. Example

Title: *itemCard
Text:
itemcard="item" shows the card of an item of a game on any element: under the pointer or the focus, beside the element (GameItems.Place), as GameInventory and GameSlot show it. The item is {Name, Rarity, Type, Stats: [{Label, Value}], Description, Class}; an item with nothing more than a name (GameItems.Carded) shows none, and neither does null. The card opens in the top layer (a popover), so no scrolling box, transform or filter around the element cuts or moves it; it follows the element when the page scrolls or moves it (a part above that renders later), and it stays in the DOM next to the element, so it takes the theme of the part of the page it is in. A card a finger opened (a tap on a tablet) closes when the page scrolls, as the tooltips of the system do. It has the classes of GameItemCard (elemenx-game-inventory-card...). Example

Point at an item, or focus it with Tab: its card shows beside it.

Title: *layer
Text: layer puts its element in the top layer of the page (a popover of the browser) while it is in the page; layer="Open" only while the expression is truthy. A part fixed to the viewport (a host of toasts, a tour, a window of the page, a point a menu opens at) is placed by the viewport there, wherever it is in the page: a box around it with containment (content-visibility, contain), a transform or a filter would otherwise place it by that box, and an overflow or a stacking context would cut or hide it. The element keeps its own place, size and look (elemenx-layer takes back the defaults of the browser for a popover), stays in the DOM where it is, so it takes the theme and the styles of that part of the page and its events bubble as before. An element put in the page later (a part of a if, a component placed after it is built, one Elemenx.Cache brings back) goes in when it is there. Out of the top layer it is the element it was (no popover: the panel of a group that is part of its bar while it is not open). The last one shown is on top, and a new truthy value brings it on top again (layer="Z": windows in the order of their stack), the focus inside it kept. A browser without popovers leaves it fixed as it was. Tests - layer puts its element in the top layer, placed by the viewport inside a box with containment and a transform — tests/regression/library-directives.test.js - layer="Open" is a popover only while it is true, and a new value brings it on top of the others again, the focus kept — tests/regression/library-directives.test.js - layer on a part of a if is in the top layer at the end of the task that opened it, not a frame later — tests/regression/library-directives.test.js

Title: *mask
Text:
mask="{Mask: Mask, Value: Value}" keeps an strictly inside a mask. Slots: # digit, A Latin letter, digit or letter; every other mask character is a literal. Value holds only the slot characters. After every input (typing, paste, drop, autofill) the text is rebuilt from the accepted characters, so nothing outside the mask survives. The element then dispatches a "mask" DOM event whose detail is {Value, Text, Complete}; a listener may rewrite detail.Value. Guide: a character ('', or true for '') shown in the empty slots while the field is focused or filled, so the whole template stays in place and a deleted character is visible. Backspace: 'delete' (default) deletes the character before a literal under the caret; 'skip' only moves the caret over the literal. Example
