Title: *modal
Text:
modal="Open" opens a element as a modal while the expression is truthy and closes it otherwise. It shows in the top layer, over everything, with its backdrop (a popover of the browser, opened at once whatever the size of the page: showModal makes the whole page inert, which costs a long pause on a large page). It is a modal all the same: aria-modal tells the readers of the screen, the backdrop takes the pointer, Tab and Shift+Tab go round inside it, and the focus goes into it when it opens ([autofocus], or its first control) and back to where it was when it closes. Escape and a press on the backdrop dispatch "dismiss" with {Reason: 'escape'} or {Reason: 'backdrop'}; the owner closes the dialog. The dialog on top of several takes the keys. The backdrop of a popover lets the pointer through, so a layer of the directive (elemenx-modal-shade, in the top layer under the dialog) takes the presses outside the dialog. Example

Title: *mount
Text: mount="source" places custom content in the element: source is a DOM node (moved in), a function (called once with the element) or an object with Element or Render(container, item). Used by ToastHost. Example

Title: *popup
Text: popup="Open" shows the element as a floating panel next to its anchor while the expression is truthy. The anchor is the closest .elemenx-popup-anchor ancestor, or the parent element. data-placement: bottom-start (default), bottom-end, top-start, top-end, right-start; start and end, and the side of right-start, follow the direction of the page (on a right-to-left page start is the right edge). A right-start panel without room on either side (a submenu on a phone) goes under its anchor, a step in. The panel dispatches a "dismiss" DOM event on an outside pointer press and on Escape; the owner closes it. The panel keeps to its anchor while the page scrolls or resizes and while its own size changes. It opens in the top layer (a popover of the browser): no overflow, transform or stacking of the parts of the page around it cuts or hides it; a browser without popovers places it as a fixed panel over the page. It works in the document of its element: in a window of its own (Platform.OpenWindow), its window measures it and hears the presses and the keys. Example

Title: *resizable
Text:
resizable="'right bottom'" adds resize handles to the element: right, left, bottom, top and corner (bottom right). The value may also be {Edges, MinWidth, MaxWidth, MinHeight, MaxHeight}. A handle is dragged with the pointer or moved with the arrow keys (Shift for larger steps). The element dispatches "resize" while it changes and "resizeend" after, both with the detail {Width, Height, Edge}. Example

Drag an edge or the corner; focus a handle and use the arrows (Shift for big steps).

Title: *swipe
Text:
swipe makes an element follow a finger (a pen, or a mouse with Mouse) along an axis and tells the end of the move: swipe, swipe="'y'" or swipe="{Axis: 'x' or 'y', Threshold: 40, Mouse: false}". The page still scrolls along the other axis (touch-action). While the finger moves the element dispatches swipemove with {DX, DY} (the move along its axis, the other one 0); when it lifts, swipe with {Direction (left, right, up or down), DX, DY} if it went past Threshold pixels (or flicked), or swipecancel if not (and when the browser takes the gesture). An owner listens with (swipe)="Handler" (event.detail). A move that began on a field, a slider or anything marked data-no-swipe is left to it. With Mouse a mouse drags the element too: the click that ends a move is no press (a link, a picture that opens), and a picture inside is not dragged away by the browser. Example

Title: *tip
Text:
tip shows a tip of the theme over an element, as the ScreenTips of Microsoft Office: tip="'Save the page'", or tip="{Title, Text, Placement, Delay, Class, Element, Render, Disabled}". Title is written in bold with Text under it; Element (a node) or Render(container) give the tip any content instead. Placement: bottom (the default), top, left or right, the other side when there is no room; Delay the time before it shows under the pointer (500 ms; a focus from the keyboard shows it at once). Pointer away, a press, Escape or a scroll hide it. One tip shows at a time, an element of its own in the body (role tooltip, the aria-describedby of the element): the body of the document the element is in, so a window of its own (Platform.OpenWindow) shows its tips in itself. Example
